# Sesión 5 — Ejercicio práctico: extendé tu agente

> **Esto es la tarea de la semana.** El Paso 0 lo hicimos en clase; el resto lo hacés en casa. Lleva entre 45 y 60 minutos. No se entrega y no se revisa en clase: es tuyo.

## Objetivo

Abrir el archivo donde vive tu propia sesión, y después escribir una extensión de Pi **dirigiendo al agente**, sin escribir TypeScript vos.

## Antes de empezar

- Trabajá sobre **el mismo proyecto** que venís usando desde la Sesión 1.
- Tené a mano tu `AGENTS.md` y tus skills de la Sesión 3.
- `git status` limpio antes de arrancar.
- **No se instala nada.** Todo lo de hoy ya está en tu máquina.

## Las reglas de hoy

1. **No hace falta que sepas TypeScript.** El agente escribe el código; vos lo dirigís, lo probás y decidís si sirve. Es lo mismo que venís haciendo hace cuatro semanas, con un objetivo nuevo: la herramienta.
2. **Pasale las docs antes de pedirle nada.** Pi es chico y reciente: el modelo no lo conoce como conoce React. Si no le das las docs, te va a inventar funciones que no existen.
3. **Que entre en una pantalla.** El ejercicio es el ciclo entre lo que pedís y lo que sale, no el tamaño de lo que sale.

## Paso 0 — Abrí tu sesión (lo hicimos en clase)

Tus sesiones están en `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`, organizadas por directorio de trabajo. Cada una es un archivo **JSONL**: una entrada por línea.

Abrí la de este proyecto y buscá tres cosas:

1. **Los `id` y `parentId`.** Cada entrada apunta a su padre. Eso es el árbol del que hablamos: la conversación no es una lista, es un árbol, y la posición actual es la hoja.
2. **Un punto donde ramificaste.** Si alguna vez usaste `/tree` para volver atrás, hay una entrada con dos hijos. Las dos ramas siguen ahí: volver atrás no borró nada.
3. **Una entrada de compactación**, si tenés. Adentro está el resumen que tu agente viene arrastrando desde entonces. Todo lo que pasó antes de ese punto, el modelo lo conoce solamente por ese texto.

No hay nada que entregar acá. Es para que veas que el contexto es un archivo, no una abstracción.

## Pasos 1 a 3 — Escribí una extensión

### Paso 1 — Elegí qué construir

Elegí **una** de estas. Todas son chicas a propósito:

- **Un `/comando`** que haga algo que hacés seguido a mano.
- **Una tool** que envuelva un CLI que ya usás, para que el agente pueda llamarlo sin pasar por `bash`.
- **Un hook** que avise o bloquee sobre algo que no querés que pase: escribir en `.env`, un `git push`, tocar un directorio.
- **Un widget o una status line** que muestre algo que querés tener siempre a la vista.

Si no se te ocurre ninguna, mirá tus notas de las semanas anteriores: lo que anotaste como fricción suele ser la mejor candidata.

### Paso 2 — Dale contexto y planificá

**Primero las docs.** Pedile que lea la documentación de extensiones de Pi y las extensiones de ejemplo antes de escribir nada:

```
Antes de escribir código: leé la documentación de extensiones de Pi
y mirá los ejemplos que vienen con la instalación.
Después contame qué API vas a usar para <lo que querés hacer>.
```

Si te contesta con nombres de funciones que no aparecen en ninguna de las dos fuentes, **los inventó**. Es el momento más útil del ejercicio: pedile que te muestre dónde lo leyó.

**Después el plan.** Entrá a plan mode (Sesión 2) y pedile el plan de la extensión. Es una pieza chica; el plan tiene que ser corto. Si te sale largo, es que estás pidiendo demasiado.

### Paso 3 — Construí, instalá y probá

Que escriba la extensión en `.pi/extensions/` (solo este proyecto) o en `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` (todos).

Para probarla, `/reload` — no hace falta reiniciar Pi. Iterá ahí: probás, no anda, se lo contás, arregla, `/reload` de nuevo.

**Cuando ande, leela.** No hace falta que entiendas cada línea, pero sí que puedas decir qué hace y en qué momento del loop se engancha. Si no podés, todavía no es tuya.

## Resultado esperado

- Una extensión propia andando, instalada en `.pi/extensions/` o `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`.
- Que puedas explicar en una frase **en qué momento del loop se engancha**: cuando arranca la sesión, antes de una tool, después del resultado, al final del turno.
- Haber visto tu propio archivo de sesión por dentro.

Commiteá la extensión si vive en el proyecto.

## Si terminaste antes

No arranques una segunda. Andá a leer el ejemplo de subagentes que viene con Pi (`examples/extensions/subagent/`) y comparalo con la versión mínima que vimos en la teoría. La pregunta que vale: **¿qué de todo eso es el mecanismo y qué es producto?**

## Preguntas para pensar

1. ¿Te inventó una función que no existía? ¿En qué momento te diste cuenta, y qué lo arregló?
2. ¿En qué parte del loop terminó enganchada tu extensión, y por qué ahí y no en otra?
3. Ahora que viste el archivo de sesión: ¿cambia en algo cómo pensás `/compact` y `/tree`?

## Para la semana

**Escribila, y después mantenela viva.** Usala, y anotá dos cosas:

1. Qué le tuviste que arreglar cuando la usaste de verdad.
2. Si la volviste a usar, o si la escribiste y nunca más.

En la Sesión 6 no hay un bloque para mostrarla: la clase se va entera en cambiar el modelo que está abajo de todo esto. Pero tu extensión es una de las cosas que deberían sobrevivir ese cambio — probala contra el modelo nuevo cuando lo tengas andando. **Si algo no te cierra, preguntá en el canal del curso durante la semana.**

# Session 5: Coding Harness (internals)

Open the box. What is the machinery the intern works inside actually made of?

**Schedule change**: Session 6 ran before Session 5, because of date conflicts with the guest. One class is left, and it combines Session 5 (harness internals) with Session 6's open-weight models block (Diego's deck).

Owner: Agus. Duration: 2 h. The delivered materials (instructor notes, deck, exercise) go in Spanish, like sessions 2, 3, 4 and 6. These vault notes stay in English.

Drafted 2026-08-30 from the [[04_Archive/pi-talk/pi-talk|BeerJS Pi talk]] (2026-06-25) plus Pi's own docs and its example extensions.

## The frame

Teach the concept, use Pi as the specimen. Every block is a design decision that any harness has to make, and Pi is the one we can open. Session 6 closes the course on the idea that what you build survives the change of tool, so this session rehearses it a week early.

## Draft skeleton (~2 h)

| Block | ~min | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Recap | 8 | Show-and-tell on Session 4's homework. Where did the docs help, where did they go stale against the code? Open questions from Session 4. |
| What we're covering today | 3 | Four sessions spent driving the thing. Today we open it. Name the shift: this is the first of two sessions that take the machine apart. |
| What a harness is, and the others | 10 | The layered diagram (Interface → Agent Loop → Tools/Memory/Context → LLM). An LLM on its own predicts tokens and can't do anything; the harness connects it to the world. Then the others: Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek's, opencode. Not a ranking. What's worth naming is open against closed source, what ships built in against what you add, whether you can extend it at all and how deep that reaches, and who controls the system prompt. Somebody decided each of those. |
| The loop, and Pi's parts | 14 | How a turn actually runs, step by step, with the extension points marked on the arrows. Then Pi's four packages, base to surface, and the line that you use only the layers you need. The densest block of the day. |
| The session tree, and steering vs follow-up | 7 | Two behaviours of the loop, quickly. The tree: entries carry `id` and `parentId`, the current position is the active leaf, the whole thing sits in one JSONL file. That's why `/tree` is cheap. You move a pointer, you don't delete anything. Steering: when does new information reach an agent that is already running? Mid-stream, after it settles, or queued for the next turn. Every harness answers this. Pi is a good specimen because it names all three out loud. |
| Break | 5 | |
| Three ways to give a model a tool, and subagents | 13 | The general design decision. An extension reaches harness internals and goes deep, but only works in that harness. A CLI is the simplest thing that works and runs anywhere there's a shell, with no auth story. MCP is for tools other people use, for auth, for remote services. What decides it is who the consumer is. Then subagents as mechanism: a separate context with its own transcript, whose entire result comes back to the parent as one message. |
| Compaction | 7 | The trigger is one line (`contextTokens > contextWindow - reserveTokens`). Then the four-step algorithm and the before/after diagram of the entry array. `session_before_compact` can cancel it or hand back a summary you wrote. |
| **Hands-on** | **35** | Read your own session file, then have the agent extend the agent. Detail below. |
| Run modes | 4 | Interactive, headless one-shot, embedded as a library, served over a protocol. The point underneath is that the agent loop is a library and the terminal is one frontend. That's why CI agents, bots and browser agents exist at all. |
| Security | 9 | Threat models, permission models, the sandbox ladder. The honest close. |
| Closing | 5 | What surprised you? Homework. Name the transition to Session 6. |

If the hands-on has to be 45 instead of 35, two content blocks pay for it. Not five minutes off each. Decide that before the class, not during it.

## Hands-on: have the agent extend the agent (~35 min)

**Step 0 (~5 min): open your own session file.** Sessions live in `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`, one JSONL file each, organised by working directory. Find your own entries, look at the `id` and `parentId` pairs, find a branch point. If anyone in the room has a compaction entry, project it. The summary they have been carrying around is a line in a file.

Everything from the theory blocks stops being a diagram here. Five minutes, no more.

**Steps 1-3 (~30 min): pick a target and direct the agent.** A menu, so a room this heterogeneous can self-select:

- a `/command` that does something small and yours
- a tool that wraps a CLI you already use
- a hook that warns or blocks on something (writing to `.env`, a `git push`)
- a widget or a status line

**You don't need to know TypeScript.** That is the exercise. They have spent four weeks learning to direct an agent, and today the target is the tool itself. Install into `.pi/extensions/` or `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`, then iterate with `/reload`. No restart, the loop stays warm.

Everything the course has taught gets pointed at the harness for the first time. Plan first, from Session 2. The `AGENTS.md` and skills they built in Session 3. And Session 4's research move, which here means pointing the agent at Pi's docs and its examples directory before it writes a line.

### What to watch for while walking the room

- **The agent will hallucinate Pi's API, and that's the best thing that can happen.** Pi is small and recent. It isn't in the model's training the way React is. This will happen on its own, to most of the room, and it makes the case about grounding better than any slide can. Don't prevent it. Let it happen, then fix it the Session 4 way, with the docs in context.
- **Watch the size of what they ask for.** The failure mode is asking for a big extension. Push for something that fits on one screen. The exercise is the loop between direction and result, not the artefact.
- **Whoever finishes doesn't start a second one.** Send them to read Pi's own `subagent/` example and compare it with the 200-line version from the talk.
- **A callback to throw while walking**: did you give it the docs before or after it invented that function?

## Security: the honest close (~9 min)

General first, Pi as the example.

- **Threat models.** What are you actually defending against? Prompt injection from repo content, a malicious extension or skill or MCP server, the agent's own destructive mistakes, credentials walking out the door. Different problems, different answers.
- **Permission models** as a design space: allowlist and denylist, ask every time, fully autonomous, read-only modes.
- **The sandbox ladder**: none → in-process → container → micro-VM → remote machine. The argument worth stating plainly is that a partial sandbox is worse than none, because it reads as a boundary while still sitting on your shell, your filesystem, your package managers and your credentials. Real isolation comes from the operating system.
- **Pi as the example.** No sandbox, on purpose. Project trust guards what gets loaded; it is not a safety boundary.

This block goes after the hands-on because that is what earns it. They just wrote an extension and installed it. Pi's own docs say it in one line: extensions run with your full system permissions and can execute arbitrary code. They have been installing them since Session 2.

## Key decisions

- **Concepts general, Pi as the specimen.** Every block is a decision any harness makes. Session 6 closes the course on the same idea, so this rehearses it a week early.
- **No harness comparison table.** The survey block names the axes, not a winner.
- **TypeScript is not assumed.** Session 3 says outright that we can't. Having the agent write the extension removes the problem, and I think it makes a better exercise than writing TypeScript would have been.
- **Security closes the session, after the hands-on.**
- **The session tree stays short.** Pi-specific, a quick look, not a block of its own.
- **Dropped from the design**: provider-level hooks (`before_provider_request` and friends) and the example catalogue as an argument — both only pay off if you already care about Pi. Two former drops need revisiting after PR #16: plan-mode internals (the `{ block: true }` hook is Session 2's unpaid debt, now this session's) and "MCP as just another extension", stale since Pi 1 ships MCP built in with `exposure`.

## Cross-session wiring

- **From [[sessions/session-1/session-1|Session 1]]**: the debt this session was created to pay. Context hygiene was taught there as four commands to use, explicitly "operations, not mechanism". Here `/compact` and `/tree` get their mechanism.
- **From [[sessions/session-3/session-3|Session 3]]**: the boundary moved again (PR #16). The anatomy block — tool, harness, extension points, plan mode as `tool_call` → `{ block: true }`, permissions and security — left Session 3's deck and is now this session's territory, unclaimed by its current INSTRUCTOR. Diego's notes ask for exactly that coordination: confirm this session covers the plan-mode hook, because nobody else pays that debt now. Session 3 also parks "writing a TypeScript extension" here, unchanged, and proposes `propuesta-mcp/` (MCP transports, code mode from the inside, FastMCP) — a deck waiting on a decision, not in this session's plan or timing.
- **From [[sessions/session-4/session-4|Session 4]]**: Session 3 now introduces subagents (PR #16); whether Session 4 still opens them through the documentation use case is unsettled — PR #6's move was reversed. Here they get their mechanism either way. Name the operation early, open the machinery in Session 5. Session 4's closing already announces this session by name.
- **To [[sessions/session-6/session-6|Session 6]]**: the handoff changed, and it got better. Nobody leaves here with a hand-written client, so Session 6's optional "point your own loop at the gateway" extension has no audience from this session. What replaces it is stronger. Session 6's opening recap asks what extension they wrote and whether it survived the week, and Session 6's whole thesis is that everything they built survives the model swap. The extension included. Diego can't write that block until this one exists.

## Homework for Session 6

Keep the extension alive during the week. Note what you had to fix and whether you reached for it again. Bring it. Next week the model underneath changes and we find out what survives.

## What's left before this is done

### To write

- The three repo files, in Spanish: `INSTRUCTOR.md`, `slides.md`, `exercise/README.md`. The deck is the biggest single lift
- Tier 5 in `COURSE_PROGRAM.md`, still one line reading "TBD, topics to be defined by the owner", and the Session 5 section under Proposed Sessions with it
- **Audience and assumptions**, the section every other session's notes open with. What they arrive with (per the merged `INSTRUCTOR.md`, touched by PR #16): Pi 1 with Plannotator and `pi-subagents`, an MCP server in `.pi/mcp.json`, their repo, their `AGENTS.md` and skills, their docs from Session 4. Nothing new gets installed, which makes this the only session in the course with no setup risk. Worth saying out loud in the notes
- The reading list. Two references are seeded in the program (Zechner on the Pi coding agent, Pi's example extensions); the rest is the owner's
- The Security and Trust cross-cutting entry, still `TBD` for this session in the program. This design answers it

### To decide

- **The fallback if the hands-on collapses.** Every other session has one and this doesn't. If the agent can't produce a working extension in 30 minutes, or the API rate-limits 30 people at once, or the room's network folds, they need a pre-written extension to read and modify instead. **The biggest unmitigated risk in the design**
- **What's on screen during the theory.** Session 3 decided its demo project is the course repo; this needs the same call. Probably Pi's own source and docs, plus a live session for the tree and compaction blocks
- **Which blocks run live rather than as diagrams.** The loop, the tree and compaction all want to be shown. Decide which, and record a backup clip for each
- How much threat-model material fits in 9 minutes. Left alone it is easily 20
- Whether the hands-on should be 45, and which two blocks pay for it
- The expected result, in the exercise's own terms: a working extension in `.pi/extensions/` that they got there by directing the agent

### To test

- **The hands-on on a clean machine, timed.** How long does the agent take to produce a *working* extension with Pi's docs in context? If it runs past about 15 minutes, the menu gets smaller, not the block longer
- One reference extension per menu item, pre-built, so nobody is stuck at minute 30 with nothing

type: talk

duration: "~31 min"

# Pi — the self-building agent

> Talk ~30 min · Mixed audience

Pi is an open-source terminal coding agent with a radically minimalist philosophy: a tiny core of four tools — read, write, edit, and bash — a prompt of less than a thousand tokens, and almost no built-in features. But what it lacks out of the box it makes up for with extensibility: Pi can even read its own code and extend itself.

## Time budget

| Time | Block |
| ---- | ----- |
| 5 min | Hook — harnesses + what is Pi? + comparison |
| 4 min | Architecture, briefly |
| 3 min | Demo 1 — Add a mascot |
| 6 min | Demo 2 — A subagent |
| 5 min | Demo 3 — Pi on a web page |
| 2 min | Try it yourself |
| ~28 min | Content + 3 min Q&A |

## Structure

### 1. Hook — 5 min

Open with the concept of harnesses — the tooling structure that wraps an LLM — then show concrete examples, introduce Pi, and finally the side-by-side comparison that makes the audience *feel* the difference in philosophy.

**Slide: Harness diagram**

ASCII diagram in a terminal window showing the layers of a harness: Interface → Agent Loop → Tools/Memory/Context → LLM. The audience needs to understand that every AI product is an LLM wrapped in tooling before we can compare them.

**Slide: Harness examples**

Three floating windows with screenshots: ChatGPT (web chat), Lovable (vibecoding platform), Claude Code (terminal agent). Each is a different kind of harness — same LLM underneath, different tooling and interface.

**Slide: Coding agents landscape**

Three info-windows: Anthropic/Claude Code, OpenAI/Codex, and an "others" window listing Amp, Droid, Aider, Cline, Goose. Quick show of hands: who's used one?

**Slide: What is Pi?**

30 seconds on what a coding agent is, then Pi's thesis: four tools, sub-thousand-token prompt, any model, no MCP / no permissions / no plan mode. Screenshots of Pi running, multi-provider diagram, no-permissions diagram, tree sessions diagram. Credibility point: OpenClaw runs on Pi.

**Slide: VSCode vs Vim analogy**

Two floating windows side by side. VS Code: everything built-in. Vim: minimal, you build what you need. Claude Code is the VS Code of agents, Pi is the Vim.

**Slide: Feature comparison**

| | Claude Code | Pi |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Core tools** | 25+ (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep, LS, TaskCreate, Agent, Skill, EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode, EnterWorktree, ExitWorktree, AskUserQuestion, SendMessage, NotebookEdit, NotebookRun, Verify, UpdateConfig, schedule, loop…) | 4 (read, write, edit, bash) |
| **System prompt** | ~5,000+ tokens, changes every release | <1,000 tokens, barely changes |
| **Permissions** | Built-in system with modes (acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, plan) + hooks + allowlists | None — containerize if you need boundaries |
| **Plan mode** | Built-in (EnterPlanMode/ExitPlanMode tools) | Build it yourself (it's ~50 lines) |
| **Subagents** | Built-in (Explore, Plan, code-reviewer, general-purpose) | Build it yourself (that's the demo) |
| **MCP** | Built-in client + servers | Not included — extensions cover the same ground |
| **Memory** | Built-in auto-memory (4 types: user, feedback, project, reference) | Build it yourself |
| **Worktrees** | Built-in (EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree tools) | Bash is right there |
| **Session branching** | Linear sessions | Tree-based with fork/branch/merge in a single file |
| **Skills** | Built-in marketplace + system | SKILL.md files, progressive disclosure |
| **Extensibility** | MCP + hooks + skills | Extensions (full event lifecycle, can register tools/commands/shortcuts/themes/providers) |
| **Models** | Anthropic only | Any provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, local…) |

**The punchline**: Claude Code is a great product. But every built-in feature is an opinion forced on you, a thing that changes between releases, a maintenance burden for the team. Pi's bet is different: give the agent a minimal core and let it build what it needs — including reading its own source code and writing its own extensions.

**Optional visual**: Show a diff of Claude Code's system prompt between two recent versions to illustrate churn. The prompt you don't control is a liability.

### 2. Architecture, briefly — 4 min

Goal: give the audience just enough mental model to understand the demos. Don't go deep — point at the shape of things.

**The four packages** (one slide — mention, don't dwell):

```
┌─────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────┐
│  pi-ai              │───▶│  pi-agent-core       │───▶│  pi-coding-agent     │───▶│  pi-tui              │
│  (Unified LLM API:  │    │  (Agent loop, event  │    │  (CLI + TUI +        │    │  (Terminal UI:       │
│   OpenAI, Anthropic,│    │   bus, tool exec)    │    │   sessions, modes)   │    │   editor, themes,    │
│   Google, local…)   │    │                      │    │                      │    │   keybindings)       │
└─────────────────────┘    └──────────────────────┘    └──────────────────────┘    └──────────────────────┘
```

Packages are layered inside-out: the unified LLM API at the base, the generic agent loop on top, the coding-specific layer, and the terminal UI at the surface. Use only the layers you need.



**The agent loop** (how a turn works):

```
User message
     │
     ▼
before_agent_start  ◀── extensions: modify system prompt, inject messages
     │
     ▼
 ┌─▶ tool_call      ◀── extensions: intercept, modify args, block
 │      │
 │      ▼
 │  tool_result     ◀── extensions: modify results
 │      │
 └──────┘            (agent loops until done)
     │
     ▼
message_end         ◀── extensions: modify the final message
```

**Extension points** — what extensions can register (one slide):

- **Tools** — LLM-callable functions (this is how you build subagents)
- **Commands** — slash commands (`/my-command`)
- **Skills** — on-demand capability packages (SKILL.md with progressive disclosure: only descriptions live in the prompt, full instructions load when the agent reads the file)
- **Shortcuts** — keyboard bindings
- **Flags** — CLI flags
- **Themes** — UI themes
- **Providers** — custom LLM providers
- **Message renderers** — custom UI for message types

**Three modes of running Pi** (sets up Demo 3):

- **Interactive** — the terminal TUI you'll see in Demos 1 and 2
- **Print mode** — headless one-shot execution for CI/pipelines
- **SDK** — embed pi in your own application (a web server, a desktop app, anything). This is what Demo 3 uses.

**Session tree** (unique to Pi — worth a mention):

Sessions aren't linear — they're a tree. Every message can branch, fork, or merge. The entire tree lives in a single JSONL file. You can navigate to any point, start a branch, and explore alternatives without losing history.

### 3. Demo 1 — Add a mascot — 3 min

The smallest possible win. Goal: show the loop and that adding a capability is cheap and readable. Keep it light and fun.

Idea: write a tiny extension that registers a `/mascot` command that prints a random ASCII goat. Shows: extensions are just TS files, `registerCommand` is the only API you need.

### 4. Demo 2 — A subagent — 6 min

The main event. Three pre-built commits, each building on the last:

**Commit 1 — One foreground subagent**

- A single `delegate` tool that opens a headless agent session, gives it a task, and returns the result
- Show the main agent delegating a focused task (e.g., "find all functions that do X") and receiving the answer
- Key insight: a subagent is just `pi.on("before_agent_start") + session.prompt()` — no magic

**Commit 2 — Background subagents**

- The delegate tool now returns immediately with a task handle instead of blocking — the subagent runs headlessly in the background
- Show the main agent dispatching a research task and then *immediately continuing* with other work (reading a file, planning) while the subagent runs
- When the subagent finishes, its result is injected back into the main agent's next turn as a message
- Key insight: pi's session model is non-blocking — you open a session, fire `session.prompt()`, and the result can be delivered asynchronously. This is fundamentally different from a synchronous tool call that blocks the main loop

**Commit 3 — Complex subagent pipelines**

- Show a pipeline: subagent A researches → subagent B implements → subagent C reviews
- Compare to Claude Code's "dynamic workflows" — same concept, but you built it in ~100 lines instead of it being a platform feature. Bonus: yours can run tasks in the background while the main agent keeps working, which Claude Code's subagent tool calls can't do (they block until completion)
- This is the moment that sells the philosophy: "you just built what Claude Code ships as a feature, and yours is exactly tailored to your workflow"

Present as git checkpoints: `git checkout commit-1` → show it working → `git checkout commit-2` → show the diff → etc. Don't type live.

### 5. Demo 3 — Pi in the browser — 5 min

The closer: "it's not just a terminal toy, it's not even just a server thing." The entire pi agent loop runs **client-side in the browser** — no backend, no server.

**The layout**:

```
┌─────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
│                     │                          │
│   Chat panel        │   Live preview           │
│   (left)            │   (right)                │
│                     │                          │
│   Type messages     │   HTML rendered from     │
│   to the agent      │   virtual files in an    │
│                     │   iframe / shadow DOM     │
│                     │                          │
│   See tool calls    │                          │
│   (write, edit)     │   The agent writes       │
│                     │   virtual files (HTML,    │
│                     │   CSS, JS) in memory and   │
│                     │   the panel re-renders    │
│                     │   when they change        │
│                     │                          │
└─────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┘
```

**How it works**:

- pi-ai + pi-agent-core are bundled for the browser (both packages have `/base` entry points and pass browser smoke tests)
- A virtual filesystem replaces the built-in tools: `write` and `edit` write to in-memory files instead of disk
- LLM calls go directly to the provider API via `fetch` (works in browser)
- The right panel reads the virtual filesystem and renders the HTML whenever a file changes
- The left panel shows tool calls ("writing index.html…", "editing styles.css…") in real time

**Custom browser tools**:

- `write(path, content)` — write to virtual filesystem in memory
- `edit(path, edits)` — edit virtual files
- `read(path)` — read virtual files
- No bash — replaced by browser-specific tools if needed

**The moment**: Ask the agent "build me a landing page for a coffee shop" and watch it write virtual files on the left while the page assembles itself on the right. The entire agent, tools, and rendering are running client-side. No server, no backend.

Have this pre-built and ready to show. The wow factor: the agent is running in the browser, the tools are in-memory, and the page materializes in real time.

### 6. Try it yourself — 2 min

The reward slide. Install command, "your first session" in one line, links to repo / docs / npm. Say exactly what to try first.

```
npm install -g @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent
pi
```

- Repo: [github.com/earendil-works/pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi)
- Docs: [pi.dev/docs](https://pi.dev/docs)
- npm: `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`

### 7. Q&A — 3 min

Reserved for the end.

## Prep checklist

- [ ] Harness diagram slide (hook)
- [ ] Harness examples screenshots: ChatGPT, Lovable, Claude Code
- [ ] Comparison slide (hook)
- [ ] Architecture diagrams (packages + agent loop + extension points + modes)
- [ ] Demo 1: mascot extension (pre-built, test it works)
- [ ] Demo 2: 3 subagent commits (pre-built, test each checkpoint)
- [ ] Demo 3: web app with chat + live preview (pre-built, ready to show)
- [ ] Claude Code prompt diff visual (optional, for hook)
- [ ] Backup recordings of each demo (20-30 sec clips)
- [ ] Final slide with install command

## Tips for this format

- Live demos are the main risk in 30 minutes. Use git checkpoints for Demo 2, not live typing.
- A mixed audience loses focus during long typing stretches. Narrate the intent ("I'm asking it to build a subagent") instead of reading the code aloud.
- Always close with a call to action: the last slide should be how to install and run Pi in under a minute. The goal is they leave wanting to try it.

## Links

- Repo: [github.com/earendil-works/pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi)
- npm: `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`
- Web: [pi.dev](https://pi.dev)
- Docs: [pi.dev/docs](https://pi.dev/docs/latest)

# Extensiones: lifecycle

## Content
- Ventana única con diagrama de flujo que se construye paso a paso
- Los boxes representan los momentos del flujo, las flechas muestran el paso entre ellos
- Los puntos de extensión se indican con flechas/etiquetas pequeñas apuntando a las conexiones entre boxes

Parte 1 — Session lifecycle (vista general):
- [session_start] → [resources_discover] → [agent loop] (box destacado, sin detalle) → [session_shutdown]

Parte 2 — Zoom in al agent loop, se recorre paso a paso:
- [input] → [before_agent_start] → [turn_start] → [context] → [LLM call] → [tool_execution_start] → [tool_call] → [tool_result] → [tool_execution_end] → [turn_end] → [agent_end]
- Flechas de extensión señalando: entre input y before_agent_start (transform), sobre tool_call (block/modify), sobre tool_result (modify), sobre context (modify messages), sobre before_agent_start (inject/modify prompt)

Parte 3 — Zoom out, vuelta a session lifecycle:
- [session_shutdown] con flechas de extensión hacia: [session_before_switch] [session_before_fork] [session_before_compact] [session_before_tree]

Texto visible en cada box (una línea por momento):
- session_start: Se crea la sesión y arranca todo.
- resources_discover: Se descubren extensiones, skills y servidores MCP.
- agent loop: El turno del agente se ejecuta como un loop, paso a paso.
- input: Llega el mensaje del usuario.
- before_agent_start (EXTENSION POINT): Inyectar o modificar el system prompt antes de arrancar.
- turn_start: Comienza un turno dentro del loop.
- context (EXTENSION POINT): Modificar los mensajes que se mandan al LLM.
- LLM call: Se llama al modelo.
- tool_execution_start: Empieza la ejecución de herramientas.
- tool_call (EXTENSION POINT): Bloquear o modificar los argumentos de la tool (permisos).
- tool_result (EXTENSION POINT): Modificar el resultado que recibe el LLM.
- tool_execution_end: Termina la ejecución de herramientas.
- turn_end: Termina el turno; el loop sigue hasta que el agente esté listo.
- agent_end: El agente terminó su trabajo.
- session_shutdown: Se cierra la sesión — y hay más hooks para interceptar (before_switch, before_fork, before_compact, before_tree).

Línea resumen (abajo del diagrama): todos los eventos son escuchables — `pi.on(evento, (e, ctx) => …)` → bloquear · modificar · inyectar, y mostrar UI propia con `ctx.ui` (notify · confirm · select · custom).

## Animation
1. Aparece [session_start]
2. Flecha hacia [resources_discover]
3. Flecha hacia [agent loop] (box destacado)
4. Flecha hacia [session_shutdown]
5. Zoom in sobre [agent loop]
6. Aparece [input], flecha hacia [before_agent_start]
7. Flecha hacia [turn_start], flecha hacia [context], flecha hacia [LLM call]
8. Flecha hacia [tool_execution_start], flecha hacia [tool_call] — flecha de extensión sobre tool_call
9. Flecha hacia [tool_result] — flecha de extensión sobre tool_result
10. Flecha hacia [tool_execution_end], flecha hacia [turn_end], flecha hacia [agent_end]
11. Zoom out, vuelta a session lifecycle
12. Aparecen [session_before_switch] [session_before_fork] [session_before_compact] [session_before_tree] con flechas desde session_shutdown

## Speaker Notes
- Arranca con session_start y resources_discover
- Zoom in al loop — boxes son los momentos, flechas son los hooks
- tool_call: bloquear o modificar (ej: permisos)
- tool_result: modificar lo que el LLM recibe
- context: modificar mensajes antes del LLM
- before_agent_start: inyectar contexto, modificar system prompt
- Zoom out — más hooks de sesión
- switch, fork, compact, tree — todo interceptable
- Todo sin tocar el código de Pi

# Extensiones: API programática

## Content
- Window 1 ("runtime.ts"): Control en runtime — pi.setModel(), pi.setActiveTools(), pi.setThinkingLevel(). Cambiá modelo, herramientas activas y nivel de razonamiento sin reiniciar
- Window 2 ("register.ts"): Registrar — pi.registerTool(), pi.registerCommand(), pi.registerShortcut(), pi.registerFlag(), pi.registerProvider(), pi.registerMessageRenderer(). Sumá tools, commands, shortcuts, flags, providers y renderers desde una extensión
- Window 3 ("mensajes.ts"): Enviar mensajes — pi.sendMessage() / pi.sendUserMessage(). Inyectar mensajes al agente o como si el usuario los escribiera, con modos de entrega (steer, followUp, nextTurn)
- Window 4 ("session.ts"): Sesiones y contexto — ctx.newSession(), ctx.fork(), ctx.navigateTree(), ctx.compact(). Crear sesiones, forkear desde un punto, navegar el árbol y compactar contexto a mano

## Animation
1-4. Cada window aparece una por vez

## Speaker Notes
- No solo hooks pasivos — control programático completo
- Runtime: cambiar modelo, herramientas y nivel de razonamiento sin reiniciar
- Registrar: un solo archivo TypeScript registra tools, commands, shortcuts, flags, providers y renderers (así se construyen subagentes)
- Inyectar mensajes: steer (durante streaming), followUp (después), nextTurn (encolado)
- Sesiones: crear, forkear, navegar el tree, compactar contexto

.hl { color: var(--a1); }

.card {
  background: var(--card);
  border: var(--border);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  box-shadow: var(--shadow);
  padding: 22px 26px;
}

.slide > .mascot { position: absolute; right: 80px; bottom: 50px; --size: 130px; }

/* ───────────── Fragments ───────────── */

[data-step] {
  opacity: 0;
  transform: translateY(18px);
  transition: opacity .45s, transform .6s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.4);
}

[data-step].on { opacity: 1; transform: none; }

.f-drop { transform: translateY(-120px) rotate(-8deg); }
.f-drop.on { transform: rotate(var(--r, 0deg)); }
.f-flip { transform: perspective(900px) rotateY(-95deg); transform-origin: left center; }
.f-flip.on { transform: perspective(900px) rotateY(0); }
.f-pop { transform: scale(.3); }
.f-pop.on { transform: scale(1); }

/* ───────────── Mascot ───────────── */

.mascot {
  width: var(--size, 120px);
  height: var(--size, 120px);
  display: inline-block;
}

.mascot svg { width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: visible; animation: bob 2.4s ease-in-out infinite; }
.mascot.jump svg { animation: jump .6s cubic-bezier(.3, 1.5, .5, 1) 1, bob 2.4s ease-in-out .6s infinite; }
.mascot.bigjump svg { animation: bigjump .9s cubic-bezier(.3, 1.5, .5, 1) 1, bob 2.4s ease-in-out .9s infinite; }
.mascot.shake svg { animation: shake .12s linear infinite; }

@keyframes bob { 50% { transform: translateY(-5px) scaleY(1.02); } }
@keyframes jump { 0% { transform: none; } 15% { transform: scale(1.15, .85); } 50% { transform: translateY(-90px) scale(.92, 1.1) rotate(-6deg); } 85% { transform: scale(1.12, .88); } 100% { transform: none; } }
@keyframes bigjump { 0% { transform: none; } 15% { transform: scale(1.2, .8); } 45% { transform: translateY(-150px) rotate(-200deg); } 70% { transform: translateY(-40px) rotate(-360deg); } 85% { transform: scale(1.15, .85) rotate(-360deg); } 100% { transform: rotate(-360deg); } }
@keyframes shake { 25% { transform: translateX(-3px) rotate(-2deg); } 75% { transform: translateX(3px) rotate(2deg); } }
@keyframes wave { 50% { transform: rotate(-22deg); } }

.mascot .arm { transform-origin: 84px 60px; animation: wave .5s ease-in-out infinite; }
.mascot .drop { animation: drip 1.1s ease-in infinite; }
.mascot .qmark { animation: qbob 1s ease-in-out infinite alternate; transform-origin: 80px 4px; }
.mascot .steam { animation: steam .35s ease-in-out infinite alternate; }
@keyframes qbob { to { transform: translateY(-4px) rotate(12deg); } }
@keyframes steam { to { opacity: .4; transform: translate(2px, -2px); } }
@keyframes drip { 0% { transform: translateY(-4px); opacity: 0; } 30% { opacity: 1; } 100% { transform: translateY(14px); opacity: 0; } }

.confetti { position: absolute; width: 12px; height: 18px; border-radius: 3px; pointer-events: none; animation: confetti 1.4s cubic-bezier(.2, .6, .4, 1) forwards; }
@keyframes confetti { 0% { transform: translate(0, 0) rotate(0); opacity: 1; } 100% { transform: translate(var(--dx), var(--dy)) rotate(var(--rot)); opacity: 0; } }

/* ───────────── Track ───────────── */

.track {
  position: relative;
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between;
  align-items: flex-start;
  padding-top: 64px;
}

.track .stop {
  position: relative;
  flex: 1;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 10px;
  font-size: 22px;
  text-align: center;
}

.track .stop::before {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  top: 14px;
  right: 50%;
  width: 100%;
  height: 6px;
  background: var(--line);
  opacity: .18;
}

.track .stop:first-child::before { display: none; }
.track .stop.lit::before { background: var(--a2); opacity: 1; }

.track .dot {
  position: relative;
  z-index: 1;
  width: 34px;
  height: 34px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--card);
  border: var(--border);
  transition: background .3s, transform .4s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.8);
}

.track .stop.lit .dot { background: var(--a2); transform: scale(1.2); }

.track .stop.finish .dot {
  width: 44px;
  height: 44px;
  margin-top: -5px;
  border-radius: 8px;
  background: conic-gradient(#111 25%, #fff 0 50%, #111 0 75%, #fff 0) 0 0 / 14px 14px;
}

.track .stop.finish.lit .dot { transform: scale(1.3) rotate(-8deg); }

.track .rider {
  position: absolute;
  top: -18px;
  --size: 78px;
  transform: translateX(-50%);
  z-index: 20;
  transition: left .6s cubic-bezier(.3, 1.3, .5, 1), opacity .3s;
}

.track.draw .stop { opacity: 0; animation: stopIn .5s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.6) forwards; }
@keyframes stopIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(20px) scale(.6); } to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }

.track.mini { padding-top: 0; transform: scale(.72); transform-origin: top left; width: 139%; margin-bottom: -18px; }
.track.mini .rider { top: -70px; --size: 60px; }
.steps-slide .track .rider { --size: 100px; top: -44px; }


/* ───────────── Shared pieces ───────────── */

.split { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 30px; align-items: start; }
.split > *, .layers3 > *, .prims > * { min-width: 0; }
.lead { color: var(--muted); font-size: 26px; margin-bottom: 26px; }
.hint { position: absolute; left: 72px; bottom: 34px; }
.ico { line-height: 1; }

.seg2 { display: inline-flex; gap: 0; border: var(--border); border-radius: 999px; overflow: hidden; box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #05051a; }
.seg2 button { padding: 8px 18px; font: 700 18px var(--font-body); color: var(--ink); background: var(--card); border: 0; cursor: pointer; transition: background .25s, color .25s; }
.seg2 button + button { border-left: 2px solid var(--line); }
.seg2 button.on { background: var(--a3); color: #111; }

.install { display: inline-block; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 20px; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 10px; background: var(--term-bg); color: var(--term-ink); }

.note2 { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; padding: 14px 20px; font-size: 21px; line-height: 1.3; }
.note2 b { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 24px; }
.note2 span { color: var(--muted); }

/* ───────────── Code blocks ───────────── */

.code { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: var(--h, auto); background: var(--term-bg); color: var(--term-ink); border: var(--border); border-radius: 16px; box-shadow: var(--shadow); overflow: hidden; font-variant-ligatures: none; }
.code .cbar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 10px 16px; background: #ffffff14; flex: none; }
.code .cbar i { width: 13px; height: 13px; border-radius: 50%; background: #ff5f57; }
.code .cbar i:nth-child(2) { background: #febc2e; }
.code .cbar i:nth-child(3) { background: #28c840; }
.code .cbar .title { margin-left: 8px; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 15px; color: var(--muted); }
.code .copy { margin-left: auto; padding: 3px 10px; font: 700 13px var(--font-body); color: var(--muted); background: transparent; border: 2px solid #ffffff30; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: color .2s, border-color .2s, background .2s; }
.code .copy:hover { color: var(--ink); border-color: var(--ink); }
.code .copy.done { color: #111; background: var(--good); border-color: var(--good); }
.code .cbody { position: relative; flex: 1; overflow: hidden; padding: 12px 0; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--fs, 18px); line-height: 1.5; scroll-behavior: smooth; }
.code .cl { display: flex; padding: 0 18px 0 0; white-space: pre; border-left: 4px solid transparent; transition: opacity .35s, background .35s, border-color .35s; }
.code .cl .ln { flex: none; width: 2.6em; padding-right: 14px; text-align: right; color: #ffffff38; user-select: none; }
.code.focus .cl { opacity: .28; }
.code.focus .cl.lit { opacity: 1; background: #ffffff0d; border-left-color: var(--a3); }
.code.swap .cbody { animation: swapIn .45s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.3); }
@keyframes swapIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); } }

.t-k { color: var(--a1); }
.t-s { color: var(--a4); }
.t-c { color: #8e8bbd; font-style: italic; }
.t-d { color: var(--a3); }
.t-num { color: var(--a3); }
.t-f { color: #7fa6ff; }
.t-key { color: #7fa6ff; }
.t-h { color: #7fa6ff; font-weight: 700; }
.t-fm { color: var(--a3); }
.t-sep { color: var(--a1); font-weight: 700; }

/* ───────────── Portada ───────────── */

.cover { display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center; height: 100%; }
.cover .kicker { font-size: 32px; color: var(--muted); }
.cover h1 { white-space: nowrap; }
.cover h1 .cursor { display: inline-block; width: .45em; height: .85em; background: var(--a1); vertical-align: -.06em; animation: blink 1s steps(1) infinite; }
@keyframes blink { 50% { opacity: 0; } }
.cover .mascot { position: absolute; right: 110px; bottom: 90px; --size: 220px; }
.cover .mascot.enter { animation: dropIn .9s cubic-bezier(.3, 1.5, .5, 1) both; }
@keyframes dropIn { from { transform: translateY(-600px) rotate(-20deg); } to { transform: none; } }
.cover-chips { display: flex; gap: 14px; margin-top: 34px; }
.cover-chips span { padding: 6px 14px; font-size: 20px; border: var(--border); border-radius: 999px; background: var(--card); opacity: 0; transform: translateY(14px) scale(.7); transition: opacity .35s, transform .45s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.8); }
.cover-chips.on span { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
.cover-chips span:nth-child(2) { transition-delay: .12s; }
.cover-chips span:nth-child(3) { transition-delay: .24s; }
.cover-chips span:nth-child(4) { transition-delay: .36s; }

/* ───────────── Secciones ───────────── */

.section { display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center; height: 100%; }
.section h1 { margin-bottom: 18px; }
.section .secttrack { position: absolute; top: 110px; left: 72px; width: 820px; }
.adopters { margin-top: 30px; }
.achips { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 10px; margin-top: 10px; max-width: 900px; }
.achips b { padding: 6px 14px; font-size: 19px; border: var(--border); border-radius: 999px; background: var(--card); opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-40px) rotate(-10deg); transition: opacity .3s, transform .5s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.5); }
.adopters.on .achips b { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
.achips b.pi { background: var(--a3); color: #111; }

/* ───────────── Cómo les fue ───────────── */

.recap2 { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 40px; margin-top: 70px; }
.recap2 .card { position: relative; min-height: 280px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center; gap: 18px; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 36px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.2; }
.recap2 .card .emo { font-size: 60px; }
.recap2 .card.hot { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 28%, var(--card)); }
.recap2 .menti { position: absolute; right: 22px; bottom: 18px; padding: 4px 12px; font: 700 18px var(--font-body); color: #111; background: var(--a3); border-radius: 999px; }

/* ───────────── Dos veces ───────────── */

.days { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 24px; margin-top: 50px; transition: opacity .6s, transform .7s, filter .6s; }
.term { font-variant-ligatures: none; background: var(--term-bg); color: var(--term-ink); border-radius: 16px; border: var(--border); box-shadow: var(--shadow); padding: 0 0 22px; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 26px; overflow: hidden; }
.term .bar3 { display: flex; gap: 10px; padding: 14px 18px; background: #ffffff14; margin-bottom: 16px; }
.term .bar3 i { width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 50%; background: #ff5f57; }
.term .bar3 i:nth-child(2) { background: #febc2e; }
.term .bar3 i:nth-child(3) { background: #28c840; }
.term .bar3 .title { margin-left: 12px; font-size: 17px; color: var(--muted); }
.term .line { padding: 6px 28px; min-height: 46px; display: flex; gap: 14px; align-items: baseline; }
.term .line .p { color: var(--a3); }
.term .caret { display: inline-block; width: 13px; height: 28px; background: var(--term-ink); animation: blink 1s steps(1) infinite; vertical-align: middle; }
.day .line { font-size: 19px; min-height: 0; padding: 6px 22px; }
.day.f-drop { transition-delay: calc(var(--i) * .2s); }
.twice-slide[data-step="2"] .days { opacity: .25; filter: grayscale(1); transform: scale(.9) translateY(-30px); }
.once { position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 300px; width: 560px; padding: 22px 28px; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 22px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--good) 22%, var(--card)); opacity: 0; transform: translate(-50%, 80px) scale(.5) rotate(-6deg); transition: opacity .4s, transform .7s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.5); }
.twice-slide[data-step="2"] .once { opacity: 1; transform: translate(-50%, 0) rotate(-1deg); }
.once .path { font-size: 15px; color: var(--muted); margin-bottom: 8px; }
.once .ln { margin: 6px 0; }
.once b { color: var(--a3); }
.twice-slide > .mascot { --size: 120px; }

/* ───────────── Dónde vive ───────────── */

.sort { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 430px 1fr; gap: 30px; margin-top: 10px; }
.pool { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; }
.schip { padding: 10px 16px; font-size: 19px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.25; border: var(--border); border-radius: 14px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 30%, var(--card)); box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #05051a; cursor: pointer; transition: transform .55s cubic-bezier(.3, 1.2, .5, 1), background .3s; }
.schip:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 45%, var(--card)); }
.bins { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 16px; }
.bin { min-height: 260px; padding: 12px 14px; border: 3px dashed color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 40%, transparent); border-radius: 18px; }
.bin .bh { display: flex; flex-direction: column; margin-bottom: 10px; }
.bin .bh b { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 24px; }
.bin .bh span { font-size: 16px; color: var(--muted); }
.bin .bslot { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; }
.bin .schip { font-size: 16px; padding: 7px 12px; }
.bin[data-kind="agents"] .schip { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 30%, var(--card)); }
.bin[data-kind="skill"] .schip { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a3) 30%, var(--card)); }
.bin[data-kind="mcp"] .schip { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 30%, var(--card)); }
.bin.dim { opacity: .55; }
.bin.dim .schip { background: var(--card); }
.sort-slide .hint { left: 72px; }

/* ───────────── Presupuesto ───────────── */

.meter { padding: 24px 28px; }
.mbarw { position: relative; }
.mbar2 { display: flex; height: 66px; padding: 6px; gap: 0; border: var(--border); border-radius: 14px; background: var(--term-bg); overflow: hidden; }
.mbar2 .mseg { height: 100%; width: 0; display: grid; place-items: center; overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; font: 700 14px var(--font-body); color: #111; border-radius: 6px; transition: width .6s cubic-bezier(.3, 1.2, .5, 1); }
.mbar2 .mseg + .mseg { margin-left: 3px; }
.half { position: absolute; left: 50%; top: -14px; bottom: -14px; border-left: 4px dashed var(--a1); }
.half span { position: absolute; top: -26px; left: -22px; font: 700 18px var(--font-mono); color: var(--a1); }
.mread { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 20px; margin-top: 16px; }
.mread .mpct { font-size: 46px; }
.mread .mtok { font-size: 20px; color: var(--muted); }
.toggles { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 14px; margin-top: 24px; }
.tgl { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 12px 16px; font: 700 19px var(--font-body); color: var(--ink); text-align: left; border: var(--border); border-radius: 14px; background: var(--card); cursor: pointer; opacity: .55; transition: opacity .25s, transform .25s, box-shadow .25s; }
.tgl i { flex: none; width: 22px; height: 22px; border-radius: 6px; border: 3px solid var(--line); }
.tgl small { display: block; font: 400 15px var(--font-mono); color: var(--muted); }
.tgl.on { opacity: 1; box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #05051a; }
.tgl.on i { background: var(--c); }
.tgl.fixed { cursor: default; }
.budget-slide .hint { bottom: 30px; }

/* ───────────── Se pega adelante ───────────── */

.stackwrap { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 640px 1fr; gap: 40px; margin-top: 4px; }
.reqs { display: flex; gap: 12px; align-items: flex-end; height: 520px; }
.req { flex: 1; display: flex; flex-direction: column-reverse; gap: 4px; padding: 8px; border: var(--border); border-radius: 14px; background: var(--card); animation: chipIn .45s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.5) both; }
.req .rl { position: relative; padding: 4px 8px; font: 700 13px var(--font-mono); border-radius: 6px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 14%, transparent); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; }
.req .rl.sys { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 40%, var(--card)); }
.req .rl.ag { height: 34px; background: var(--a3); color: #111; display: flex; align-items: center; }
.req .rl.me { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 35%, var(--card)); }
.req .rl.bot { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 30%, var(--card)); }
.req .rh { text-align: center; font: 700 15px var(--font-body); color: var(--muted); padding-top: 4px; }
.req.fresh .rl.ag { animation: glow 1s ease-out; }
@keyframes glow { 0% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 var(--a3); } 40% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 8px color-mix(in srgb, var(--a3) 40%, transparent); } }
@keyframes chipIn { from { transform: scale(0) rotate(-30deg); } }
.stackside { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 26px; padding-top: 20px; }
.stackside .big { font-size: 34px; }
.paid { text-align: center; padding: 18px; }
.paidn { font-size: 84px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--a3); line-height: 1.1; }

/* ───────────── Qué va adentro ───────────── */

.notes { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 14px; }
.inside-slide .split { grid-template-columns: 650px 1fr; }
.inside-slide .code { --fs: 15px; }

/* ───────────── Wiki ───────────── */

.wiki-slide .split { grid-template-columns: 600px 1fr; }
.wiki { padding-bottom: 0; }
.wview { height: 470px; overflow: hidden; }
.wfeed { padding: 0 22px; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.55; }
.wfeed div { white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; color: #d6d3f0; }
.wfeed .h { color: #7fa6ff; font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px; }
.wfeed .gen { transition: color .4s; }
.wiki-slide[data-step="3"] .wfeed .gen { color: var(--a1); text-decoration: line-through; }
.wside { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 18px; }
.wcount { display: flex; flex-direction: column; padding: 16px 22px; }
.wcount b { font-size: 56px; color: var(--a3); }
.wcount.bad b { color: var(--a1); }
.nope { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; font-size: 22px; line-height: 1.3; }

/* ───────────── Proyecto y global ───────────── */

.layers-slide .split { grid-template-columns: 640px 1fr; margin-top: 20px; }
.tree { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 16px; padding: 24px 26px; font-size: 20px; }
.tree .tl { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: baseline; gap: 4px 6px; }
.tree .tl .ico { margin-right: 6px; }
.tree .tl b { color: var(--a3); }
.tree .tl em { flex-basis: 100%; padding-left: 36px; font: italic 16px var(--font-body); color: var(--muted); }
.tree .dimline { color: var(--muted); }
.tree .tl.on b { animation: glowtxt 1.2s ease-out; }
@keyframes glowtxt { 30% { text-shadow: 0 0 18px var(--a3); } }
.concat { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; }
.cpiece { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline; padding: 12px 18px; font-size: 20px; }
.cpiece small { font-size: 15px; color: var(--muted); }
.cpiece:nth-of-type(2) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 26%, var(--card)); }
.cpiece:nth-of-type(3) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 24%, var(--card)); }
.cpiece:nth-of-type(4) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a3) 24%, var(--card)); }

/* ───────────── Carpeta ───────────── */

.ftree { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; padding: 22px 24px; font-size: 19px; }
.ftree .fl { padding: 3px 8px; border-radius: 8px; transition: background .35s, color .35s; white-space: nowrap; }
.ftree .fl em { margin-left: 8px; font: italic 14px var(--font-body); color: var(--a3); }
.ftree .fl.root { font-weight: 700; }
.ftree .fl.hot { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a3) 30%, transparent); }
.fwhere { margin-top: 18px; padding-top: 14px; border-top: 2px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 15%, transparent); display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; }
.folder-slide .code { --fs: 16px; }

/* ───────────── Validador ───────────── */

.vform { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; padding: 24px 26px; background: var(--term-bg); }
.vrow { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; font-size: 20px; }
.vrow.top { align-items: flex-start; }
.vrow .k { color: var(--a3); flex: none; }
.vrow .dash { color: var(--a1); font-weight: 700; }
.vform input, .vform textarea { flex: 1; padding: 8px 12px; font: 20px var(--font-mono); color: var(--ink); background: #ffffff10; border: 2px solid #ffffff30; border-radius: 10px; outline: none; transition: border-color .2s, background .2s; }
.vform textarea { height: 190px; resize: none; font-size: 17px; line-height: 1.45; }
.vform input:focus, .vform textarea:focus { border-color: var(--a3); }
.vform input.bad { border-color: var(--bad); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--bad) 14%, transparent); }
.vcount { text-align: right; }
.vcount.bad { color: var(--bad); }
.vtry { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 8px; margin-top: 6px; }
.vtry button { padding: 5px 12px; font: 15px var(--font-mono); color: var(--ink); background: var(--card); border: 2px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; }
.vtry button:hover { background: var(--a2); }
.vrules { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; padding: 22px 24px; font-size: 20px; min-height: 470px; }
.rule2 { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; transition: color .25s; }
.rule2 i { flex: none; width: 30px; height: 30px; display: grid; place-items: center; font-style: normal; font-weight: 700; border: 3px solid var(--line); border-radius: 50%; transition: background .25s, transform .3s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.8); }
.rule2.ok i { background: var(--good); color: #111; }
.rule2.ok i::after { content: "✓"; }
.rule2.no { color: var(--bad); }
.rule2.no i { background: var(--bad); color: #fff; transform: scale(1.12); }
.rule2.no i::after { content: "✗"; }
.rule2.soft.no { color: var(--a3); }
.rule2.soft.no i { background: var(--a3); color: #111; }
.rule2.soft.no i::after { content: "?"; }
.vrules .mascot { position: absolute; right: 16px; bottom: 14px; --size: 90px; }

/* ───────────── Tres etapas ───────────── */

.pd-slide .track.mini { margin-bottom: 4px; }
.pdwrap { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 330px; gap: 26px; margin-top: 30px; }
.sgrid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(5, 1fr); gap: 10px; align-content: start; }
.sk { position: relative; padding: 8px 10px; min-height: 68px; font: 700 14px var(--font-mono); border: 2px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 40%, transparent); border-radius: 10px; background: var(--card); opacity: .35; transition: opacity .4s, background .4s, transform .45s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.6), box-shadow .3s; }
.sk small { display: block; margin-top: 4px; font: 400 11px var(--font-body); color: var(--muted); }
.sk.meta { opacity: 1; }
.sk.active { background: var(--a3); color: #111; transform: scale(1.14); box-shadow: 5px 5px 0 #05051a; z-index: 2; }
.sk.active small { color: #333; }
.sk .res { display: none; margin-top: 6px; padding: 4px 6px; font: 700 11px var(--font-mono); color: #111; background: var(--a4); border-radius: 6px; animation: chipIn .4s both; }
.sk.res-on .res { display: block; }
.pdside { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 18px; }
.pdstage { padding: 18px 22px; min-height: 150px; }
.pdtitle { font-family: var(--font-display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 30px; margin-bottom: 8px; }
.pdmeter { padding: 18px 22px; }
.pdmeter b { display: block; font-size: 52px; color: var(--a3); }
.pdall { margin-top: 4px; }

/* ───────────── Trigger ───────────── */

.tprompt { padding: 8px 0; font-size: 24px; margin-top: 8px; }
.tprompt .line { min-height: 40px; }
.tcards { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1.5fr; gap: 28px; margin-top: 30px; }
.tcard { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; padding: 22px 24px; min-height: 280px; transition: background .5s, opacity .5s, transform .5s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.5), filter .5s; }
.tname { font-size: 26px; font-weight: 700; }
.tdesc { font-size: 17px; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--muted); }
.tdesc u { text-decoration: none; border-radius: 4px; padding: 0 2px; transition: background .3s, color .3s; }
.tverdict { margin-top: auto; align-self: flex-start; padding: 6px 14px; font-weight: 700; border-radius: 999px; opacity: 0; transform: scale(.5); transition: opacity .3s, transform .45s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.8); }
.trigger-slide[data-step="2"] .tverdict { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
.trigger-slide[data-step="2"] .vague { filter: grayscale(1); opacity: .5; }
.trigger-slide[data-step="2"] .vague .tverdict { background: var(--card); border: 2px solid var(--muted); }
.trigger-slide[data-step="2"] .good { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--good) 22%, var(--card)); transform: scale(1.02); }
.trigger-slide[data-step="2"] .good .tverdict { background: var(--good); color: #111; }
.trigger-slide[data-step="2"] .good u { background: var(--a3); color: #111; }

/* ───────────── Regla ───────────── */

.rulebig { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 34px; margin-top: 150px; }
.rb { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 420px 80px 360px; align-items: center; padding: 22px 34px; font-family: var(--font-display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 56px; }
.rb b { color: var(--a1); text-align: center; }
.rb .mono { font-size: 50px; }
.rb:nth-child(1) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 26%, var(--card)); }
.rb:nth-child(2) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a3) 26%, var(--card)); }

/* ───────────── Tool ───────────── */

.chat .viewport { height: 418px; overflow: hidden; }
.chat .feed { transition: transform .45s cubic-bezier(.3, 1, .4, 1); }
.chat .line { min-height: 0; padding: 4px 28px; font-size: 22px; transition: opacity .4s; }
.chat .line.gap { margin-top: 14px; }
.chat .line.ag { color: var(--muted); }
.chat .line.ag .p { color: var(--muted); }
.chat .line.q .p { color: var(--a1); }
.chat .line.ok .p { color: var(--a4); }
.chat .line.ans { padding-left: 64px; }
.chat .line.hide { display: none; }
.chat .line.add, .chat .line.del, .chat .line.cmd, .chat .line.out { padding: 0 28px 0 64px; font-size: 19px; }
.chat .line.cmd { padding-left: 28px; padding-top: 6px; color: var(--term-ink); }
.chat .line.cmd .p { color: var(--a2); }
