.chat .line.wait .p { color: var(--a3); }
.chat .line.wait.done .p { color: var(--a4); }
.chat .line .t { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.chat .line.doc { padding: 0 28px 0 64px; font-size: 19px; color: var(--a3); }
.chat .line.doc .p { color: var(--a2); }
.chat .line.doc .t { white-space: pre; }
.tool-slide .chat .line { font-size: 20px; }
.tool-slide .chat .line.doc { font-size: 17px; }
.tool-slide .code { --fs: 16px; }

/* ───────────── N×M ───────────── */

.nm { width: 100%; height: 470px; overflow: visible; margin-top: -10px; }
.nm .mesh line { stroke: var(--a1); stroke-width: 2.5; opacity: .7; transition: opacity .5s; }
.nm .hubl line { stroke: var(--a4); stroke-width: 4; stroke-dasharray: 600; stroke-dashoffset: 600; transition: stroke-dashoffset 1s ease-out; }
.nm .hub { opacity: 0; transform: scale(.3); transform-origin: 568px 235px; transform-box: view-box; transition: opacity .4s, transform .6s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.6); }
.nm .hub circle { fill: var(--a4); stroke: var(--line); stroke-width: 4; }
.nm .hub text { font-family: var(--font-display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 34px; fill: #111; text-anchor: middle; }
.nm .nodes rect { fill: var(--card); stroke: var(--line); stroke-width: 3; }
.nm .nodes .h rect { fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 40%, var(--card)); }
.nm .nodes text { font-family: var(--font-body); font-weight: 700; font-size: 21px; fill: var(--ink); text-anchor: middle; dominant-baseline: middle; }
.nm.hubbed .mesh line { opacity: 0; }
.nm.hubbed .hubl line { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
.nm.hubbed .hub { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
.nm:not(.hubbed) .mesh { animation: jitter .18s linear infinite; }
@keyframes jitter { 50% { transform: translate(0, 1px); } }
.nmcount { position: absolute; left: 72px; bottom: 44px; display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 16px; }
.nmcount b { font-size: 44px; color: var(--a1); transition: color .4s; }
.nm-slide[data-step="1"] .nmcount b { color: var(--a4); }

/* ───────────── Arquitectura ───────────── */

.arch { width: 100%; height: 470px; overflow: visible; }
.arch .a1, .arch .a2, .arch .a3 { opacity: 0; transition: opacity .5s; }
.arch-slide[data-step="1"] .a1, .arch-slide[data-step="2"] .a1, .arch-slide[data-step="3"] .a1,
.arch-slide[data-step="2"] .a2, .arch-slide[data-step="3"] .a2, .arch-slide[data-step="3"] .a3 { opacity: 1; }
.arch .host { fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 14%, var(--card)); stroke: var(--line); stroke-width: 3; }
.arch .model { fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 35%, var(--card)); stroke: var(--line); stroke-width: 3; }
.arch .client { fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 40%, var(--card)); stroke: var(--line); stroke-width: 3; }
.arch .server { fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 30%, var(--card)); stroke: var(--line); stroke-width: 3; }
.arch .server.remote { fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a3) 30%, var(--card)); }
.arch .wire { fill: none; stroke: var(--muted); stroke-width: 3; }
.arch .link { fill: none; stroke: var(--line); stroke-width: 4; stroke-dasharray: 10 8; animation: dash 1s linear infinite; }
@keyframes dash { to { stroke-dashoffset: -18; } }
.arch .lbl { font-family: var(--font-body); font-weight: 700; font-size: 22px; fill: var(--ink); text-anchor: middle; }
.arch .lbl.big { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 26px; text-anchor: start; }
.arch .sub { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 16px; fill: var(--muted); text-anchor: middle; }
.arch .tlbl { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 17px; fill: var(--a3); text-anchor: middle; paint-order: stroke; stroke: var(--bg); stroke-width: 6px; }
.arch .pkt { fill: var(--a3); }
.archnotes { position: absolute; left: 72px; right: 72px; bottom: 30px; display: flex; gap: 40px; font-size: 22px; color: var(--muted); }

/* ───────────── Capas ───────────── */

.outer { margin-top: 22px; padding: 18px 20px 20px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a3) 14%, var(--card)); }
.otitle { font-size: 24px; margin-bottom: 6px; }
.otitle b { font-family: var(--font-display); }
.trdesc { min-height: 56px; margin-bottom: 14px; }
.inner { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; padding: 16px 18px; font-size: 22px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 30%, var(--card)); }
.inner b { font-family: var(--font-display); }
.layer2-slide .outer[data-step] { opacity: .2; transform: none; }
.layer2-slide .outer.on { opacity: 1; }
.layer2-slide .outer .inner[data-step].on { opacity: 1; }

/* ───────────── Primitivas ───────────── */

.prims { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 24px; margin-top: 20px; }
.prim { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; min-height: 290px; font-size: 21px; line-height: 1.3; }
.prim .ico { font-size: 46px; }
.prim h3 { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-mono); }
.prim p { color: var(--muted); }
.prim .who { margin-top: auto; padding: 6px 12px; align-self: flex-start; border-radius: 999px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 10%, transparent); }
.prim .m { font-size: 14px; color: var(--muted); }
.prim:nth-child(1) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 22%, var(--card)); }
.prim:nth-child(2) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 26%, var(--card)); }
.prim:nth-child(3) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 22%, var(--card)); }
.clientprim { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 20px; margin-top: 24px; padding: 16px 24px; font-size: 22px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a3) 22%, var(--card)); }
.clientprim .ico { font-size: 44px; }
.clientprim div { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; }

/* ───────────── Secuencia ───────────── */

.seq { width: 430px; height: 480px; padding: 0; overflow: visible; }
.seq .actor rect { fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 35%, var(--card)); stroke: var(--line); stroke-width: 3; }
.seq .actor.server rect { fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 35%, var(--card)); }
.seq .actor text { font-family: var(--font-display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 20px; fill: var(--ink); text-anchor: middle; dominant-baseline: middle; }
.seq .life { stroke: var(--muted); stroke-width: 2; stroke-dasharray: 6 6; }
.seq text { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 15px; fill: var(--ink); text-anchor: middle; paint-order: stroke; stroke: var(--card); stroke-width: 6px; }
.seq .msg { opacity: 0; transition: opacity .3s; }
.seq .msg.on { opacity: 1; }
.seq .msg.cur text { fill: var(--a3); font-weight: 700; }
.seq .msg line { stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 2.5; marker-end: url(#seq-head); stroke-dasharray: 262; stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
.seq .msg.back line { stroke-dasharray: 7 6; }
.seq .msg.fresh:not(.back) line { animation: seqdraw .5s ease-out; }
.seq .msg.ok text { fill: var(--good); }
.seq .msg.nt line { stroke: var(--a3); }
.seq .notelbl { font-size: 13px; fill: var(--muted); }
.seq marker path { fill: var(--ink); }
@keyframes seqdraw { from { stroke-dashoffset: 262; } }
.seqright .code { --fs: 15px; }
.seqcap { margin-top: 14px; }

/* ───────────── Config ───────────── */

.cfgside { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 14px; }
.cfgn { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; padding: 14px 18px; font-size: 20px; line-height: 1.3; }
.cfgn b { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 24px; }
.cfgn span { color: var(--muted); }

/* ───────────── Costo ───────────── */

.costs { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; margin-top: 40px; }
.crow { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 360px 120px 160px 1fr; align-items: center; gap: 20px; padding: 16px 24px; font-size: 28px; border: var(--border); border-radius: 16px; background: var(--card); }
.crow.head { padding: 4px 24px; font-size: 20px; color: var(--muted); border: 0; background: none; }
.cbar { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 14px; }
.cbar i { display: block; height: 30px; width: 0; border-radius: 8px; background: var(--a1); transition: width 1.2s cubic-bezier(.3, 1.2, .5, 1) .2s; }
.crow.on .cbar i { width: calc(var(--w) * 4); }
.cbar b { font-size: 26px; }
.cite2 { position: absolute; right: 72px; bottom: 34px; }

/* ───────────── Discovery ───────────── */

.discbar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 22px; padding: 16px 22px; margin-top: 4px; }
.dmeter { flex: 1; height: 40px; padding: 4px; border: var(--border); border-radius: 10px; background: var(--term-bg); }
.dfill { height: 100%; width: 75%; border-radius: 5px; background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, var(--a1) 0 14px, color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 70%, #000) 14px 16px); transition: width 1s cubic-bezier(.3, 1.2, .5, 1), background .4s; }
.disc-slide.prog .dfill { width: 1%; background: var(--a4); }
.dtok { min-width: 150px; font-size: 32px; color: var(--a1); text-align: right; transition: color .4s; }
.disc-slide.prog .dtok { color: var(--a4); }
.layers3 { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 20px; margin-top: 22px; }
.l3c { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; padding: 16px 18px; }
.l3c h3 { margin: 0; font-size: 26px; }
.l3c .code { --fs: 15px; box-shadow: none; }
.l3c .code .ln { display: none; }
.l3c .code .cl { padding-left: 14px; }
.l3c .code .cbar { display: none; }
.discnote { margin-top: 18px; }

/* ───────────── Code mode ───────────── */

.lanes { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 22px; }
.lane { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 260px 1fr 200px; align-items: center; gap: 22px; padding: 18px 24px; }
.lh { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; }
.lh b { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 28px; }
.ltrack { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; height: 110px; }
.lnode { position: relative; z-index: 2; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 96px; height: 96px; font-size: 40px; border: var(--border); border-radius: 18px; background: var(--card); }
.lnode small { font-size: 13px; color: var(--muted); }
.lnode.sbx { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a3) 25%, var(--card)); }
.lpipe { position: relative; flex: 1; height: 8px; border-radius: 4px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 18%, transparent); }
.ltok { text-align: right; }
.ltok b { display: block; font-size: 40px; color: var(--muted); transition: color .3s; }
.lane.hot .ltok b { color: var(--a1); }
.lane.cool .ltok b { color: var(--a4); }
.dot2 { position: absolute; top: 50%; z-index: 3; padding: 2px 6px; font: 700 12px var(--font-mono); color: #111; border-radius: 6px; white-space: nowrap; background: var(--a1); transform: translate(-50%, -50%); pointer-events: none; }
.dot2.code { background: var(--a3); }
.dot2.res { background: var(--a4); }
.cm2-slide .code { --fs: 15px; }
.cmside { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 14px; }

/* ───────────── Sandbox ───────────── */

.flowsvg { width: 560px; height: 420px; overflow: visible; }
.flowsvg .hostbox { fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 12%, var(--card)); stroke: var(--line); stroke-width: 3; }
.flowsvg .b { stroke: var(--line); stroke-width: 3; fill: var(--card); }
.flowsvg .llm { fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 32%, var(--card)); }
.flowsvg .box { fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a3) 28%, var(--card)); }
.flowsvg .cli { fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 36%, var(--card)); }
.flowsvg .srv { fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 30%, var(--card)); }
.flowsvg .lbl { font-family: var(--font-body); font-weight: 700; font-size: 20px; fill: var(--ink); text-anchor: middle; }
.flowsvg .lbl.s { font-size: 16px; }
.flowsvg .cap { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 14px; fill: var(--a3); }
.flowsvg path { fill: none; stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 3; stroke-dasharray: 8 7; animation: dash 1s linear infinite; }
.flowsvg .fl3 { stroke: var(--a4); }
.sec { list-style: none; margin: 10px 0 0; padding: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 18px; font-size: 25px; line-height: 1.3; }

/* ───────────── Pi: no y después sí ───────────── */

.posts { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 60px 1fr; align-items: stretch; gap: 14px; margin-top: 10px; }
.post { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; padding: 20px 24px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 16%, var(--card)); }
.post.yes { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 18%, var(--card)); }
.post h3 { margin: 0; font-size: 26px; }
.post ul { margin: 0; padding-left: 22px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; font-size: 20px; line-height: 1.3; }
.post q { margin-top: auto; font: italic 18px var(--font-body); color: var(--a3); }
.pdate { font-size: 15px; color: var(--muted); }
.parrow { align-self: center; text-align: center; font: 700 48px var(--font-display); color: var(--a1); }

/* ───────────── Exposure ───────────── */

.exseg button { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 16px; }
.expo-slide .code { --fs: 16px; }
.xflist.exlist { gap: 6px; }
.xflist.exlist span { padding: 4px 7px; font-size: 12.5px; }

/* ───────────── Anatomía ───────────── */

.term.mini2 { padding-bottom: 14px; }
.term.mini2 .line { min-height: 0; padding: 4px 22px; font-size: 17px; }
.term.mini2 .line.dim { color: var(--muted); }
.tally { margin: 12px 22px 0; padding: 6px 14px; display: inline-block; font: 700 17px var(--font-body); border-radius: 999px; }
.tally.bad { background: var(--a1); color: #111; }
.tally.good { background: var(--good); color: #111; }
.better-slide .term.mini2 { min-height: 330px; }
.reason-slide .term.mini2 { min-height: 360px; }

.hgrid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 260px 1fr; grid-template-rows: 1fr 1fr; gap: 24px; margin-top: 30px; height: 460px; }
.hgrid > :nth-child(1) { grid-column: 1; grid-row: 1; }
.hgrid > :nth-child(2) { grid-column: 3; grid-row: 1; }
.hgrid > :nth-child(3) { grid-column: 2; grid-row: 1 / 3; }
.hgrid > :nth-child(4) { grid-column: 1; grid-row: 2; }
.hgrid > :nth-child(5) { grid-column: 3; grid-row: 2; }
.hcard { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; padding: 20px 24px; font-size: 22px; line-height: 1.3; }
.hcard b { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 30px; }
.hcard small { margin-top: auto; font-size: 17px; color: var(--muted); }
.hcard.hot { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a3) 26%, var(--card)); }
.hcard.hot small { color: var(--a3); font-weight: 700; }
.hcore { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 10px; border: 4px dashed color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 35%, transparent); border-radius: 50%; font-size: 26px; font-weight: 700; }
.hcore .mascot { --size: 140px; }

.exttable { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; margin-top: 10px; }
.er { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 260px 1fr 220px; align-items: center; gap: 16px; padding: 10px 20px; font-size: 21px; border: var(--border); border-radius: 12px; background: var(--card); }
.er > span:first-child { font-weight: 700; }
.er em { text-align: right; font-size: 17px; color: var(--muted); }
.er.hot { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 28%, var(--card)); }
.er.hot em { color: var(--ink); font-weight: 700; }
.er.dim { opacity: .55; }

.reveal-slide .code { --fs: 15px; }
.calls { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; padding: 18px 20px; }
.callsh { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 4px; }
.pmode { padding: 6px 14px; font: 700 16px var(--font-mono); color: var(--ink); background: var(--card); border: var(--border); border-radius: 999px; cursor: pointer; }
.pmode.on { background: var(--a3); color: #111; }
.call { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 10px 14px; font-size: 17px; border: 2px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 30%, transparent); border-radius: 10px; }
.call b { padding: 3px 10px; font: 700 14px var(--font-body); border-radius: 999px; opacity: 0; transform: scale(.5); transition: opacity .3s, transform .4s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.8); }
.calls.show .call b { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
.call b.ok { background: var(--good); color: #111; }
.call b.no { background: var(--bad); color: #fff; }
.call.blocked { border-color: var(--bad); }
.creason { min-height: 52px; padding: 8px 12px; color: var(--a3); border-left: 4px solid var(--a3); opacity: 0; transition: opacity .3s; }
.calls.show .creason.on { opacity: 1; }

.secgrid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 22px; margin-top: 20px; }
.secgrid .card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; min-height: 200px; font-size: 22px; line-height: 1.3; }
.secgrid .card h3 { margin: 0; }
.secgrid .card .ico { font-size: 40px; }
.secgrid .card p { color: var(--muted); }
.secgrid .card.hot { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 22%, var(--card)); }

.eli5-slide .code { --fs: 16px; }
.eli5-slide .code .cl { white-space: pre-wrap; }

/* ───────────── FastMCP ───────────── */

.fserver-slide .code { --fs: 14.5px; }
.gen { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; }
.gen .code { --fs: 14.5px; }
.genh { font-weight: 700; }
.frun-slide .chat .line { font-size: 18px; }
.frun-slide .chat .line.cmd, .frun-slide .chat .line.out { font-size: 16px; }
.fclient-slide .code, .compose-slide .code { --fs: 16px; }
.frun-slide .code { --fs: 15px; }
.ctree { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 14px; }
.cnode { padding: 12px 18px; font-size: 24px; font-weight: 700; }
.cnode.main { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a3) 30%, var(--card)); }
.cnode.remote { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 30%, var(--card)); }
.cbranch { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; margin-left: 40px; padding-left: 20px; border-left: 4px solid var(--line); }
.ctool { color: var(--a4); }
.xfseg button { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 16px; }
.xf-slide .code { --fs: 16px; }
.xfsees { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; padding: 18px 20px; min-height: 400px; }
.xflist { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; align-content: flex-start; min-height: 230px; }
.xflist span { padding: 5px 10px; font: 700 15px var(--font-mono); border: 2px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 28%, var(--card)); animation: chipIn .35s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.8) both; }
.xflist span.meta { background: var(--a3); color: #111; font-size: 18px; padding: 8px 14px; }
.xfcap { margin-top: auto; font-size: 18px; }
.xfcap b { color: var(--a3); }

/* ───────────── Tabla ───────────── */

.bigtable { width: 100%; margin-top: 40px; border-collapse: separate; border-spacing: 0 12px; font-size: 30px; }
.bigtable th { text-align: left; padding: 0 24px; font-size: 22px; font-weight: 400; color: var(--muted); }
.bigtable td { padding: 20px 24px; background: var(--card); border-top: var(--border); border-bottom: var(--border); }
.bigtable td:first-child { border-left: var(--border); border-radius: 16px 0 0 16px; font-weight: 700; }
.bigtable td:last-child { border-right: var(--border); border-radius: 0 16px 16px 0; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 22%, var(--card)); }
.bigtable td.open { color: var(--muted); font-style: italic; background: var(--card); }
.bigtable tr[data-step] { transform: translateX(-30px); }
.bigtable tr[data-step].on { transform: none; }

/* ───────────── Práctica ───────────── */

.timer { position: absolute; right: 72px; top: 50px; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 40px; padding: 8px 18px; border: var(--border); border-radius: 12px; background: var(--card); box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 var(--line); cursor: pointer; user-select: none; }
.installs { display: flex; gap: 16px; }
.steps-slide .track { margin-top: 140px; }
.steps-slide .track .rider { --size: 100px; top: -44px; }

/* ───────────── Cierre ───────────── */

.live { display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center; align-items: center; height: 88%; gap: 30px; }
.collage { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); gap: 24px 22px; margin-top: 6px; }
.tile { display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-between; gap: 10px; height: 205px; padding: 16px 18px; font-size: 21px; font-weight: 700; }
.tile.f-drop { transition-delay: calc(var(--i) * .16s); }
.tile:nth-child(4n + 1) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 22%, var(--card)); }
.tile:nth-child(4n + 2) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 26%, var(--card)); }
.tile:nth-child(4n + 3) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a3) 22%, var(--card)); }
.tile:nth-child(4n + 4) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 22%, var(--card)); }
.tile .viz { flex: 1; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 12px; }
.tile .viz.big { font-size: 30px; white-space: nowrap; }
.vcards2 { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 26px; margin-top: 50px; }
.vcards2 .card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; min-height: 280px; font-size: 23px; line-height: 1.35; }
.vcards2 .card h3 { margin: 0; }
.vcards2 .card .ico { font-size: 44px; }
.vcards2 .card.next { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 28%, var(--card)); }

/* ───────────── HUD ───────────── */

#hud {
  position: fixed;
  left: 0;
  right: 0;
  bottom: 0;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  padding: 10px 18px;
  font: 14px/1 system-ui, sans-serif;
  color: var(--muted);
  opacity: .25;
  transition: opacity .3s;
  z-index: 60;
}

#hud:hover { opacity: 1; }
#hud.hidden { display: none; }
#hud .stepdots i { display: inline-block; width: 7px; height: 7px; margin: 0 2px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; opacity: .3; }
#hud .stepdots i.on { opacity: 1; }
</style>
</head>
<body>

<div id="deck">

  <section class="slide" data-id="portada-propuesta">
    <div class="section">
      <div class="small">Propuesta para la Sesión 5 · salió de la Sesión 3</div>
      <h1>MCP por dentro</h1>
      <p class="big">transportes, code mode y <span class="hl">tu propio servidor</span> con FastMCP</p>
      <p class="small" style="margin-top: 18px">a coordinar con Agus: no está en el plan de la Sesión 5</p>
    </div>
    <div class="mascot" data-mood="happy"></div>
  </section>

  <section class="slide layer2-slide" data-id="capas" data-steps="2">
    <h2>Dos capas</h2>
    <div class="split" style="grid-template-columns: 470px 1fr">
      <div>
        <div class="seg2"><button data-tr="stdio" class="on">stdio</button><button data-tr="http">Streamable HTTP</button></div>
        <div class="outer card" data-step="2">
          <div class="otitle"><b>transporte</b> · <span class="trname">stdio</span></div>
          <div class="small trdesc"></div>
          <div class="inner card" data-step="1">
            <b>datos · JSON-RPC 2.0</b>
            <div class="small">los mismos mensajes, vayan por donde vayan: <span class="mono">tools/list</span>, <span class="mono">tools/call</span>…</div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="code" data-code="tr-stdio" style="--h: 470px"></div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="slide race-slide" data-id="codemode" data-steps="2">
    <h2>Code mode</h2>
    <p class="mid lead">"Encontrá los errores de la última hora y abrí un ticket por cada error distinto"</p>
    <div class="lanes">
      <div class="lane card" data-lane="direct">
        <div class="lh"><b>llamada directa</b><span class="small">cada resultado pasa por el modelo</span></div>
        <div class="ltrack"><span class="lnode">🧠<small>modelo</small></span><div class="lpipe"></div><span class="lnode">🔧<small>tools</small></span></div>
        <div class="ltok"><b class="mono">0</b><span class="small">tokens en contexto</span></div>
      </div>
      <div class="lane card" data-lane="code">
        <div class="lh"><b>code mode</b><span class="small">el modelo escribe código; corre en un sandbox</span></div>
        <div class="ltrack"><span class="lnode">🧠<small>modelo</small></span><div class="lpipe"></div><span class="lnode sbx">📦<small>sandbox</small></span><div class="lpipe in"></div><span class="lnode">🔧<small>tools</small></span></div>
        <div class="ltok"><b class="mono">0</b><span class="small">tokens en contexto</span></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="slide cm2-slide" data-id="codemode2" data-steps="3">
    <h2>Lo que escribe el modelo</h2>
    <div class="split" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 380px">
      <div class="code" data-code="codemode" data-marks="1=1-5 2=7-13 3=15-17" style="--h: 540px"></div>
      <div class="cmside">
        <div class="card note2" data-step="1"><b>🔧 las tools son funciones</b><span>el host genera una API tipada a partir de los schemas MCP</span></div>
        <div class="card note2" data-step="2"><b>🧹 filtrar no gasta contexto</b><span>miles de logs se deduplican adentro del sandbox</span></div>
        <div class="card note2" data-step="3"><b>📨 vuelve una línea</b><span>solo el <span class="mono">console.log</span> entra al contexto</span></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="slide sbx-slide" data-id="sandbox" data-steps="2">
    <h2>Code mode necesita un sandbox</h2>
    <div class="split" style="grid-template-columns: 560px 1fr">
      <svg class="flowsvg" viewBox="0 0 560 420">
        <rect class="hostbox" x="10" y="10" width="360" height="400" rx="18" />
        <text class="lbl" x="30" y="44" style="text-anchor: start">host</text>
        <rect class="b llm" x="40" y="70" width="140" height="70" rx="12" /><text class="lbl" x="110" y="112">🧠 modelo</text>
        <rect class="b box" x="40" y="200" width="300" height="70" rx="12" /><text class="lbl" x="190" y="242">📦 sandbox · sin red</text>
        <rect class="b cli" x="40" y="320" width="300" height="70" rx="12" /><text class="lbl" x="190" y="362">🔌 cliente MCP · 🔑</text>
        <path class="fl1" d="M110 140 V200" /><text class="cap" x="120" y="176">código</text>
        <path class="fl2" d="M250 270 V320" /><text class="cap" x="260" y="300">call_tool</text>
        <path class="fl3" d="M220 200 Q220 105 180 105" /><text class="cap" x="230" y="160">console.log</text>
        <path class="fl4" d="M340 345 H440 M340 365 H440" />
        <rect class="b srv" x="440" y="300" width="110" height="40" rx="10" /><text class="lbl s" x="495" y="326">server A</text>
        <rect class="b srv" x="440" y="350" width="110" height="40" rx="10" /><text class="lbl s" x="495" y="376">server B</text>
      </svg>
      <ul class="sec stagger2">
        <li data-step="1">🚫 el sandbox <b>no tiene red</b>: solo puede llamar a los stubs</li>
        <li data-step="1">🔑 las credenciales las tiene el host, <b>nunca el código</b></li>
        <li data-step="2">✋ aprobar el script <b>no aprueba</b> cada llamada que hace</li>
        <li data-step="2">⏱️ timeout y límite de memoria</li>
        <li data-step="2">☣️ lo que devuelve un servidor es <b>input no confiable</b> para otro</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </section>

  <!-- ───────── FastMCP ───────── -->

  <section class="slide" data-id="sec-fastmcp">
    <div class="section">
      <div class="track mini secttrack" data-stops="MCP por dentro|FastMCP"></div>
      <h1>FastMCP</h1>
      <p class="big">tu propio servidor (y cliente) MCP,<br>con funciones de Python <span class="hl">de toda la vida</span></p>
      <p class="small" style="margin-top: 18px"><span class="mono">uv add fastmcp</span> · gofastmcp.com · su API de alto nivel entró al SDK oficial de Python en 2024</p>
    </div>
    <div class="mascot" data-mood="joy"></div>
  </section>

  <section class="slide fserver-slide" data-id="servidor" data-steps="3">
    <h2>Un servidor en 20 líneas</h2>
    <div class="split" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 470px">
      <div class="code" data-code="fastmcp-server" data-marks="1=6-9 2=11-14 3=16-19" style="--h: 540px"></div>
      <div class="gen">
        <div class="small genh">lo que FastMCP genera y publica</div>
        <div class="code" data-code="gen1" style="--h: 400px"></div>
        <div class="small gencap">type hints → <b>inputSchema</b> · docstring → <b>description</b></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="slide frun-slide" data-id="correr" data-steps="4">
    <h2>Correrlo y enchufarlo</h2>
    <div class="split" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 450px">
      <div class="term chat">
        <div class="bar3"><i></i><i></i><i></i><span class="title">tareas-mcp</span></div>
        <div class="viewport" style="height: 440px"><div class="feed" data-chat="fastrun"></div></div>
      </div>
      <div>
        <div class="code" data-code="fastmcp-json" style="--h: 300px"></div>
        <p class="small" style="margin-top: 14px">stdio para usarlo vos · <span class="mono">--transport http</span> para que lo use otro</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="slide fclient-slide" data-id="cliente" data-steps="2">
    <h2>El cliente: el mismo para usarlo y para testearlo</h2>
    <div class="split" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr">
      <div class="f-flip" data-step="1"><div class="code" data-code="fastmcp-client" style="--h: 400px"></div><p class="small" style="margin-top: 12px">contra un servidor de verdad, por HTTP</p></div>
      <div class="f-flip" data-step="2"><div class="code" data-code="fastmcp-test" style="--h: 400px"></div><p class="small" style="margin-top: 12px"><span class="mono">Client(mcp)</span>: en memoria, sin red ni procesos</p></div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="slide compose-slide" data-id="componer" data-steps="2">
    <h2>Componer servidores: mount y proxy</h2>
    <div class="split" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 460px">
      <div class="code" data-code="fastmcp-mount" data-marks="1=6 2=7-8" style="--h: 300px"></div>
      <div class="ctree">
        <div class="card cnode main">🧩 curso</div>
        <div class="cbranch" data-step="1"><div class="card cnode">📋 tareas <span class="mono small">en proceso</span></div><div class="mono small ctool">tareas_agregar_tarea</div></div>
        <div class="cbranch" data-step="2"><div class="card cnode remote">🌐 api <span class="mono small">proxy remoto</span></div><div class="mono small ctool">api_…</div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <p class="small" style="margin-top: 26px">el <span class="mono">namespace</span> le pone prefijo a cada tool: nada choca con nada</p>
  </section>

  <section class="slide xf-slide" data-id="transforms" data-steps="2">
    <h2>Las buenas prácticas, del lado del servidor</h2>
    <div class="seg2 xfseg"><button data-xf="none" class="on">sin transform</button><button data-xf="search">BM25SearchTransform</button><button data-xf="code">CodeMode</button></div>
    <div class="split" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 440px; margin-top: 18px">
      <div class="code" data-code="xf-none" style="--h: 400px"></div>
      <div class="card xfsees">
        <div class="small">lo que ve el cliente en <span class="mono">tools/list</span></div>
        <div class="xflist"></div>
        <div class="small xfcap"></div>
      </div>

</div>

<div id="hud">
  <div><span class="count"></span>   <span class="stepdots"></span></div>
  <div>← → navegar · F pantalla completa · H ocultar</div>
</div>

<script>
const $ = (sel, root = document) => root.querySelector(sel);
const $$ = (sel, root = document) => [...root.querySelectorAll(sel)];
const rand = (a, b) => a + Math.random() * (b - a);
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

/* ───────────── Mascot ───────────── */

const EYES = {
  open: '<ellipse cx="38" cy="52" rx="5" ry="6.5" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/><ellipse cx="62" cy="52" rx="5" ry="6.5" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/><circle cx="40" cy="50" r="1.8" fill="#fff"/><circle cx="64" cy="50" r="1.8" fill="#fff"/>',
  wide: '<circle cx="38" cy="51" r="8" fill="#fff" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="62" cy="51" r="8" fill="#fff" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="39" cy="52" r="3.5" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/><circle cx="61" cy="52" r="3.5" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/>',
  half: '<path d="M32 51 h12 M56 51 h12" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M33 52 q5 6 10 0 M57 52 q5 6 10 0" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/><path d="M31 42 l12 3 M69 42 l-12 3" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
  x: '<path d="M33 47 l10 10 M43 47 l-10 10 M57 47 l10 10 M67 47 l-10 10" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3.5" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
  happy: '<path d="M32 54 q6 -9 12 0 M56 54 q6 -9 12 0" fill="none" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3.5" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
  odd: '<circle cx="38" cy="53" r="4" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/><circle cx="62" cy="50" r="8" fill="#fff" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="61" cy="51" r="3.5" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/><path d="M30 44 l14 -3 M55 36 l14 4" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
};

const MOUTH = {
  smile: '<path d="M42 64 Q50 73 58 64" fill="none" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3.5" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
  grin: '<path d="M40 63 Q50 78 60 63 Z" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/><path d="M45 69 Q50 73 55 69" fill="#ff7a93"/>',
  worried: '<path d="M43 69 Q50 63 57 69" fill="none" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3.5" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
  flat: '<path d="M44 67 h12" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3.5" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
  wow: '<ellipse cx="50" cy="68" rx="4.5" ry="5.5" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/>',
  squiggle: '<path d="M40 68 q3 -4 6 0 t6 0 t6 0" fill="none" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
};

const MOODS = {
  happy: { eyes: "open", mouth: "smile" },
  wave: { eyes: "happy", mouth: "grin", arm: true },
  joy: { eyes: "happy", mouth: "grin" },
  sweat: { eyes: "wide", mouth: "worried", drop: true },
  dizzy: { eyes: "x", mouth: "squiggle" },
  skeptic: { eyes: "half", mouth: "flat" },
  wow: { eyes: "wide", mouth: "wow" },
  confused: { eyes: "odd", mouth: "squiggle", q: true },
  frustrated: { eyes: "half", mouth: "worried", steam: true },
};

const mascotSVG = (mood) => {
  const m = MOODS[mood] || MOODS.happy;

  return `<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100">
    <ellipse cx="50" cy="94" rx="30" ry="4" fill="#000" opacity=".12"/>
    ${m.arm ? '<path class="arm" d="M84 60 q14 -8 10 -26" fill="none" stroke="var(--mascot)" stroke-width="9" stroke-linecap="round"/>' : ""}
    <path d="M50 12 C78 12 90 34 90 58 C90 80 74 90 50 90 C26 90 10 80 10 58 C10 34 22 12 50 12Z" fill="var(--mascot)" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="2.5"/>
    <ellipse cx="34" cy="28" rx="9" ry="5" fill="#fff" opacity=".45" transform="rotate(-25 34 28)"/>
    <circle cx="28" cy="63" r="5" fill="#ff7a93" opacity=".45"/><circle cx="72" cy="63" r="5" fill="#ff7a93" opacity=".45"/>
    ${EYES[m.eyes]}${MOUTH[m.mouth]}
    ${m.q ? '<text class="qmark" x="74" y="12" font-size="30" font-weight="700" fill="var(--a1)" font-family="var(--font-display)">?</text>' : ""}
    ${m.steam ? '<path class="steam" d="M84 22 l8 -8 M90 32 l11 -3 M76 16 l2 -11" stroke="var(--a1)" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"/>' : ""}
    ${m.drop ? '<path class="drop" d="M80 26 q-5 8 0 11 q5 -3 0 -11Z" fill="#6ec3ff" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="1.5"/>' : ""}
  </svg>`;
};

const setMood = (el, mood) => {
  if (el == null || el.dataset.cur === mood) {
    return;
  }

  el.dataset.cur = mood;
  el.innerHTML = mascotSVG(mood);
};

const replay = (el, cls) => {
  el.classList.remove(cls);
  void el.offsetWidth;
  el.classList.add(cls);
};

const confetti = (container, x, y, count = 28) => {
  const colors = ["--a1", "--a2", "--a3", "--a4"];

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) {
    const c = document.createElement("div");
    c.className = "confetti";
    c.style.left = `${x}px`;
    c.style.top = `${y}px`;

    c.style.setProperty("--dx", `${rand(-220, 220)}px`);
    c.style.setProperty("--dy", `${rand(-200, 160)}px`);
    c.style.setProperty("--rot", `${rand(-540, 540)}deg`);
    container.appendChild(c);

/* ───────────── Track ───────────── */

const buildTrack = (track) => {
  const stops = track.dataset.stops.split("|");

  track.innerHTML = stops.map((label, i) => {
    const finish = track.hasAttribute("data-finish") && i === stops.length - 1;

    return `<div class="stop${finish ? " finish" : ""}" style="animation-delay: ${i * .18}s; z-index: ${stops.length - i}"><div class="dot"></div><span>${label}</span></div>`;
  }).join("") + '<div class="mascot rider" data-mood="happy"></div>';
};

const setTrack = (track, pos) => {
  const stops = $$(".stop", track);
  const rider = $(".rider", track);

  stops.forEach((s, i) => s.classList.toggle("lit", i <= pos));

  const target = stops[Math.max(pos, 0)];
  rider.style.left = `${target.offsetLeft + target.offsetWidth / 2}px`;
  rider.style.opacity = pos < 0 ? 0 : 1;
};

const redraw = (track) => replay(track, "draw");

/* ───────────── Slide hooks ───────────── */

let run = 0;
let visit = 0;

const typeInto = async (el, text, speed, token, clock = () => run) => {
  el.textContent = "";

  for (const ch of text) {
    if (token !== clock()) {
      return;
    }

    el.textContent += ch;
    await sleep(speed);
  }
};

const fmt = (n) => Math.round(n).toLocaleString("es-AR");

// Counts a number up (or down) into el; stops when the slide moves on
const countTo = async (el, from, to, ms, token, render = fmt) => {
  const t0 = Date.now();

  while (Date.now() - t0 < ms) {
    if (token !== run) {
      return;
    }

    const k = (Date.now() - t0) / ms;
    el.textContent = render(from + (to - from) * (1 - (1 - k) ** 3));
    await sleep(30);
  }

  el.textContent = render(to);
};

const highlight = (line, lang) => {
  const rules = (RULES[lang] || []).map(([re, cls]) => [new RegExp(re.source, "y"), cls]);
  let out = "";
  let i = 0;

  while (i < line.length) {
    let hit = null;

    for (const [re, cls] of rules) {
      re.lastIndex = i;
      const m = re.exec(line);

      if (m != null && m[0].length > 0) {
        hit = [m[0], cls];
        break;
      }
    }

    if (hit == null) {
      out += esc(line[i]);
      i += 1;
    } else {
      out += hit[1] == null ? esc(hit[0]) : `<span class="t-${hit[1]}">${esc(hit[0])}</span>`;
      i += hit[0].length;
    }
  }

  return out;
};

// Moves elements in the DOM and animates them from where they were to where they land
const flip = (els, mutate) => {
  const k = $("#deck").getBoundingClientRect().width / 1280;
  const before = new Map(els.map((e) => [e, e.getBoundingClientRect()]));

  mutate();

  els.forEach((e) => {
    const a = before.get(e);
    const b = e.getBoundingClientRect();
    const dx = (a.left - b.left) / k;
    const dy = (a.top - b.top) / k;

    if (dx === 0 && dy === 0) {
      return;
    }

    e.style.transition = "none";
    e.style.transform = `translate(${dx}px, ${dy}px)`;
    void e.offsetWidth;
    e.style.transition = "";
    e.style.transform = "";
  });
};

const validate = (el) => {
  const name = $(".vname", el).value;
  const desc = $(".vdesc", el).value;

  const rules = {
    len: name.length >= 1 && name.length <= 64,
    chars: name.length > 0 && /^[a-z0-9-]+$/.test(name),
    edge: name.length > 0 && !/^-|-$/.test(name),
    double: !name.includes("--"),
    dir: name === "verificar-api",
    desc: desc.trim().length >= 1 && desc.length <= 1024,
  };

  const soft = { when: /usar|cuando|cuándo/i.test(desc) && desc.trim().split(/\s+/).length >= 8 };

  Object.entries({ ...rules, ...soft }).forEach(([k, ok]) => {
    const r = $(`[data-rule="${k}"]`, el);
    r.classList.toggle("ok", ok);
    r.classList.toggle("no", !ok);
  });

  const hard = Object.values(rules).every(Boolean);

  $(".vname", el).classList.toggle("bad", !(rules.len && rules.chars && rules.edge && rules.double && rules.dir));
  $(".dcount", el).textContent = desc.length;

const walkSteps = async (track, token, walk) => {
  const rider = $(".rider", track);
  const finish = walk[walk.length - 1];

  await sleep(1600);

  while (token === visit) {
    for (let i = 0; i < walk.length; i += 1) {
      if (token !== visit) {
        return;
      }

      const pos = walk[i];
      const backNext = walk[i + 1] != null && walk[i + 1] < pos;
      const wentBack = i > 0 && pos < walk[i - 1];

      if (i > 0) {
        replay(rider, "jump");
      }

      setTrack(track, pos);
      setMood(rider, wentBack ? "sweat" : pos === finish ? "joy" : "happy");

      if (backNext) {
        await sleep(700);
        setMood(rider, "frustrated");
        await sleep(900);
      } else {
        await sleep(pos === finish ? 300 : 1100);
      }
    }

    if (token !== visit) {
      return;
    }

    setMood(rider, "wave");
    confetti(track, rider.offsetLeft, 20, 36);
    await sleep(2600);

    const data = [

      extra.act == null ? "" : `data-act="${extra.act}"`,

    return `<div class="${cls}" ${data}><span class="p">${CHAT_MARK[kind]}</span><span class="t"></span>${tag}</div>`;

    return;
  }

  for (const l of lines.filter((x) => Number(x.dataset.group) === current)) {
    if (token !== run) {
      return;
    }

    const typed = l.classList.contains("me") || l.classList.contains("cmd");

    if (typed) {
      $(".t", l).textContent = "";
    } else if (l.classList.contains("wait")) {
      $(".t", l).textContent = l.dataset.text;
    }

    l.classList.remove("hide");
    scroll();

    if (typed) {
      const speed = l.classList.contains("cmd") ? 14 : l.classList.contains("ans") ? 40 : 22;
      await typeInto($(".t", l), l.dataset.text, speed, token);
      await sleep(250);
    } else if (l.classList.contains("wait")) {
      const end = Date.now() + Number(l.dataset.ms);

      for (let f = 0; Date.now() < end; f += 1) {
        if (token !== run) {
          return;
        }

        $(".p", l).textContent = SPIN[f % SPIN.length];
        await sleep(80);
      }

      settleLine(l);
      await sleep(300);
    } else {
      await sleep(PAUSE[l.classList[1]] ?? 450);
    }

    if (token !== run) {
      return;
    }

    if (l.dataset.act != null) {
      await act(l.dataset.act, true);
      await sleep(400);
    }
  }
};

/* ───────────── Timer ───────────── */

let timerStart = null;
let timerTick = null;

const startTimer = (el) => {
  if (timerStart != null) {
    return;
  }

  timerStart = Date.now();
  clearInterval(timerTick);

  timerTick = setInterval(() => {
    const s = Math.floor((Date.now() - timerStart) / 1000);
    el.textContent = `⏱ ${String(Math.floor(s / 60)).padStart(2, "0")}:${String(s % 60).padStart(2, "0")}`;
  }, 250);
};

$(".timer")?.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
  timerStart = null;
  e.currentTarget.textContent = "⏱ 00:00";
  startTimer(e.currentTarget);
});

/* ───────────── Titles ───────────── */

// Titles stay on one line: shrink the ones that would overflow the slide width
const fitTitles = () => $$(".slide h2").forEach((h) => {
  h.style.fontSize = "";

  let size = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(h).fontSize);

  while (h.scrollWidth > h.clientWidth && size > 30) {
    size -= 2;
    h.style.fontSize = `${size}px`;
  }
});

/* ───────────── Navigation ───────────── */

const slides = $$(".slide");
let idx = 0;
let step = 0;

// Inside kurasu the deck runs in a sandboxed iframe: the web moves it with kurasu:go messages and owns the
// navigation, so the deck leaves the keys, the address bar and its own HUD alone.
const embedded = window.parent !== window;

const stepsOf = (s) => Number(s.dataset.steps || Math.max(0, ...$$("[data-step]", s).map((e) => Number(e.dataset.step))));

const show = (entered, forward) => {
  run += 1;

  if (entered) {
    visit += 1;
  }

  slides.forEach((s, i) => {
    s.classList.toggle("active", i === idx);
    s.classList.toggle("past", i < idx);
  });

  const slide = slides[idx];
  slide.dataset.step = step;
  $$("[data-step]", slide).forEach((e) => e.classList.toggle("on", Number(e.dataset.step) <= step));

  const hook = hooks[slide.dataset.id];

  if (hook != null) {
    hook(step, slide, { entered, forward });
  }

  $$(".code[data-marks]", slide).forEach((c) => markCode(c, step));

  $(".count").textContent = `${idx + 1} / ${slides.length}`;
  $(".stepdots").innerHTML = Array.from({ length: stepsOf(slide) }, (_, i) => `<i class="${i < step ? "on" : ""}"></i>`).join("");
  if (!embedded) {
    history.replaceState(null, "", `${location.search}#${idx + 1}${step > 0 ? `.${step}` : ""}`);
  }
};

const next = () => {
  if (step < stepsOf(slides[idx])) {
    step += 1;
    show(false, true);
  } else if (idx < slides.length - 1) {
    idx += 1;
    step = 0;
    show(true, true);
  }
};

const prev = () => {
  if (step > 0) {
    step -= 1;
    show(false, false);
  } else if (idx > 0) {
    idx -= 1;
    step = stepsOf(slides[idx]);
    show(true, false);
  }
};

document.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  if (embedded || e.target.closest("input, textarea") != null) {
    return;
  }

  if (["ArrowRight", " ", "PageDown", "Enter"].includes(e.key)) {
    e.preventDefault();
    next();
  } else if (["ArrowLeft", "PageUp", "Backspace"].includes(e.key)) {
    e.preventDefault();
    prev();
  } else if (e.key === "f" || e.key === "F") {
    document.fullscreenElement == null ? document.documentElement.requestFullscreen() : document.exitFullscreen();
  } else if (e.key === "h" || e.key === "H") {
    $("#hud").classList.toggle("hidden");
  }
});

const fit = () => {
  const k = Math.min(innerWidth / 1280, innerHeight / 720);
  $("#deck").style.transform = `translate(-50%, -50%) scale(${k})`;
};

addEventListener("resize", fit);

/* ───────────── Init ───────────── */

const slideById = (id) => $(`.slide[data-id="${id}"]`);

// Each deck carries a subset of the slides: wire only the ones that are there
const withSlide = (id, fn) => {
  const el = slideById(id);

  if (el != null) {
    fn(el);
  }
};

hooks.reveal = (step, el) => {
  planOn = true;
  callsShown = step >= 2;
  renderCalls(el);
};

withSlide("dondevive", (el) => $$(".schip", el).forEach((c, i) => {
  c.dataset.i = i;
  c.addEventListener("click", () => {
    if (sorted.has(c)) {
      sorted.delete(c);
    } else {
      sorted.add(c);
    }

    placeChips(el, true);
  });
}));

withSlide("presupuesto", buildBudget);
withSlide("noVa", buildWiki);
withSlide("nxm", (el) => buildNM($(".nm", el)));
withSlide("tresetapas", (el) => {
  $(".sgrid", el).innerHTML = SKILLS.map((s, i) => `<div class="sk">${s}<small>name + description</small>${i === 0 ? '<div class="res">📄 references/errores.md</div>' : ""}</div>`).join("");
});
$$(".achips b").forEach((b, i) => { b.style.transitionDelay = `${i * .08}s`; });
$$(".code").forEach(buildCode);

withSlide("capas", (el) => {
  $$(".seg2 button", el).forEach((b) => b.addEventListener("click", () => setTransport(el, b.dataset.tr)));
  setTransport(el, "stdio");
});

withSlide("discovery", (el) => $$(".discbar .seg2 button", el).forEach((b) => b.addEventListener("click", () => {
  discManual = b.dataset.mode;
  setDiscovery(el, discManual, true);
})));

withSlide("transforms", (el) => $$(".xfseg button", el).forEach((b) => b.addEventListener("click", () => {
  xfManual = b.dataset.xf;
  setTransform(el, xfManual);
})));

withSlide("exposure", (el) => $$(".exseg button", el).forEach((b) => b.addEventListener("click", () => setExposure(el, b.dataset.ex))));

withSlide("reveal", (el) => $(".pmode", el).addEventListener("click", () => {
  planOn = !planOn;
  callsShown = true;
  renderCalls(el);
}));

withSlide("frontmatter", (fm) => {
  $$(".vname, .vdesc", fm).forEach((i) => i.addEventListener("input", () => validate(fm)));
  $$(".vtry button", fm).forEach((b) => b.addEventListener("click", () => {
    $(".vname", fm).value = b.dataset.try;
    validate(fm);
  }));
});

$$(".track").forEach(buildTrack);
$$(".chat .feed").forEach(buildChat);
$$(".mascot").forEach((m) => setMood(m, m.dataset.mood));
fit();

fitTitles();

const [hashSlide, hashStep] = location.hash.slice(1).split(".").map(Number);
idx = Math.min(Math.max((hashSlide || 1) - 1, 0), slides.length - 1);
step = Math.min(hashStep || 0, stepsOf(slides[idx]));
show(true, step === 0);

document.fonts.ready.then(() => {
  fitTitles();
  show(false, false);
});

/* ───────────── kurasu ───────────── */

// kurasu counts slides and steps from 1 and gives a slide without inner steps one step, so the deck's
// step 0 is kurasu's step 1.
if (embedded) {
  $("#hud").classList.add("hidden");

  window.parent.postMessage({
    type: "kurasu:manifest",
    slides: slides.map((s) => ({ steps: stepsOf(s) + 1 })),
  }, "*");

  addEventListener("message", (e) => {
    const go = e.data;

    if (e.source !== window.parent || go?.type !== "kurasu:go" || !Number.isInteger(go.slide) || !Number.isInteger(go.step)) {
      return;
    }

    const nextIdx = Math.min(Math.max(go.slide - 1, 0), slides.length - 1);
    const nextStep = Math.min(Math.max(go.step - 1, 0), stepsOf(slides[nextIdx]));
    const forward = nextIdx > idx || (nextIdx === idx && nextStep >= step);
    const entered = nextIdx !== idx;

    if (!entered && nextStep === step) {
      return;
    }

    idx = nextIdx;
    step = nextStep;
    show(entered, forward);
  });
}
</script>
</body>
</html>

---
title: "Talk: Pi, the self-building agent"
type: talk
status: draft
duration: "~31 min"
audience: "Mixed audience"
date: 2026-06-25
added: 2026-06-17
---

# Pi — the self-building agent

> Talk ~30 min · Mixed audience

Pi is an open-source terminal coding agent with a radically minimalist philosophy: a tiny core of four tools — read, write, edit, and bash — a prompt of less than a thousand tokens, and almost no built-in features. But what it lacks out of the box it makes up for with extensibility: Pi can even read its own code and extend itself.

## Time budget

| Time | Block |
| ---- | ----- |
| 5 min | Hook — harnesses + what is Pi? + comparison |
| 4 min | Architecture, briefly |
| 3 min | Demo 1 — Add a mascot |
| 6 min | Demo 2 — A subagent |
| 5 min | Demo 3 — Pi on a web page |
| 2 min | Try it yourself |
| ~28 min | Content + 3 min Q&A |

## Structure

### 1. Hook — 5 min

Open with the concept of harnesses — the tooling structure that wraps an LLM — then show concrete examples, introduce Pi, and finally the side-by-side comparison that makes the audience *feel* the difference in philosophy.

**Slide: Harness diagram**

ASCII diagram in a terminal window showing the layers of a harness: Interface → Agent Loop → Tools/Memory/Context → LLM. The audience needs to understand that every AI product is an LLM wrapped in tooling before we can compare them.

**Slide: Harness examples**

Three floating windows with screenshots: ChatGPT (web chat), Lovable (vibecoding platform), Claude Code (terminal agent). Each is a different kind of harness — same LLM underneath, different tooling and interface.

**Slide: Coding agents landscape**

Three info-windows: Anthropic/Claude Code, OpenAI/Codex, and an "others" window listing Amp, Droid, Aider, Cline, Goose. Quick show of hands: who's used one?

**Slide: What is Pi?**

30 seconds on what a coding agent is, then Pi's thesis: four tools, sub-thousand-token prompt, any model, no MCP / no permissions / no plan mode. Screenshots of Pi running, multi-provider diagram, no-permissions diagram, tree sessions diagram. Credibility point: OpenClaw runs on Pi.

**Slide: VSCode vs Vim analogy**

Two floating windows side by side. VS Code: everything built-in. Vim: minimal, you build what you need. Claude Code is the VS Code of agents, Pi is the Vim.

**Slide: Feature comparison**

| | Claude Code | Pi |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Core tools** | 25+ (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep, LS, TaskCreate, Agent, Skill, EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode, EnterWorktree, ExitWorktree, AskUserQuestion, SendMessage, NotebookEdit, NotebookRun, Verify, UpdateConfig, schedule, loop…) | 4 (read, write, edit, bash) |
| **System prompt** | ~5,000+ tokens, changes every release | <1,000 tokens, barely changes |
| **Permissions** | Built-in system with modes (acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, plan) + hooks + allowlists | None — containerize if you need boundaries |
| **Plan mode** | Built-in (EnterPlanMode/ExitPlanMode tools) | Build it yourself (it's ~50 lines) |
| **Subagents** | Built-in (Explore, Plan, code-reviewer, general-purpose) | Build it yourself (that's the demo) |
| **MCP** | Built-in client + servers | Not included — extensions cover the same ground |
| **Memory** | Built-in auto-memory (4 types: user, feedback, project, reference) | Build it yourself |
| **Worktrees** | Built-in (EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree tools) | Bash is right there |
| **Session branching** | Linear sessions | Tree-based with fork/branch/merge in a single file |
| **Skills** | Built-in marketplace + system | SKILL.md files, progressive disclosure |
| **Extensibility** | MCP + hooks + skills | Extensions (full event lifecycle, can register tools/commands/shortcuts/themes/providers) |
| **Models** | Anthropic only | Any provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, local…) |

**The punchline**: Claude Code is a great product. But every built-in feature is an opinion forced on you, a thing that changes between releases, a maintenance burden for the team. Pi's bet is different: give the agent a minimal core and let it build what it needs — including reading its own source code and writing its own extensions.

**Optional visual**: Show a diff of Claude Code's system prompt between two recent versions to illustrate churn. The prompt you don't control is a liability.

### 2. Architecture, briefly — 4 min

Goal: give the audience just enough mental model to understand the demos. Don't go deep — point at the shape of things.

**The four packages** (one slide — mention, don't dwell):

```
┌─────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────┐
│  pi-ai              │───▶│  pi-agent-core       │───▶│  pi-coding-agent     │───▶│  pi-tui              │
│  (Unified LLM API:  │    │  (Agent loop, event  │    │  (CLI + TUI +        │    │  (Terminal UI:       │
│   OpenAI, Anthropic,│    │   bus, tool exec)    │    │   sessions, modes)   │    │   editor, themes,    │
│   Google, local…)   │    │                      │    │                      │    │   keybindings)       │
└─────────────────────┘    └──────────────────────┘    └──────────────────────┘    └──────────────────────┘
```

Packages are layered inside-out: the unified LLM API at the base, the generic agent loop on top, the coding-specific layer, and the terminal UI at the surface. Use only the layers you need.



**The agent loop** (how a turn works):

```
User message
     │
     ▼
before_agent_start  ◀── extensions: modify system prompt, inject messages
     │
     ▼
 ┌─▶ tool_call      ◀── extensions: intercept, modify args, block
 │      │
 │      ▼
 │  tool_result     ◀── extensions: modify results
 │      │
 └──────┘            (agent loops until done)
     │
     ▼
message_end         ◀── extensions: modify the final message
```

**Extension points** — what extensions can register (one slide):

- **Tools** — LLM-callable functions (this is how you build subagents)
- **Commands** — slash commands (`/my-command`)
- **Skills** — on-demand capability packages (SKILL.md with progressive disclosure: only descriptions live in the prompt, full instructions load when the agent reads the file)
- **Shortcuts** — keyboard bindings
- **Flags** — CLI flags
- **Themes** — UI themes
- **Providers** — custom LLM providers
- **Message renderers** — custom UI for message types

**Three modes of running Pi** (sets up Demo 3):

- **Interactive** — the terminal TUI you'll see in Demos 1 and 2
- **Print mode** — headless one-shot execution for CI/pipelines
- **SDK** — embed pi in your own application (a web server, a desktop app, anything). This is what Demo 3 uses.

**Session tree** (unique to Pi — worth a mention):

Sessions aren't linear — they're a tree. Every message can branch, fork, or merge. The entire tree lives in a single JSONL file. You can navigate to any point, start a branch, and explore alternatives without losing history.

### 3. Demo 1 — Add a mascot — 3 min

The smallest possible win. Goal: show the loop and that adding a capability is cheap and readable. Keep it light and fun.

Idea: write a tiny extension that registers a `/mascot` command that prints a random ASCII goat. Shows: extensions are just TS files, `registerCommand` is the only API you need.

### 4. Demo 2 — A subagent — 6 min

The main event. Three pre-built commits, each building on the last:

**Commit 1 — One foreground subagent**

- A single `delegate` tool that opens a headless agent session, gives it a task, and returns the result
- Show the main agent delegating a focused task (e.g., "find all functions that do X") and receiving the answer
- Key insight: a subagent is just `pi.on("before_agent_start") + session.prompt()` — no magic

**Commit 2 — Background subagents**

- The delegate tool now returns immediately with a task handle instead of blocking — the subagent runs headlessly in the background
- Show the main agent dispatching a research task and then *immediately continuing* with other work (reading a file, planning) while the subagent runs
- When the subagent finishes, its result is injected back into the main agent's next turn as a message
- Key insight: pi's session model is non-blocking — you open a session, fire `session.prompt()`, and the result can be delivered asynchronously. This is fundamentally different from a synchronous tool call that blocks the main loop

**Commit 3 — Complex subagent pipelines**

- Show a pipeline: subagent A researches → subagent B implements → subagent C reviews
- Compare to Claude Code's "dynamic workflows" — same concept, but you built it in ~100 lines instead of it being a platform feature. Bonus: yours can run tasks in the background while the main agent keeps working, which Claude Code's subagent tool calls can't do (they block until completion)
- This is the moment that sells the philosophy: "you just built what Claude Code ships as a feature, and yours is exactly tailored to your workflow"

Present as git checkpoints: `git checkout commit-1` → show it working → `git checkout commit-2` → show the diff → etc. Don't type live.

### 5. Demo 3 — Pi in the browser — 5 min

The closer: "it's not just a terminal toy, it's not even just a server thing." The entire pi agent loop runs **client-side in the browser** — no backend, no server.

**The layout**:

```
┌─────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
│                     │                          │
│   Chat panel        │   Live preview           │
│   (left)            │   (right)                │
│                     │                          │
│   Type messages     │   HTML rendered from     │
│   to the agent      │   virtual files in an    │
│                     │   iframe / shadow DOM     │
│                     │                          │
│   See tool calls    │                          │
│   (write, edit)     │   The agent writes       │
│                     │   virtual files (HTML,    │
│                     │   CSS, JS) in memory and   │
│                     │   the panel re-renders    │
│                     │   when they change        │
│                     │                          │
└─────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┘
```

**How it works**:

- pi-ai + pi-agent-core are bundled for the browser (both packages have `/base` entry points and pass browser smoke tests)
- A virtual filesystem replaces the built-in tools: `write` and `edit` write to in-memory files instead of disk
- LLM calls go directly to the provider API via `fetch` (works in browser)
- The right panel reads the virtual filesystem and renders the HTML whenever a file changes
- The left panel shows tool calls ("writing index.html…", "editing styles.css…") in real time

**Custom browser tools**:

- `write(path, content)` — write to virtual filesystem in memory
- `edit(path, edits)` — edit virtual files
- `read(path)` — read virtual files
- No bash — replaced by browser-specific tools if needed

**The moment**: Ask the agent "build me a landing page for a coffee shop" and watch it write virtual files on the left while the page assembles itself on the right. The entire agent, tools, and rendering are running client-side. No server, no backend.

Have this pre-built and ready to show. The wow factor: the agent is running in the browser, the tools are in-memory, and the page materializes in real time.

### 6. Try it yourself — 2 min

The reward slide. Install command, "your first session" in one line, links to repo / docs / npm. Say exactly what to try first.

```
npm install -g @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent
pi
```

- Repo: [github.com/earendil-works/pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi)
- Docs: [pi.dev/docs](https://pi.dev/docs)
- npm: `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`

### 7. Q&A — 3 min

Reserved for the end.

## Prep checklist

- [ ] Harness diagram slide (hook)
- [ ] Harness examples screenshots: ChatGPT, Lovable, Claude Code
- [ ] Comparison slide (hook)
- [ ] Architecture diagrams (packages + agent loop + extension points + modes)
- [ ] Demo 1: mascot extension (pre-built, test it works)
- [ ] Demo 2: 3 subagent commits (pre-built, test each checkpoint)
- [ ] Demo 3: web app with chat + live preview (pre-built, ready to show)
- [ ] Claude Code prompt diff visual (optional, for hook)
- [ ] Backup recordings of each demo (20-30 sec clips)
- [ ] Final slide with install command

## Tips for this format

- Live demos are the main risk in 30 minutes. Use git checkpoints for Demo 2, not live typing.
- A mixed audience loses focus during long typing stretches. Narrate the intent ("I'm asking it to build a subagent") instead of reading the code aloud.
- Always close with a call to action: the last slide should be how to install and run Pi in under a minute. The goal is they leave wanting to try it.

## Links

- Repo: [github.com/earendil-works/pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi)
- npm: `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`
- Web: [pi.dev](https://pi.dev)
- Docs: [pi.dev/docs](https://pi.dev/docs/latest)

# Extensiones: lifecycle

## Content
- Ventana única con diagrama de flujo que se construye paso a paso
- Los boxes representan los momentos del flujo, las flechas muestran el paso entre ellos
- Los puntos de extensión se indican con flechas/etiquetas pequeñas apuntando a las conexiones entre boxes

Parte 1 — Session lifecycle (vista general):
- [session_start] → [resources_discover] → [agent loop] (box destacado, sin detalle) → [session_shutdown]

Parte 2 — Zoom in al agent loop, se recorre paso a paso:
- [input] → [before_agent_start] → [turn_start] → [context] → [LLM call] → [tool_execution_start] → [tool_call] → [tool_result] → [tool_execution_end] → [turn_end] → [agent_end]
- Flechas de extensión señalando: entre input y before_agent_start (transform), sobre tool_call (block/modify), sobre tool_result (modify), sobre context (modify messages), sobre before_agent_start (inject/modify prompt)

Parte 3 — Zoom out, vuelta a session lifecycle:
- [session_shutdown] con flechas de extensión hacia: [session_before_switch] [session_before_fork] [session_before_compact] [session_before_tree]

Texto visible en cada box (una línea por momento):
- session_start: Se crea la sesión y arranca todo.
- resources_discover: Se descubren extensiones, skills y servidores MCP.
- agent loop: El turno del agente se ejecuta como un loop, paso a paso.
- input: Llega el mensaje del usuario.
- before_agent_start (EXTENSION POINT): Inyectar o modificar el system prompt antes de arrancar.
- turn_start: Comienza un turno dentro del loop.
- context (EXTENSION POINT): Modificar los mensajes que se mandan al LLM.
- LLM call: Se llama al modelo.
- tool_execution_start: Empieza la ejecución de herramientas.
- tool_call (EXTENSION POINT): Bloquear o modificar los argumentos de la tool (permisos).
- tool_result (EXTENSION POINT): Modificar el resultado que recibe el LLM.
- tool_execution_end: Termina la ejecución de herramientas.
- turn_end: Termina el turno; el loop sigue hasta que el agente esté listo.
- agent_end: El agente terminó su trabajo.
- session_shutdown: Se cierra la sesión — y hay más hooks para interceptar (before_switch, before_fork, before_compact, before_tree).

Línea resumen (abajo del diagrama): todos los eventos son escuchables — `pi.on(evento, (e, ctx) => …)` → bloquear · modificar · inyectar, y mostrar UI propia con `ctx.ui` (notify · confirm · select · custom).

## Animation
1. Aparece [session_start]
2. Flecha hacia [resources_discover]
3. Flecha hacia [agent loop] (box destacado)
4. Flecha hacia [session_shutdown]
5. Zoom in sobre [agent loop]
6. Aparece [input], flecha hacia [before_agent_start]
7. Flecha hacia [turn_start], flecha hacia [context], flecha hacia [LLM call]
8. Flecha hacia [tool_execution_start], flecha hacia [tool_call] — flecha de extensión sobre tool_call
9. Flecha hacia [tool_result] — flecha de extensión sobre tool_result
10. Flecha hacia [tool_execution_end], flecha hacia [turn_end], flecha hacia [agent_end]
11. Zoom out, vuelta a session lifecycle
12. Aparecen [session_before_switch] [session_before_fork] [session_before_compact] [session_before_tree] con flechas desde session_shutdown

## Speaker Notes
- Arranca con session_start y resources_discover
- Zoom in al loop — boxes son los momentos, flechas son los hooks
- tool_call: bloquear o modificar (ej: permisos)
- tool_result: modificar lo que el LLM recibe
- context: modificar mensajes antes del LLM
- before_agent_start: inyectar contexto, modificar system prompt
- Zoom out — más hooks de sesión
- switch, fork, compact, tree — todo interceptable
- Todo sin tocar el código de Pi

# Pi — the self-building agent

> Talk ~30 min · Mixed audience

Pi is an open-source terminal coding agent with a radically minimalist philosophy: a tiny core of four tools — read, write, edit, and bash — a prompt of less than a thousand tokens, and almost no built-in features. But what it lacks out of the box it makes up for with extensibility: Pi can even read its own code and extend itself.

## Time budget

| Time | Block |
| ---- | ----- |
| 5 min | Hook — harnesses + what is Pi? + comparison |
| 4 min | Architecture, briefly |
| 3 min | Demo 1 — Add a mascot |
| 6 min | Demo 2 — A subagent |
| 5 min | Demo 3 — Pi on a web page |
| 2 min | Try it yourself |
| ~28 min | Content + 3 min Q&A |

## Structure

### 1. Hook — 5 min

Open with the concept of harnesses — the tooling structure that wraps an LLM — then show concrete examples, introduce Pi, and finally the side-by-side comparison that makes the audience *feel* the difference in philosophy.

**Slide: Harness diagram**

ASCII diagram in a terminal window showing the layers of a harness: Interface → Agent Loop → Tools/Memory/Context → LLM. The audience needs to understand that every AI product is an LLM wrapped in tooling before we can compare them.

**Slide: Harness examples**

Three floating windows with screenshots: ChatGPT (web chat), Lovable (vibecoding platform), Claude Code (terminal agent). Each is a different kind of harness — same LLM underneath, different tooling and interface.

**Slide: Coding agents landscape**

Three info-windows: Anthropic/Claude Code, OpenAI/Codex, and an "others" window listing Amp, Droid, Aider, Cline, Goose. Quick show of hands: who's used one?

**Slide: What is Pi?**

30 seconds on what a coding agent is, then Pi's thesis: four tools, sub-thousand-token prompt, any model, no MCP / no permissions / no plan mode. Screenshots of Pi running, multi-provider diagram, no-permissions diagram, tree sessions diagram. Credibility point: OpenClaw runs on Pi.

**Slide: VSCode vs Vim analogy**

Two floating windows side by side. VS Code: everything built-in. Vim: minimal, you build what you need. Claude Code is the VS Code of agents, Pi is the Vim.

**Slide: Feature comparison**

| | Claude Code | Pi |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Core tools** | 25+ (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep, LS, TaskCreate, Agent, Skill, EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode, EnterWorktree, ExitWorktree, AskUserQuestion, SendMessage, NotebookEdit, NotebookRun, Verify, UpdateConfig, schedule, loop…) | 4 (read, write, edit, bash) |
| **System prompt** | ~5,000+ tokens, changes every release | <1,000 tokens, barely changes |
| **Permissions** | Built-in system with modes (acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, plan) + hooks + allowlists | None — containerize if you need boundaries |
| **Plan mode** | Built-in (EnterPlanMode/ExitPlanMode tools) | Build it yourself (it's ~50 lines) |
| **Subagents** | Built-in (Explore, Plan, code-reviewer, general-purpose) | Build it yourself (that's the demo) |
| **MCP** | Built-in client + servers | Not included — extensions cover the same ground |
| **Memory** | Built-in auto-memory (4 types: user, feedback, project, reference) | Build it yourself |
| **Worktrees** | Built-in (EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree tools) | Bash is right there |
| **Session branching** | Linear sessions | Tree-based with fork/branch/merge in a single file |
| **Skills** | Built-in marketplace + system | SKILL.md files, progressive disclosure |
| **Extensibility** | MCP + hooks + skills | Extensions (full event lifecycle, can register tools/commands/shortcuts/themes/providers) |
| **Models** | Anthropic only | Any provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, local…) |

**The punchline**: Claude Code is a great product. But every built-in feature is an opinion forced on you, a thing that changes between releases, a maintenance burden for the team. Pi's bet is different: give the agent a minimal core and let it build what it needs — including reading its own source code and writing its own extensions.

**Optional visual**: Show a diff of Claude Code's system prompt between two recent versions to illustrate churn. The prompt you don't control is a liability.

### 2. Architecture, briefly — 4 min

Goal: give the audience just enough mental model to understand the demos. Don't go deep — point at the shape of things.

**The four packages** (one slide — mention, don't dwell):

```
┌─────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────┐
│  pi-ai              │───▶│  pi-agent-core       │───▶│  pi-coding-agent     │───▶│  pi-tui              │
│  (Unified LLM API:  │    │  (Agent loop, event  │    │  (CLI + TUI +        │    │  (Terminal UI:       │
│   OpenAI, Anthropic,│    │   bus, tool exec)    │    │   sessions, modes)   │    │   editor, themes,    │
│   Google, local…)   │    │                      │    │                      │    │   keybindings)       │
└─────────────────────┘    └──────────────────────┘    └──────────────────────┘    └──────────────────────┘
```

Packages are layered inside-out: the unified LLM API at the base, the generic agent loop on top, the coding-specific layer, and the terminal UI at the surface. Use only the layers you need.



**The agent loop** (how a turn works):

```
User message
     │
     ▼
before_agent_start  ◀── extensions: modify system prompt, inject messages
     │
     ▼
 ┌─▶ tool_call      ◀── extensions: intercept, modify args, block
 │      │
 │      ▼
 │  tool_result     ◀── extensions: modify results
 │      │
 └──────┘            (agent loops until done)
     │
     ▼
message_end         ◀── extensions: modify the final message
```

**Extension points** — what extensions can register (one slide):

- **Tools** — LLM-callable functions (this is how you build subagents)
- **Commands** — slash commands (`/my-command`)
- **Skills** — on-demand capability packages (SKILL.md with progressive disclosure: only descriptions live in the prompt, full instructions load when the agent reads the file)
- **Shortcuts** — keyboard bindings
- **Flags** — CLI flags
- **Themes** — UI themes
- **Providers** — custom LLM providers
- **Message renderers** — custom UI for message types

**Three modes of running Pi** (sets up Demo 3):

- **Interactive** — the terminal TUI you'll see in Demos 1 and 2
- **Print mode** — headless one-shot execution for CI/pipelines
- **SDK** — embed pi in your own application (a web server, a desktop app, anything). This is what Demo 3 uses.

**Session tree** (unique to Pi — worth a mention):

Sessions aren't linear — they're a tree. Every message can branch, fork, or merge. The entire tree lives in a single JSONL file. You can navigate to any point, start a branch, and explore alternatives without losing history.

### 3. Demo 1 — Add a mascot — 3 min

The smallest possible win. Goal: show the loop and that adding a capability is cheap and readable. Keep it light and fun.

Idea: write a tiny extension that registers a `/mascot` command that prints a random ASCII goat. Shows: extensions are just TS files, `registerCommand` is the only API you need.

### 4. Demo 2 — A subagent — 6 min

The main event. Three pre-built commits, each building on the last:

**Commit 1 — One foreground subagent**

- A single `delegate` tool that opens a headless agent session, gives it a task, and returns the result
- Show the main agent delegating a focused task (e.g., "find all functions that do X") and receiving the answer
- Key insight: a subagent is just `pi.on("before_agent_start") + session.prompt()` — no magic

**Commit 2 — Background subagents**

- The delegate tool now returns immediately with a task handle instead of blocking — the subagent runs headlessly in the background
- Show the main agent dispatching a research task and then *immediately continuing* with other work (reading a file, planning) while the subagent runs
- When the subagent finishes, its result is injected back into the main agent's next turn as a message
- Key insight: pi's session model is non-blocking — you open a session, fire `session.prompt()`, and the result can be delivered asynchronously. This is fundamentally different from a synchronous tool call that blocks the main loop

**Commit 3 — Complex subagent pipelines**

- Show a pipeline: subagent A researches → subagent B implements → subagent C reviews
- Compare to Claude Code's "dynamic workflows" — same concept, but you built it in ~100 lines instead of it being a platform feature. Bonus: yours can run tasks in the background while the main agent keeps working, which Claude Code's subagent tool calls can't do (they block until completion)
- This is the moment that sells the philosophy: "you just built what Claude Code ships as a feature, and yours is exactly tailored to your workflow"

Present as git checkpoints: `git checkout commit-1` → show it working → `git checkout commit-2` → show the diff → etc. Don't type live.

### 5. Demo 3 — Pi in the browser — 5 min

The closer: "it's not just a terminal toy, it's not even just a server thing." The entire pi agent loop runs **client-side in the browser** — no backend, no server.

**The layout**:

```
┌─────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
│                     │                          │
│   Chat panel        │   Live preview           │
│   (left)            │   (right)                │
│                     │                          │
│   Type messages     │   HTML rendered from     │
│   to the agent      │   virtual files in an    │
│                     │   iframe / shadow DOM     │
│                     │                          │
│   See tool calls    │                          │
│   (write, edit)     │   The agent writes       │
│                     │   virtual files (HTML,    │
│                     │   CSS, JS) in memory and   │
│                     │   the panel re-renders    │
│                     │   when they change        │
│                     │                          │
└─────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┘
```

**How it works**:

- pi-ai + pi-agent-core are bundled for the browser (both packages have `/base` entry points and pass browser smoke tests)
- A virtual filesystem replaces the built-in tools: `write` and `edit` write to in-memory files instead of disk
- LLM calls go directly to the provider API via `fetch` (works in browser)
- The right panel reads the virtual filesystem and renders the HTML whenever a file changes
- The left panel shows tool calls ("writing index.html…", "editing styles.css…") in real time

**Custom browser tools**:

- `write(path, content)` — write to virtual filesystem in memory
- `edit(path, edits)` — edit virtual files
- `read(path)` — read virtual files
- No bash — replaced by browser-specific tools if needed

**The moment**: Ask the agent "build me a landing page for a coffee shop" and watch it write virtual files on the left while the page assembles itself on the right. The entire agent, tools, and rendering are running client-side. No server, no backend.

Have this pre-built and ready to show. The wow factor: the agent is running in the browser, the tools are in-memory, and the page materializes in real time.

### 6. Try it yourself — 2 min

The reward slide. Install command, "your first session" in one line, links to repo / docs / npm. Say exactly what to try first.

```
npm install -g @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent
pi
```

- Repo: [github.com/earendil-works/pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi)
- Docs: [pi.dev/docs](https://pi.dev/docs)
- npm: `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`

### 7. Q&A — 3 min

Reserved for the end.

## Prep checklist

- [ ] Harness diagram slide (hook)
- [ ] Harness examples screenshots: ChatGPT, Lovable, Claude Code
- [ ] Comparison slide (hook)
- [ ] Architecture diagrams (packages + agent loop + extension points + modes)
- [ ] Demo 1: mascot extension (pre-built, test it works)
- [ ] Demo 2: 3 subagent commits (pre-built, test each checkpoint)
- [ ] Demo 3: web app with chat + live preview (pre-built, ready to show)
- [ ] Claude Code prompt diff visual (optional, for hook)
- [ ] Backup recordings of each demo (20-30 sec clips)

## Tips for this format

- Live demos are the main risk in 30 minutes. Use git checkpoints for Demo 2, not live typing.
- A mixed audience loses focus during long typing stretches. Narrate the intent ("I'm asking it to build a subagent") instead of reading the code aloud.
- Always close with a call to action: the last slide should be how to install and run Pi in under a minute. The goal is they leave wanting to try it.
