     1	# tentacles
     2	
     3	tentacles runs coding-agent sessions remotely, on pi-durable, over infrastructure behind provider-neutral contracts, with Cloudflare as the first setup. A plugin for pi and Claude Code lets a local agent spawn, steer, question and collect those remote sessions the way it does local subagents.
     4	
     5	## Docs
     6	
     7	- **Docs**: `docs/`. Read its `README.md` before adding, editing, renaming or moving anything under it.
     8	- **Folders**: `technical-design/`, the shape of the system and how each part works; `product-design/`, what tentacles is and what it is like to use.
     9	- **Checks**: `pnpm check` · `pnpm test`
    10	
    11	### When adding something
    12	
    13	- A change to how a part of the system works → a note in `docs/technical-design/`
    14	- A change to what the parent agent or the person using tentacles sees or does → a note in `docs/product-design/`
    15	- A rule every change has to respect → a line in `docs/invariants.md`

docs/technical-design/runtime-components.md:
     1	---
     2	title: "Runtime components"
     3	summary: "The roles tentacles' shared logic reaches through provider-neutral contracts, what crosses between them, and how a provider plugs its implementation in."
     4	created: "2026-11-09"
     5	---
     6	
     7	# Runtime components
     8	
     9	## 🔭 Overview
    10	
    11	tentacles runs as a set of roles: an API entry that is the only way in, a registry for everything that spans sessions, one session object per session running pi-durable, a workspace per session that holds the agent's files and runs its commands, model providers, a codemode sandbox, a managed browser for previews and a daily scheduler. tentacles' shared logic reaches each role through a contract, and a provider fills every contract, so another setup can replace the infrastructure without changing the plugin. No container holds a credential: the provider adds the tokens to requests outside the container. Cloudflare is the first provider; [deploy](providers/cloudflare/deploy.md) covers how it fills each role.
    12	
    13	## 🏗️ Architecture
    14	
    15	```mermaid
    16	flowchart LR
    17	    subgraph dev["Developer machine"]
    18	        Plugin@{ shape: stadium, label: "tentacles plugin<br/>helper" }
    19	    end
    20	    subgraph prov["A provider"]
    21	        Entry@{ shape: rect, label: "API entry<br/>API key, routes,<br/>preview route" }
    22	        Registry@{ shape: rect, label: "Registry<br/>sessions per parent,<br/>each session's preview" }
    23	        Session@{ shape: rect, label: "Session object<br/>pi-durable Harness, storage,<br/>socket, wake-up timer" }
    24	        Workspace@{ shape: rect, label: "Workspace<br/>files, isolate shell,<br/>container" }
    25	        Models@{ shape: rect, label: "Model providers" }
    26	        Codemode@{ shape: rect, label: "Codemode sandbox" }
    27	        Browser@{ shape: rect, label: "Browser" }
    28	        Cron@{ shape: rect, label: "Scheduler" }
    29	    end
    30	    GitHub@{ shape: cloud, label: "GitHub" }
    31	
    32	    Plugin -->|"requests, socket"| Entry
    33	    Entry -->|"listings, preview lookups"| Registry
    34	    Entry -->|"session requests by id,<br/>preview requests"| Session
    35	    Session -->|"status changes,<br/>preview opened and cleared"| Registry
    36	    Session -->|"create at spawn,<br/>tool calls, forward"| Workspace
    37	    Session -->|"model calls"| Models
    38	    Session -->|"codemode scripts"| Codemode
    39	    Session -->|"open and close<br/>the preview's browser"| Browser
    40	    Workspace -->|"clone, fetch, push,<br/>token added outside the container"| GitHub
    41	    Browser -->|"preview URL"| Entry
    42	    Cron -->|"daily cleanup"| Registry
    43	
    44	    classDef grey fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#4b5563,color:#1f2937
    45	    classDef blue fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1f2937
    46	    classDef green fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#1f2937
    47	    classDef violet fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#1f2937
    48	    class Plugin grey
    49	    class Entry blue
    50	    class Registry,Session,Workspace,Models,Codemode,Browser,Cron green
    51	    class GitHub violet
    52	```
    53	
    54	The **API entry** checks the API key on every plugin request and socket, then routes it: listings and preview lookups go to the registry, and everything about one session goes to that session's object by its id. Its preview route turns a preview URL's token into a session and a port and hands the request to the session object. [worker-api](worker-api.md) lists its calls and the session socket.
    55	
    56	The **registry** is the one store that spans sessions: an entry per session with its name, its parent, its status, the time its last run stopped, its settings and skill and agent names, and the session's preview while one is open. [sessions](sessions.md) lists the fields of each entry.
    57	
    58	The **session object** is one live instance per session, keyed by its session id. It runs pi-durable's Harness over its own storage, with the question tool and the wake-up timer that resumes a run after an eviction. It creates the session's workspace at spawn and installs the tools the workspace returns, holds the parent's socket, sends each model call to the provider the settings name, and opens and closes the preview's browser. It never writes the status ahead of the run: it watches pi-durable's state and tells the registry each time the derived status changes.
    59	
    60	The **workspace** holds the session's files under `/workspace` and runs the agent's commands on the cheapest backend that can run them, the isolate shell or the container. Its git reaches GitHub with the token added outside the container. [workspace](workspace.md) covers its contract, setup and tools.
    61	
    62	The **model providers**, the **codemode sandbox**, the **browser** and the **scheduler** each answer one kind of call: a model call, a codemode script, opening or closing the preview's browser, and firing the daily cleanup job.
    63	
    64	## 🔌 Provider-neutral roles
    65	
    66	Each component above plays a role that any provider has to fill. Several roles already sit behind an interface the pi libraries define: pi-durable takes its storage, its wake-up timer and its tools from the host, and pi-ai reaches models through providers. The plugin talks only to the Worker API and the session socket, so it does not change with the provider.
    67	
    68	| Role | Contract | What the common logic asks it | Interface it builds on |
    69	|---|---|---|---|
    70	| Session host: one live instance per session, revived on demand | `SessionHost` | reach a session by id and run one of its operations: create, prompt, answer, close, messages, status, connect a socket, forward a preview request, delete | pi-durable's Harness opens over any host |
    71	| Session storage | `SessionStorage` | pi-durable's storage for one session | pi-durable's storage adapter |
    72	| Wake-up timer | `WakeTimer` | set or clear the one timer that resumes a run after an eviction | pi-durable's `onWake`; the host writes the timer |
    73	| Parent socket | `ParentChannel` | send the session state to every socket the parent holds open | none |
    74	| Registry of sessions and their preview | `RegistryStore` | add an entry, record a status and the time a run stops, list one parent's sessions, open a preview and return its token, resolve and clear a preview, remove an entry, find the sessions stopped before a given time | none |
    75	| Workspace: the session's files and the backends that run its commands | `Workspace` | `create(init)`: set up the workspace at spawn from the repository URL or none, the git identity, the container's size and image, and the skills and context archives, and return the tools the harness installs, each with its replay policy and its own execute; `forward`: hand a preview request to a port and return the app's answer, 502 when nothing listens | pi-durable's tool registrations |
    76	| Browser | `Browser` | open a browser for the session's preview, returning the CDP URL agent-browser connects to, and close it | agent-browser speaks CDP to any URL |
    77	| Preview routing | `PreviewRouter` | the public URL a preview token is served on | none |
    78	| Models | `ModelProviders` | every model provider the session's settings can name | pi-ai providers |
    79	| Daily cleanup | `Scheduler` | run a job once a day | none |
    80	| Codemode sandbox | `CodeSandbox` | the sandbox codemode scripts run in | pi-durable's codemode sandbox |
    81	| API entry: auth and routing | none, the Worker API itself | nothing: the API entry runs the API handlers | [worker-api](worker-api.md) |
    82	
    83	A provider implements every contract in the table. The common logic (the API handlers, the session logic with its lifecycle and deletion, the preview handler, the cleanup job and the remote agent's tools other than the workspace's) and the pi libraries are the same for every provider. A deploy uses one provider for every role, and a variable read by the deploy picks the provider. [providers](providers/README.md) lists the providers.
    84	
    85	```mermaid
    86	flowchart LR
    87	    subgraph setup["A provider"]
    88	        In@{ shape: rect, label: "Entry points<br/>Worker fetch, session object,<br/>preview route, cron, alarm" }
    89	        Impl@{ shape: rect, label: "One implementation<br/>per contract" }
    90	    end
    91	    subgraph core["Common logic"]
    92	        Logic@{ shape: rect, label: "API handlers, session logic,<br/>preview handler, cleanup job,<br/>the remote agent's tools" }
    93	        Pi@{ shape: hex, label: "pi libraries<br/>pi-durable, pi-ai" }
    94	        Logic --> Pi
    95	    end
    96	    Contracts@{ shape: braces, label: "The contracts" }
    97	    In -->|"call"| Logic
    98	    Logic -->|"reaches each role through"| Contracts
    99	    Impl -.->|"implements"| Contracts
   100	    classDef blue fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1f2937
   101	    classDef green fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#1f2937
   102	    classDef amber fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#1f2937
   103	    classDef payload stroke:#d97706
   104	    class Logic blue
   105	    class Pi amber
   106	    class Contracts payload
   107	    class In,Impl green
   108	```
   109	
   110	The calls run both ways. The provider receives every outside event (the API requests, the preview route, the cron trigger and the alarm) and calls the common logic. Each session object hosts its session's logic. The common logic calls the provider only through the contracts. `SessionHost` goes both ways: the provider hosts each session, and the common logic reaches a session by its id through it.
   111	
   112	> [!TIP] Considered and not taken: roles from different providers in one deploy
   113	> On Cloudflare one session object fills five roles (`SessionHost`, `SessionStorage`, `WakeTimer`, `ParentChannel`, and `Workspace`, whose files and container live in it), so a role taken from another provider would have to split that object apart. One provider per deploy keeps each provider's parts together.
   114	
   115	> [!NOTE] Why credentials are not a contract
   116	> Keeping credentials out of containers is how a provider implements `Workspace` and `ModelProviders`: it adds the tokens to requests outside the container, in its git client and at egress. Each provider keeps them out in its own way, so the shared logic never sees a credential and has nothing to ask a contract for.
   117	
   118	> [!NOTE] Where the contracts come from
   119	> The contracts follow the roles and the host interfaces pi already defines, not any infrastructure library. A role pi already abstracts, such as storage, the wake-up timer or the agent's tools, takes pi's interface as its contract's shape.
   120	
   121	## 🧩 Provider contracts
   122	
   123	Each contract in the table under 🔌 Provider-neutral roles is an Effect service, and each provider supplies its implementation as a Layer. The common logic asks for a contract and never names a provider.
   124	
   125	Shapes the API defines, such as the session state, pass through the contracts with the types the API declares, so a contract and the API cannot disagree.
   126	
   127	A member that can fail declares a tagged error with a message: `Workspace.create` fails with the setup error, `Browser.open` with `BrowserUnavailable`, and every `RegistryStore` member with `RegistryUnavailable`. The common logic handles each by its tag: a failed `create` marks the session failed and create answers the parent with the error, the preview tool closes the browser it opened when the registry fails, and the cleanup job logs a registry failure.
   128	
   129	> [!NOTE] Why the roles pi already defines get contracts of their own
   130	> Storage, the wake-up timer, the agent's tools and the model providers already have interfaces in pi, and their contracts often hand pi's object through unchanged. Every role gets a contract anyway, so all roles are defined one way, and a reader and a new provider find every contract in the same form.
   131	
   132	A provider is one package that declares its own infrastructure. It exports a stack, which a deploy runs with Alchemy on the stage `prod`. The stack declares the provider's resources, and the code that runs in those resources builds the Layer of the contracts from the same declarations.
   133	
   134	> [!NOTE] Why each implementation declares its own infrastructure
   135	> A provider plugs an implementation in once, and both the running code and the deploy use it. When the declaration of a resource and the code that uses it are the same code, a resource the code needs cannot be missing from the deploy.
   136	
   137	---

     6	
     7	# Sessions
     8	
     9	## 🔭 Overview
    10	
    11	A session is one remote agent: a session object keyed by its session id, where pi-durable keeps its conversations and tentacles keeps a record of who started it, with which settings, and in what state it is. The registry keeps one entry per session so the list call returns a parent's sessions with their status in one call. At spawn, a session sets up its workspace and then starts running; a failed setup leaves it failed instead. It goes idle or failed when a run stops, waits while its agent asks a question, and stays readable after it is closed. A session also carries the skills and agent definitions its parent sent at spawn, which its agent finds by name, and the context files, which sit in `/workspace/context`. A daily job deletes every session whose last run stopped more than a month ago.
    12	
    13	## 🗺️ A session from spawn to deletion
    14	
    15	```mermaid
    16	sequenceDiagram
    17	    autonumber
    18	    actor P as Parent agent
    19	    participant H as Plugin
    20	    participant W as Worker
    21	    participant R as Registry
    22	    participant S as Session
    23	    participant Ws as Workspace
    24	    participant M as Model
    25	    P->>H: spawn with name, prompt, settings, skill, agent and context paths
    26	    H->>H: check the files, pack the archives
    27	    H->>W: create
    28	    W->>S: create
    29	    S->>S: store the record and the documents
    30	    S->>R: add the entry with settings, skill and agent names
    31	    S->>Ws: create: clone the repository, expand the skills and context
    32	    Ws-->>S: the workspace's tools, or the setup error
    33	    S-->>P: session id once the first run starts, or the setup error
    34	    loop every run
    35	        S->>S: expand the prompt's named skills
    36	        S->>M: model call
    37	        M-->>S: text and tool calls
    38	        S->>Ws: tool call
    39	        Ws-->>S: tool result
    40	        opt the agent asks the parent
    41	            S->>R: status waiting
    42	            S-->>H: state with the question
    43	            H-->>P: wake with the question
    44	            P->>W: answer
    45	            W->>S: answer, the run continues
    46	        end
    47	    end
    48	    S->>R: status idle or failed, time the run stopped
    49	    S-->>H: state with the last entry
    50	    H-->>P: wake with the result
    51	    P->>W: prompt for a new run, or close
    52	    W->>S: prompt or close
    53	    Note over W,S: a month after the last run stopped,<br/>the daily job deletes the session and drops its entry
    54	```
    55	
    56	The parent spawns with a name, a first prompt, its settings and any skill, agent and context paths (1). The plugin checks the files and packs them into up to three archives (2), and sends create through the Worker to a new session (3, 4). The session stores its record and its skills, agents and context documents (5) and adds its registry entry (6). It then creates its workspace, which clones the repository and expands the skills and context archives into `/workspace` (7), and hands back the workspace's tools or the setup error (8). The session answers with its id once the first run has started, or with the setup error, which leaves it failed (9; [workspace](workspace.md)).
    57	
    58	In every run, the session expands any skill the prompt names (10), sends the conversation to the model (11, 12) and runs the tools the model calls in the workspace (13, 14). When the agent asks the parent, the session waits, the plugin wakes the parent with the question and the answer continues the run (15 to 19; [question-round-trip](question-round-trip.md)).
    59	
    60	When a run ends, the session records the new status and the time the run stopped in the registry (20), and sends the state with the run's last entry, which the plugin turns into a wake (21, 22). A prompt starts a new run and close stops the session (23, 24; [worker-api](worker-api.md)). A month after the last run stopped, the daily job deletes the session (see Daily cleanup below).
    61	
    62	## 💽 Modeling
    63

   122	
   123	pi-durable's conversations (the root, its forks and subagent conversations) live inside the session object as pi-durable stores them. tentacles adds the other entities.
   124	
   125	### 🧠 Session
   126	
   127	SESSION is the record each session object keeps next to pi-durable's history. `id` is the session id the object is keyed by. `name` is required and given by the parent at spawn; it is what the parent's status line shows. `parent_harness` (pi or claude) and `parent_session_id` identify the parent: its harness and that harness's session id. `settings` holds what the parent chose at spawn, with the plugin's defaults for anything the parent left out: provider, model, effort level, image and size, and optionally the repository tentacles clones into the workspace. close sets `closed`, and a prompt that reopens the session clears it. `last_stopped` is the time the session's last run stopped, and is empty while the first run is going. `setup_error` holds why the workspace's setup failed at spawn, and is empty for every session whose setup succeeded (see [workspace](workspace.md)).
   128	
   129	The session state it sends the parent also carries its settings and the names of its skills and agents.
   130	
   131	The session's status is not a field. The session object watches pi-durable's state and derives it: a run going is running, an unanswered question is waiting, no run with `closed` set is closed, no run with the last run's failure recorded is failed (pi-durable keeps why the run failed), and no run otherwise is idle. A `setup_error` makes the status failed, with that error as the failure's detail. Each time the derived status changes, the session reports it to the registry and sends the session state to the parent, so a status always follows something the session did.
   132	
   133	> [!NOTE] Why the session records a failed setup itself
   134	> pi-durable records a failure only when a run ends, and the setup fails before any run exists. The session keeps the setup error in its own record, which makes a failed setup the one status that does not come from pi-durable. It happens only before the first run, since the first run starts only after a successful setup.
   135	
   136	### 📒 Registry entry
   137	
   138	REGISTRY_ENTRY lives in the registry, one for the whole deploy, with one entry per session: the session id, its name, the parent's harness and session id, the session's status (the same values as the session's derived status, closed included, and empty until the session reports its first one) and `last_stopped`, the time the last run stopped. When the session adds its entry at create, it also writes three values that never change: `settings`, and `skill_names` and `agent_names`, the names of the skills and agent definitions its spawn sent, which it reads from the archives. The registry records `last_stopped` itself when a status change reports a stopped run, keeps it when one stopped status follows another, and clears it when a new run starts. The session updates its entry on every state change, so the list call and the plugin's start-up sync get each session's status without asking each session. The daily cleanup job picks its candidates from the registry's `last_stopped`, and drops the entry after it deletes the session.
   139	
   140	`preview_port` and `preview_token` hold the session's preview while one is open, and are empty otherwise. A session has at most one preview, and only to validate the app in the preview's browser; the agent validates anything else, such as an API, inside the workspace with no preview. `preview_port` is the workspace port the preview exposes. `preview_token` is a random UUID that the registry generates when the preview tool opens a preview. It is the only value the registry returns for the new preview, so a preview URL carries neither the API key nor the session id. Opening a preview while one is open replaces it: the previous token stops working and its browser closes. When the run stops, the registry clears both fields. [workspace](workspace.md) covers how the agent opens and uses a preview.
   141	
   142	> [!TIP] Rejected: listing the session objects directly
   143	> The session host reaches a session only by its id, and session objects cannot be enumerated or queried across instances, so "the sessions of this parent" has no answer without a store that spans sessions. The registry is that store, and holding the status there spares the plugin one status call per session.
   144	
   145	### ❓ Question
   146	
   147	QUESTION is a question the session's agent asked with `ask_parent`: its id, its text and its answer, empty until the parent answers. Every question of the session lives in one session-wide document, one entry per question, and an entry stays after its answer. The id is the id of the asking tool call. When an eviction makes the tool run again, the replay finds its question in the document and keeps the id. If the answer already arrived, the replay returns the answer without asking again. The waiting question is the one with no answer whose tool call is still live; an aborted or finished call takes its question out of waiting. [question-round-trip](question-round-trip.md) follows the question to the parent and back.
   148	
   149	### 📚 Skills and agents documents
   150	
   151	A skill is a folder that holds a SKILL.md and whatever the skill points to. An agent definition is a file whose frontmatter names a subagent and whose body is that subagent's prompt. The skills document and the agents document are pi-durable documents of the session, written once at spawn. A skill entry holds the skill's name and description, which the prompt lists. It also holds the full path of its SKILL.md in the workspace, which the skill tool and a prompt expansion point the agent to. An agent entry holds the agent's name, description and prompt, which the subagent tool starts a subagent with. Agent definitions live only here and never enter the workspace.
   152	
   153	The session keeps no archive. It reads every archive at create to build the documents and hands the skills and context archives to the workspace's create, which expands them into `/workspace/skills` and `/workspace/context` once, at spawn. The agents archive goes no further, since agent definitions never enter the workspace. Deleting the session clears the documents, the workspace and the rest of its storage.
   154	
   155	CONTEXT_DOCUMENT records whether the spawn sent context files, so the prompt section renders without reading the workspace. The session state, the list and the registry entry carry nothing about the context.
   156	
   157	The API key and the Claude and GitHub credentials are Worker secrets, and none of these entities stores them.
   158	
   159	## 🟢 Lifecycle
   160	
   161	```mermaid
   162	stateDiagram-v2
   163	    [*] --> Running : spawn, setup succeeds (first prompt)
   164	    [*] --> Failed : spawn, setup fails
   165	    Running --> Idle : run finishes
   166	    Running --> Waiting : ask_parent asks
   167	    Waiting --> Running : answer
   168	    Running --> Failed : run fails
   169	    Idle --> Running : prompt
   170	    Failed --> Running : prompt
   171	    Closed --> Running : prompt (reopens)
   172	    Running --> Closed : close (aborts)
   173	    Waiting --> Closed : close (aborts)
   174	    Idle --> Closed : close
   175	    Failed --> Closed : close
   176	    Idle --> Deleted : a month after the run stopped
   177	    Failed --> Deleted : a month after the run stopped
   178	    Closed --> Deleted : a month after the run stopped
   179	    Deleted --> [*]
   180	
   181	    note right of Running : working, prompts follow up or steer
   182	    note right of Waiting : question shown to the parent,<br/>prompts queue as steers until answered
   183	    note right of Failed : like idle, shows the last run failed,<br/>or why the setup failed
   184	    note left of Closed : kept and readable, a prompt reopens it
   185	
   186	    classDef working fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e293b
   187	    classDef waiting fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#1e293b
   188	    classDef done fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#1e293b
   189	    classDef failed fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#1e293b
   190	    classDef ended fill:#f1f5f9,stroke:#64748b,color:#1e293b
   191	    class Running working
   192	    class Waiting waiting
   193	    class Idle done
   194	    class Failed failed
   195	    class Closed,Deleted ended
   196	```
   197	
   198	A session starts running when the parent spawns it, since spawn carries the first prompt; the session stores the skills and agent definitions and sets up its workspace before the run starts. When the setup fails, the session starts failed: its first run never starts, it has no workspace to use, and the failure carries the setup error. While it runs, a prompt from the parent follows up or steers. An eviction is not a state: pi-durable resumes the run by the session's alarm and the session stays running.
   199	
   200	When the agent asks a question, the session waits. The conversation cannot continue until the parent answers. A prompt sent meanwhile is a steer whatever its mode, and reaches the agent after the answer; it neither answers nor cancels the question.
   201	
   202	A run ends in one of two ways. When it finishes, the session is idle. When the run fails on an error it cannot recover from, the session is failed: it behaves like idle and records why the last run failed. The plugin notifies the parent either way, and a prompt on either starts a new run. The session's preview, if one is open, closes when a run stops.
   203	
   204	close aborts whatever the session is doing and leaves it closed: kept in its session object, where its history and state stay readable until it is deleted. close sets `closed` and aborts any run; the status turns closed once the session sees no run and `closed` set, at once for an idle or failed session. A prompt on a closed session clears `closed` and starts a new run, whether sent as a follow-up or a steer, and the status leaves closed once the run starts.
   205	
   206	The month before deletion counts from when the last run stops: when it finishes, fails or is aborted by close. Closing a session that is already idle or failed aborts no run, so its month keeps counting from when its last run stopped. A session is never deleted while a run is going, including while a question waits inside it, and reading a session (its messages, its status, a socket connecting) does not renew the month.
   207	
   208	## 🧩 Skills and agents
   209	
   210	### 🏗️ Which conversations get them
   211	
   212	```mermaid
   213	flowchart LR
   214	    subgraph root["Root conversation"]
   215	        R1@{ shape: rect, label: "Workspace tools,<br/>codemode, preview" }

odel and the tools of its level in the session, whatever its definition declares.
   307	
   308	### 📩 How the archives move
   309	
   310	#### 🧳 At spawn
   311	
   312	```mermaid
   313	sequenceDiagram
   314	    autonumber
   315	    actor P as Parent agent
   316	    participant H as Plugin helper
   317	    participant W as Worker
   318	    participant S as Session
   319	    participant DB as Session storage
   320	    participant R as Registry
   321	    participant Ws as Workspace
   322	    P->>+H: spawn with skill, agent and context paths
   323	    H->>H: stat every path, read and check each SKILL.md and agent file
   324	    alt a check fails
   325	        H-->>P: every problem with its path, grouped by kind
   326	    else every check passes
   327	        H->>H: pack one archive per kind that has paths
   328	        H->>+W: create with the archives
   329	        W->>+S: create
   330	        S->>DB: skills, agents and context documents
   331	        S->>R: add the entry with settings, skill and agent names
   332	        S->>Ws: create with the skills and context archives
   333	        alt the setup succeeds
   334	            Ws-->>S: the workspace's tools
   335	            S->>S: start the first run
   336	            S-->>W: started
   337	            W-->>H: session id
   338	            H-->>P: session id
   339	        else the setup fails
   340	            Ws-->>S: the setup error
   341	            S->>R: status failed
   342	            S-->>-W: the setup error
   343	            W-->>-H: the setup error
   344	            H-->>-P: the setup error
   345	        end
   346	    end
   347	```
   348	
   349	The parent calls the spawn tool with paths (1). The plugin's helper stats every path and reads and checks each SKILL.md and agent definition file (2). On any failure, the helper returns every problem as the spawn tool's result and sends nothing (3). Otherwise it packs one archive for each kind that has paths (4) and sends create with them (5), which the Worker hands to the session (6). The session reads every archive again to build the skills and agents documents and writes the context document (7). When it cannot read one or more archives, create returns one error that names each invalid archive and its problem, and the session stores nothing (see [worker-api](worker-api.md)). It adds its registry entry with the settings and the skill and agent names it read (8), and creates its workspace with the skills and context archives (9), which the provider expands into `/workspace/skills`, one folder per skill, and `/workspace/context`. When the setup succeeds, the workspace hands back its tools (10), the session starts the first run (11), and create answers with the session id once the run has started (12 to 14). When the setup fails, the workspace hands back the setup error (15), the session records it and reports the failed status (16), and create answers with the error (17 to 19).
   350	
   351	> [!NOTE] Why the archives travel in create
   352	> Only the workspace's setup reads the skills and context archives, and it runs once, at spawn. Handing the archives to create lets the session drop them once the files are in `/workspace`, so the session never stores them twice.
   353	
   354	#### 💬 In a prompt that names a skill
   355	
   356	```mermaid
   357	sequenceDiagram
   358	    autonumber
   359	    actor P as Parent
   360	    participant S as Session
   361	    participant D as Skills document
   362	    participant A as Conversation
   363	    P->>S: create or prompt
   364	    S->>S: find /skill:name and /name triggers
   365	    alt a trigger names a skill the session holds
   366	        S->>D: the skill's SKILL.md path
   367	        D-->>S: path
   368	        S->>A: prompt with each trigger replaced by a pointer block
   369	    else no trigger names a held skill
   370	        S->>A: prompt as written
   371	    end
   372	```
   373	
   374	The session expands every prompt, the first one included, before the conversation admits it (1, 2). `/skill:<name>` and `/<name>` name a skill when the word after the slash is one of the session's skill names and the trigger stands on its own, with whitespace or the start or end of the text on each side. For each one, the session takes the skill's path from the skills document (3, 4) and replaces the `/skill:<name>` or `/<name>` in place with a block that points at the skill (5); a skill named twice gets a block at each one. A prompt with no such name reaches the conversation as written (6), and so does any `/word` that names no skill, sits inside a path or has punctuation attached. The conversation keeps the expanded prompt, so the session's messages show what the agent saw.
   375	
   376	The prompt "Run /implement on the api repo" reaches the agent as:
   377	
   378	```text
   379	Run <skill name="implement" location="/workspace/skills/implement/SKILL.md">
   380	Read /workspace/skills/implement/SKILL.md before acting on this skill. Paths it names, such as references/ or scripts/, are relative to /workspace/skills/implement/.
   381	</skill> on the api repo
   382	```
   383	
   384	> [!NOTE] Why the block points at the skill instead of holding it
   385	> The agent reads SKILL.md with its read tool when it acts on the block, the same way it reads the files the skill refers to. The block stays a few lines whatever the skill's size, and expanding a prompt reads nothing but the skills document.
   386	
   387	### ♠️ What they expose
   388	
   389	| Member | Answers | Who asks |
   390	|---|---|---|
   391	| skills section | each skill's name and description, and that the skill tool loads one | the model, in every conversation, when the session holds skills |
   392	| skill tool | given a skill name, the same pointer block a prompt expansion adds; an unknown name fails the call, naming the skills that exist | the model, when a task matches a listed skill |
   393	| agents section | each agent's name and description, and how to spawn one with the subagent tool | the model, in the root and its children, when the session holds agents |
   394	| subagent tool, run and spawn | an optional agent name: with one, the subagent starts with that agent's prompt as its instructions; an unknown name fails the call, naming the agents that exist | the model, in the root and its children |
   395	
   396	Without an agent name, run starts the subagent with no instructions of its own, and spawn starts it with a line giving the subagent's name.
   397	
   398	When a subagent's input ends unanswered, pi-durable settles it with a reason (`aborted`, or the failure's code such as `model_error`) and, for failures, the error's message. run fails with `The subagent did not answer: unanswered (<reason>)`. A spawned subagent's reporter posts `[subagent <name> stopped: aborted]` or `[subagent <name> failed: <reason>]` to the parent, and wait returns that same text.
   399	
   400	> [!WARNING] A skill that names a skill the session does not hold
   401	> Skills often load other skills by name, sometimes with a plugin prefix such as `plugin:skill`, and refer to their own files through variables such as `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`. tentacles resolves neither. The model works them out from the listing and the `/workspace/skills/<name>/` layout, and a skill the parent did not send is missing: the agent finds no such name and carries on without it.
   402	
   403	## 📎 Context files
   404	
   405	The parent can send files and folders that the repository does not hold, such as a change's scratch files. They travel the way the skills do: a spawn parameter, an archive the plugin packs, and the archive expanded into the workspace at spawn. They land in `/workspace/context`, next to `/workspace/repo` and `/workspace/skills`.
   406	
   407	- **Where the files land.** The parent passes `context`, a list of file and folder paths on its machine. Each path lands under its basename: a file at `/workspace/context/<file name>` and a folder at `/workspace/context/<folder name>/…`. Two paths with the same basename fail the spawn. How the helper checks and packs the paths, how create reads the archive and how the setup expands it are in What a spawn sends and How the archives move.
   408	- **What the agent sees.** When the spawn sent context, every conversation's prompt carries a context section that says the parent sent files for context and that they are in `/workspace/context`. It names the folder only, not its entries, and without context there is no section. The agent reads the files with the workspace's tools.
   409	- **What stays outside.** `/workspace/context` is outside the repository. What the agent changes there stays in the workspace for the session's life and never returns to the parent. A different set of files means a new session. Deleting the session deletes the files with the rest of the workspace.

   438	A job runs once a day through the `Scheduler` contract (see [runtime-components](runtime-components.md)). It reads the registry and picks the sessions whose last run stopped more than a month ago. A running or waiting session is never a candidate. For each candidate it deletes the session through its session object, which clears the object's storage, removing its history, its record, its skills and agent definitions and its workspace with every file in it, and then drops the registry entry. The entry goes only after the session is gone, so a deletion that stopped halfway leaves the session a candidate, and the next day's job deletes it again and drops the entry. No preview is left by then, since the preview closes when a run stops. Nothing outside tentacles is touched: branches the agent pushed stay on GitHub, and work it never pushed is gone with the workspace.

A deletion written to the same alarm would be lost the first time a run stopped, and the alarm handler could not tell a due deletion from a resume. A daily job over the registry keeps the two apart.

docs/technical-design/sessions.md:11:A session is one remote agent: a session object keyed by its session id, where pi-durable keeps its conversations and tentacles keeps a record of who started it, with which settings, and in what state it is. The registry keeps one entry per session so the list call returns a parent's sessions with their status in one call. At spawn, a session sets up its workspace and then starts running; a failed setup leaves it failed instead. It goes idle or failed when a run stops, waits while its agent asks a question, and stays readable after it is closed. A session also carries the skills and agent definitions its parent sent at spawn, which its agent finds by name, and the context files, which sit in `/workspace/context`. A daily job deletes every session whose last run stopped more than a month ago.

docs/technical-design/sessions.md:127:SESSION is the record each session object keeps next to pi-durable's history. `id` is the session id the object is keyed by. `name` is required and given by the parent at spawn; it is what the parent's status line shows. `parent_harness` (pi or claude) and `parent_session_id` identify the parent: its harness and that harness's session id. `settings` holds what the parent chose at spawn, with the plugin's defaults for anything the parent left out: provider, model, effort level, image and size, and optionally the repository tentacles clones into the workspace. close sets `closed`, and a prompt that reopens the session clears it. `last_stopped` is the time the session's last run stopped, and is empty while the first run is going. `setup_error` holds why the workspace's setup failed at spawn, and is empty for every session whose setup succeeded (see [workspace](workspace.md)).
docs/technical-design/sessions.md:131:The session's status is not a field. The session object watches pi-durable's state and derives it: a run going is running, an unanswered question is waiting, no run with `closed` set is closed, no run with the last run's failure recorded is failed (pi-durable keeps why the run failed), and no run otherwise is idle. A `setup_error` makes the status failed, with that error as the failure's detail. Each time the derived status changes, the session reports it to the registry and sends the session state to the parent, so a status always follows something the session did.
docs/technical-design/sessions.md:134:> pi-durable records a failure only when a run ends, and the setup fails before any run exists. The session keeps the setup error in its own record, which makes a failed setup the one status that does not come from pi-durable. It happens only before the first run, since the first run starts only after a successful setup.
docs/technical-design/sessions.md:151:A skill is a folder that holds a SKILL.md and whatever the skill points to. An agent definition is a file whose frontmatter names a subagent and whose body is that subagent's prompt. The skills document and the agents document are pi-durable documents of the session, written once at spawn. A skill entry holds the skill's name and description, which the prompt lists. It also holds the full path of its SKILL.md in the workspace, which the skill tool and a prompt expansion point the agent to. An agent entry holds the agent's name, description and prompt, which the subagent tool starts a subagent with. Agent definitions live only here and never enter the workspace.
docs/technical-design/sessions.md:198:A session starts running when the parent spawns it, since spawn carries the first prompt; the session stores the skills and agent definitions and sets up its workspace before the run starts. While it runs, a prompt from the parent follows up or steers. An eviction is not a state: pi-durable resumes the run by the session's alarm and the session stays running.

Every conversation in a session gets the skills extension: the root, its children and their children. The root and its children also get the agents extension, so a child can spawn subagents of its own; a grandchild cannot. Only the root carries the question tool and tentacles' own instructions. An extension leaves its section out of the prompt when the section has nothing to list.

     9	## 🔭 Overview
    10	
    11	tentacles runs as a set of roles: an API entry that is the only way in, a registry for everything that spans sessions, one session object per session running pi-durable, a workspace per session that holds the agent's files and runs its commands, model providers, a codemode sandbox, a managed browser for previews and a daily scheduler. tentacles' shared logic reaches each role through a contract, and a provider fills every contract, so another setup can replace the infrastructure without changing the plugin. No container holds a credential: the provider adds the tokens to requests outside the container. Cloudflare is the first provider; [deploy](providers/cloudflare/deploy.md) covers how it fills each role.
    12	
    13	## 🏗️ Architecture
    14	
    15	```mermaid
    16	flowchart LR
    17	    subgraph dev["Developer machine"]
    18	        Plugin@{ shape: stadium, label: "tentacles plugin<br/>helper" }
    19	    end
    20	    subgraph prov["A provider"]
    21	        Entry@{ shape: rect, label: "API entry<br/>API key, routes,<br/>preview route" }
    22	        Registry@{ shape: rect, label: "Registry<br/>sessions per parent,<br/>each session's preview" }
    23	        Session@{ shape: rect, label: "Session object<br/>pi-durable Harness, storage,<br/>socket, wake-up timer" }
    24	        Workspace@{ shape: rect, label: "Workspace<br/>files, isolate shell,<br/>container" }
    25	        Models@{ shape: rect, label: "Model providers" }
    26	        Codemode@{ shape: rect, label: "Codemode sandbox" }
    27	        Browser@{ shape: rect, label: "Browser" }
    28	        Cron@{ shape: rect, label: "Scheduler" }
    29	    end
    30	    GitHub@{ shape: cloud, label: "GitHub" }
    31	
    32	    Plugin -->|"requests, socket"| Entry
    33	    Entry -->|"listings, preview lookups"| Registry
    34	    Entry -->|"session requests by id,<br/>preview requests"| Session
    35	    Session -->|"status changes,<br/>preview opened and cleared"| Registry
    36	    Session -->|"create at spawn,<br/>tool calls, forward"| Workspace
    37	    Session -->|"model calls"| Models
    38	    Session -->|"codemode scripts"| Codemode
    39	    Session -->|"open and close<br/>the preview's browser"| Browser
    40	    Workspace -->|"clone, fetch, push,<br/>token added outside the container"| GitHub
    41	    Browser -->|"preview URL"| Entry
    42	    Cron -->|"daily cleanup"| Registry
    43	
    44	    classDef grey fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#4b5563,color:#1f2937
    45	    classDef blue fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1f2937
    46	    classDef green fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#1f2937
    47	    classDef violet fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#1f2937
    48	    class Plugin grey
    49	    class Entry blue
    50	    class Registry,Session,Workspace,Models,Codemode,Browser,Cron green
    51	    class GitHub violet
    52	```
    53	
    54	The **API entry** checks the API key on every plugin request and socket, then routes it: listings and preview lookups go to the registry, and everything about one session goes to that session's object by its id. Its preview route turns a preview URL's token into a session and a port and hands the request to the session object. [worker-api](worker-api.md) lists its calls and the session socket.
    55	
    56	The **registry** is the one store that spans sessions: an entry per session with its name, its parent, its status, the time its last run stopped, its settings and skill and agent names, and the session's preview while one is open. [sessions](sessions.md) lists the fields of each entry.
    57	
    58	The **session object** is one live instance per session, keyed by its session id. It runs pi-durable's Harness over its own storage, with the question tool and the wake-up timer that resumes a run after an eviction. It creates the session's workspace at spawn and installs the tools the workspace returns, holds the parent's socket, sends each model call to the provider the settings name, and opens and closes the preview's browser. It never writes the status ahead of the run: it watches pi-durable's state and tells the registry each time the derived status changes.
    59	
    60	The **workspace** holds the session's files under `/workspace` and runs the agent's commands on the cheapest backend that can run them, the isolate shell or the container. Its git reaches GitHub with the token added outside the container. [workspace](workspace.md) covers its contract, setup and tools.
    61	
    62	The **model providers**, the **codemode sandbox**, the **browser** and the **scheduler** each answer one kind of call: a model call, a codemode script, opening or closing the preview's browser, and firing the daily cleanup job.
    63	
    64	## 🔌 Provider-neutral roles
    65	
    66	Each component above plays a role that any provider has to fill. Several roles already sit behind an interface the pi libraries define: pi-durable takes its storage, its wake-up timer and its tools from the host, and pi-ai reaches models through providers. The plugin talks only to the Worker API and the session socket, so it does not change with the provider.
    67	
    68	| Role | Contract | What the common logic asks it | Interface it builds on |
    69	|---|---|---|---|
    70	| Session host: one live instance per session, revived on demand | `SessionHost` | reach a session by id and run one of its operations: create, prompt, answer, close, messages, status, connect a socket, forward a preview request, delete | pi-durable's Harness opens over any host |
    71	| Session storage | `SessionStorage` | pi-durable's storage for one session | pi-durable's storage adapter |
    72	| Wake-up timer | `WakeTimer` | set or clear the one timer that resumes a run after an eviction | pi-durable's `onWake`; the host writes the timer |
    73	| Parent socket | `ParentChannel` | send the session state to every socket the parent holds open | none |
    74	| Registry of sessions and their preview | `RegistryStore` | add an entry, record a status and the time a run stops, list one parent's sessions, open a preview and return its token, resolve and clear a preview, remove an entry, find the sessions stopped before a given time | none |
    75	| Workspace: the session's files and the backends that run its commands | `Workspace` | `create(init)`: set up the workspace at spawn from the repository URL or none, the git identity, the container's size and image, and the skills and context archives, and return the tools the harness installs, each with its replay policy and its own execute; `forward`: hand a preview request to a port and return the app's answer, 502 when nothing listens | pi-durable's tool registrations |
    76	| Browser | `Browser` | open a browser for the session's preview, returning the CDP URL agent-browser connects to, and close it | agent-browser speaks CDP to any URL |
    77	| Preview routing | `PreviewRouter` | the public URL a preview token is served on | none |
    78	| Models | `ModelProviders` | every model provider the session's settings can name | pi-ai providers |
    79	| Daily cleanup | `Scheduler` | run a job once a day | none |
    80	| Codemode sandbox | `CodeSandbox` | the sandbox codemode scripts run in | pi-durable's codemode sandbox |
    81	| API entry: auth and routing | none, the Worker API itself | nothing: the API entry runs the API handlers | [worker-api](worker-api.md) |
    82	
    83	A provider implements every contract in the table. The common logic (the API handlers, the session logic with its lifecycle and deletion, the preview handler, the cleanup job and the remote agent's tools other than the workspace's) and the pi libraries are the same for every provider. A deploy uses one provider for every role, and a variable read by the deploy picks the provider. [providers](providers/README.md) lists the providers.
    84	
    85	```mermaid
    86	flowchart LR
    87	    subgraph setup["A provider"]
    88	        In@{ shape: rect, label: "Entry points<br/>Worker fetch, session object,<br/>preview route, cron, alarm" }
    89	        Impl@{ shape: rect, label: "One implementation<br/>per contract" }
    90	    end
    91	    subgraph core["Common logic"]
    92	        Logic@{ shape: rect, label: "API handlers, session logic,<br/>preview handler, cleanup job,<br/>the remote agent's tools" }
    93	        Pi@{ shape: hex, label: "pi libraries<br/>pi-durable, pi-ai" }
    94	        Logic --> Pi
    95	    end
    96	    Contracts@{ shape: braces, label: "The contracts" }
    97	    In -->|"call"| Logic
    98	    Logic -->|"reaches each role through"| Contracts
    99	    Impl -.->|"implements"| Contracts
   100	    classDef blue fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1f2937
   101	    classDef green fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#1f2937
   102	    classDef amber fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#1f2937
   103	    classDef payload stroke:#d97706
   104	    class Logic blue
   105	    class Pi amber
   106	    class Contracts payload
   107	    class In,Impl green
   108	```
   109	
   110	The calls run both ways. The provider receives every outside event (the API requests, the preview route, the cron trigger and the alarm) and calls the common logic. Each session object hosts its session's logic. The common logic calls the provider only through the contracts. `SessionHost` goes both ways: the provider hosts each session, and the common logic reaches a session by its id through it.
   111	
   112	> [!TIP] Considered and not taken: roles from different providers in one deploy
   113	> On Cloudflare one session object fills five roles (`SessionHost`, `SessionStorage`, `WakeTimer`, `ParentChannel`, and `Workspace`, whose files and container live in it), so a role taken from another provider would have to split that object apart. One provider per deploy keeps each provider's parts together.
   114	
   115	> [!NOTE] Why credentials are not a contract
   116	> Keeping credentials out of containers is how a provider implements `Workspace` and `ModelProviders`: it adds the tokens to requests outside the container, in its git client and at egress. Each provider keeps them out in its own way, so the shared logic never sees a credential and has nothing to ask a contract for.
   117	
   118	> [!NOTE] Where the contracts come from
   119	> The contracts follow the roles and the host interfaces pi already defines, not any infrastructure library. A role pi already abstracts, such as storage, the wake-up timer or the agent's tools, takes pi's interface as its contract's shape.
   120	
   121	## 🧩 Provider contracts
   122	
   123	Each contract in the table under 🔌 Provider-neutral roles is an Effect service, and each provider supplies its implementation as a Layer. The common logic asks for a contract and never names a provider.
   124	
   125	Shapes the API defines, such as the session state, pass through the contracts with the types the API declares, so a contract and the API cannot disagree.
   126	
   127	A member that can fail declares a tagged error with a message: `Workspace.create` fails with the setup error, `Browser.open` with `BrowserUnavailable`, and every `RegistryStore` member with `RegistryUnavailable`. The common logic handles each by its tag: a failed `create` marks the session failed and create answers the parent with the error, the preview tool closes the browser it opened when the registry fails, and the cleanup job logs a registry failure.
   128	
   129	> [!NOTE] Why the roles pi already defines get contracts of their own
   130	> Storage, the wake-up timer, the agent's tools and the model providers already have interfaces in pi, and their contracts often hand pi's object through unchanged. Every role gets a contract anyway, so all roles are defined one way, and a reader and a new provider find every contract in the same form.
   131	
   132	A provider is one package that declares its own infrastructure. It exports a stack, which a deploy runs with Alchemy on the stage `prod`. The stack declares the provider's resources, and the code that runs in those resources builds the Layer of the contracts from the same declarations.
   133	
   134	> [!NOTE] Why each implementation declares its own infrastructure
   135	> A provider plugs an implementation in once, and both the running code and the deploy use it. When the declaration of a resource and the code that uses it are the same code, a resource the code needs cannot be missing from the deploy.
   136	
   137	---
   138

     3	summary: "What tentacles stores about a remote session, how a session runs from spawn to deletion, the skills, agents and context files it carries, and the daily job that deletes sessions a month after their last run."
     4	created: "2026-11-09"
     5	---
     6	
     7	# Sessions
     8	
     9	## 🔭 Overview
    10	
    11	A session is one remote agent: a session object keyed by its session id, where pi-durable keeps its conversations and tentacles keeps a record of who started it, with which settings, and in what state it is. The registry keeps one entry per session so the list call returns a parent's sessions with their status in one call. At spawn, a session sets up its workspace and then starts running; a failed setup leaves it failed instead. It goes idle or failed when a run stops, waits while its agent asks a question, and stays readable after it is closed. A session also carries the skills and agent definitions its parent sent at spawn, which its agent finds by name, and the context files, which sit in `/workspace/context`. A daily job deletes every session whose last run stopped more than a month ago.
    12	
    13	## 🗺️ A session from spawn to deletion
    14	
    15	```mermaid
    16	sequenceDiagram
    17	    autonumber
    18	    actor P as Parent agent
    19	    participant H as Plugin
    20	    participant W as Worker
    21	    participant R as Registry
    22	    participant S as Session
    23	    participant Ws as Workspace
    24	    participant M as Model
    25	    P->>H: spawn with name, prompt, settings, skill, agent and context paths
    26	    H->>H: check the files, pack the archives
    27	    H->>W: create
    28	    W->>S: create
    29	    S->>S: store the record and the documents
    30	    S->>R: add the entry with settings, skill and agent names
    31	    S->>Ws: create: clone the repository, expand the skills and context
    32	    Ws-->>S: the workspace's tools, or the setup error
    33	    S-->>P: session id once the first run starts, or the setup error
    34	    loop every run
    35	        S->>S: expand the prompt's named skills
    36	        S->>M: model call
    37	        M-->>S: text and tool calls
    38	        S->>Ws: tool call
    39	        Ws-->>S: tool result
    40	        opt the agent asks the parent
    41	            S->>R: status waiting
    42	            S-->>H: state with the question
    43	            H-->>P: wake with the question
    44	            P->>W: answer
    45	            W->>S: answer, the run continues
    46	        end
    47	    end
    48	    S->>R: status idle or failed, time the run stopped
    49	    S-->>H: state with the last entry
    50	    H-->>P: wake with the result
    51	    P->>W: prompt for a new run, or close
    52	    W->>S: prompt or close
    53	    Note over W,S: a month after the last run stopped,<br/>the daily job deletes the session and drops its entry
    54	```
    55	
    56	The parent spawns with a name, a first prompt, its settings and any skill, agent and context paths (1). The plugin checks the files and packs them into up to three archives (2), and sends create through the Worker to a new session (3, 4). The session stores its record and its skills, agents and context documents (5) and adds its registry entry (6). It then creates its workspace, which clones the repository and expands the skills and context archives into `/workspace` (7), and hands back the workspace's tools or the setup error (8). The session answers with its id once the first run has started, or with the setup error, which leaves it failed (9; [workspace](workspace.md)).
    57	
    58	In every run, the session expands any skill the prompt names (10), sends the conversation to the model (11, 12) and runs the tools the model calls in the workspace (13, 14). When the agent asks the parent, the session waits, the plugin wakes the parent with the question and the answer continues the run (15 to 19; [question-round-trip](question-round-trip.md)).
    59	
    60	When a run ends, the session records the new status and the time the run stopped in the registry (20), and sends the state with the run's last entry, which the plugin turns into a wake (21, 22). A prompt starts a new run and close stops the session (23, 24; [worker-api](worker-api.md)). A month after the last run stopped, the daily job deletes the session (see Daily cleanup below).
    61	
    62	## 💽 Modeling
    63	
    64	```mermaid
    65	erDiagram
    66	    REGISTRY_ENTRY ||--|| SESSION : "points to"

    73	    AGENTS_DOCUMENT ||--o{ AGENT : "lists"

    86	    }

    88	        string id PK
    89	        string name

    96	    }

    98	        string id PK
    99	        text text
   100	        text answer "nullable"
   101	    }

   103	        json skills "written once at spawn"
   104	    }

   106	        json agents "written once at spawn"

   112	        string name

   122	
   123	pi-durable's conversations (the root, its forks and subagent conversations) live inside the session object as pi-durable stores them. tentacles adds the other entities.
   124	
   125	### 🧠 Session
   126	
   127	SESSION is the record each session object keeps next to pi-durable's history. `id` is the session id the object is keyed by. `name` is required and given by the parent at spawn; it is what the parent's status line shows. `parent_harness` (pi or claude) and `parent_session_id` identify the parent: its harness and that harness's session id. `settings` holds what the parent chose at spawn, with the plugin's defaults for anything the parent left out: provider, model, effort level, image and size, and optionally the repository tentacles clones into the workspace. close sets `closed`, and a prompt that reopens the session clears it. `last_stopped` is the time the session's last run stopped, and is empty while the first run is going. `setup_error` holds why the workspace's setup failed at spawn, and is empty for every session whose setup succeeded (see [workspace](workspace.md)).
   128	
   129	The session state it sends the parent also carries its settings and the names of its skills and agents.
   130	
   131	The session's status is not a field. The session object watches pi-durable's state and derives it: a run going is running, an unanswered question is waiting, no run with `closed` set is closed, no run with the last run's failure recorded is failed (pi-durable keeps why the run failed), and no run otherwise is idle. A `setup_error` makes the status failed, with that error as the failure's detail. Each time the derived status changes, the session reports it to the registry and sends the session state to the parent, so a status always follows something the session did.
   132	
   133	> [!NOTE] Why the session records a failed setup itself
   134	> pi-durable records a failure only when a run ends, and the setup fails before any run exists. The session keeps the setup error in its own record, which makes a failed setup the one status that does not come from pi-durable. It happens only before the first run, since the first run starts only after a successful setup.
   135	
   136	### 📒 Registry entry
   137	
   138	REGISTRY_ENTRY lives in the registry, one for the whole deploy, with one entry per session: the session id, its name, the parent's harness and session id, the session's status (the same values as the session's derived status, closed included, and empty until the session reports its first one) and `last_stopped`, the time the last run stopped. When the session adds its entry at create, it also writes three values that never change: `settings`, and `skill_names` and `agent_names`, the names of the skills and agent definitions its spawn sent, which it reads from the archives. The registry records `last_stopped` itself when a status change reports a stopped run, keeps it when one stopped status follows another, and clears it when a new run starts. The session updates its entry on every state change, so the list call and the plugin's start-up sync get each session's status without asking each session. The daily cleanup job picks its candidates from the registry's `last_stopped`, and drops the entry after it deletes the session.
   139	
   140	`preview_port` and `preview_token` hold the session's preview while one is open, and are empty otherwise. A session has at most one preview, and only to validate the app in the preview's browser; the agent validates anything else, such as an API, inside the workspace with no preview. `preview_port` is the workspace port the preview exposes. `preview_token` is a random UUID that the registry generates when the preview tool opens a preview. It is the only value the registry returns for the new preview, so a preview URL carries neither the API key nor the session id. Opening a preview while one is open replaces it: the previous token stops working and its browser closes. When the run stops, the registry clears both fields. [workspace](workspace.md) covers how the agent opens and uses a preview.
   141	
   142	> [!TIP] Rejected: listing the session objects directly
   143	> The session host reaches a session only by its id, and session objects cannot be enumerated or queried across instances, so "the sessions of this parent" has no answer without a store that spans sessions. The registry is that store, and holding the status there spares the plugin one status call per session.
   144	
   145	### ❓ Question
   146	
   147	QUESTION is a question the session's agent asked with `ask_parent`: its id, its text and its answer, empty until the parent answers. Every question of the session lives in one session-wide document, one entry per question, and an entry stays after its answer. The id is the id of the asking tool call. When an eviction makes the tool run again, the replay finds its question in the document and keeps the id. If the answer already arrived, the replay returns the answer without asking again. The waiting question is the one with no answer whose tool call is still live; an aborted or finished call takes its question out of waiting. [question-round-trip](question-round-trip.md) follows the question to the parent and back.
   148	
   149	### 📚 Skills and agents documents
   150	
   151	A skill is a folder that holds a SKILL.md and whatever the skill points to. An agent definition is a file whose frontmatter names a subagent and whose body is that subagent's prompt. The skills document and the agents document are pi-durable documents of the session, written once at spawn. A skill entry holds the skill's name and description, which the prompt lists. It also holds the full path of its SKILL.md in the workspace, which the skill tool and a prompt expansion point the agent to. An agent entry holds the agent's name, description and prompt, which the subagent tool starts a subagent with. Agent definitions live only here and never enter the workspace.
   152	
   153	The session keeps no archive. It reads every archive at create to build the documents and hands the skills and context archives to the workspace's create, which expands them into `/workspace/skills` and `/workspace/context` once, at spawn. The agents archive goes no further, since agent definitions never enter the workspace. Deleting the session clears the documents, the workspace and the rest of its storage.
   154	
   155	CONTEXT_DOCUMENT records whether the spawn sent context files, so the prompt section renders without reading the workspace. The session state, the list and the registry entry carry nothing about the context.
   156	
   157	The API key and the Claude and GitHub credentials are Worker secrets, and none of these entities stores them.
   158	
   159	## 🟢 Lifecycle
   160	
   161	```mermaid
   162	stateDiagram-v2
   163	    [*] --> Running : spawn, setup succeeds (first prompt)
   164	    [*] --> Failed : spawn, setup fails
   165	    Running --> Idle : run finishes
   166	    Running --> Waiting : ask_parent asks
   167	    Waiting --> Running : answer
   168	    Running --> Failed : run fails
   169	    Idle --> Running : prompt
   170	    Failed --> Running : prompt
   171	    Closed --> Running : prompt (reopens)
   172	    Running --> Closed : close (aborts)
   173	    Waiting --> Closed : close (aborts)
   174	    Idle --> Closed : close
   175	    Failed --> Closed : close
   176	    Idle --> Deleted : a month after the run stopped
   177	    Failed --> Deleted : a month after the run stopped
   178	    Closed --> Deleted : a month after the run stopped
   179	    Deleted --> [*]
   180	
   181	    note right of Running : working, prompts follow up or steer
   182	    note right of Waiting : question shown to the parent,<br/>prompts queue as steers until answered
   183	    note right of Failed : like idle, shows the last run failed,<br/>or why the setup failed
   184	    note left of Closed : kept and readable, a prompt reopens it
   185	
   186	    classDef working fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e293b
   187	    classDef waiting fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#1e293b
   188	    classDef done fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#1e293b
   189	    classDef failed fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#1e293b
   190	    classDef ended fill:#f1f5f9,stroke:#64748b,color:#1e293b
   191	    class Running working
   192	    class Waiting waiting
   193	    class Idle done
   194	    class Failed failed
   195	    class Closed,Deleted ended
   196	```
   197	
   198	A session starts running when the parent spawns it, since spawn carries the first prompt; the session stores the skills and agent definitions and sets up its workspace before the run starts. When the setup fails, the session starts failed: its first run never starts, it has no workspace to use, and the failure carries the setup error. While it runs, a prompt from the parent follows up or steers. An eviction is not a state: pi-durable resumes the run by the session's alarm and the session stays running.
   199	
   200	When the agent asks a question, the session waits. The conversation cannot continue until the parent answers. A prompt sent meanwhile is a steer whatever its mode, and reaches the agent after the answer; it neither answers nor cancels the question.
   201	
   202	A run ends in one of two ways. When it finishes, the session is idle. When the run fails on an error it cannot recover from, the session is failed: it behaves like idle and records why the last run failed. The plugin notifies the parent either way, and a prompt on either starts a new run. The session's preview, if one is open, closes when a run stops.
   203	
   204	close aborts whatever the session is doing and leaves it closed: kept in its session object, where its history and state stay readable until it is deleted. close sets `closed` and aborts any run; the status turns closed once the session sees no run and `closed` set, at once for an idle or failed session.    349	The parent calls the spawn tool with paths (1). The plugin's helper stats every path and reads and checks each SKILL.md and agent definition file (2). On any failure, the helper returns every problem as the spawn tool's result and sends nothing (3). Otherwise it packs one archive for each kind that has paths (4) and sends create with them (5), which the Worker hands to the session (6). The session reads every archive again to build the skills and agents documents and writes the context document (7). When it cannot read one or more archives, create returns one error that names each invalid archive and its problem, and the session stores nothing (see [worker-api](worker-api.md)). It adds its registry entry with the settings and the skill and agent names it read (8), and creates its workspace with the skills and context archives (9), which the provider expands into `/workspace/skills`, one folder per skill, and `/workspace/context`. When the setup succeeds, the workspace hands back its tools (10), the session starts the first run (11), and create answers with the session id once the run has started (12 to 14). When the setup fails, the workspace hands back the setup error (15), the session records it and reports the failed status (16), and create answers with the error (17 to 19).

   351	> [!NOTE] Why the archives travel in create
   352	> Only the workspace's setup reads the skills and context archives, and it runs once, at spawn. Handing the archives to create lets the session drop them once the files are in `/workspace`, so the session never stores them twice.

   374	The session expands every prompt, the first one included, before the conversation admits it (1, 2). `/skill:<name>` and `/<name>` name a skill when the word after the slash is one of the session's skill names and the trigger stands on its own, with whitespace or the start or end of the text on each side. For each one, the session takes the skill's path from the skills document (3, 4) and replaces the `/skill:<name>` or `/<name>` in place with a block that points at the skill (5); a skill named twice gets a block at each one. A prompt with no such name reaches the conversation as written (6), and so does any `/word` that names no skill, sits inside a path or has punctuation attached. The conversation keeps the expanded prompt, so the session's messages show what the agent saw.

   388

The model works them out from the listing and the `/workspace/skills/<name>/` layout, and a skill the parent did not send is missing: the agent finds no such name and carries on without it.

   403	## 📎 Context files
   404	
   405	The parent can send files and folders that the repository does not hold, such as a change's scratch files. They travel the way the skills do: a spawn parameter, an archive the plugin packs, and the archive expanded into the workspace at spawn. They land in `/workspace/context`, next to `/workspace/repo` and `/workspace/skills`.
   406	
   407	- **Where the files land.** The parent passes `context`, a list of file and folder paths on its machine. Each path lands under its basename: a file at `/workspace/context/<file name>` and a folder at `/workspace/context/<folder name>/…`. Two paths with the same basename fail the spawn. How the helper checks and packs the paths, how create reads the archive and how the setup expands it are in What a spawn sends and How the archives move.
   408	- **What the agent sees.** When the spawn sent context, every conversation's prompt carries a context section that says the parent sent files for context and that they are in `/workspace/context`. It names the folder only, not its entries, and without context there is no section. The agent reads the files with the workspace's tools.
   409	- **What stays outside.** `/workspace/context` is outside the repository. What the agent changes there stays in the workspace for the session's life and never returns to the parent. A different set of files means a new session. Deleting the session deletes the files with the rest of the workspace.

   438	A job runs once a day through the `Scheduler` contract (see [runtime-components](runtime-components.md)). It reads the registry and picks the sessions whose last run stopped more than a month ago. A running or waiting session is never a candidate. For each candidate it deletes the session through its session object, which clears the object's storage, removing its history, its record, its skills and agent definitions and its workspace with every file in it, and then drops the registry entry. The entry goes only after the session is gone, so a deletion that stopped halfway leaves the session a candidate, and the next day's job deletes it again and drops the entry. No preview is left by then, since the preview closes when a run stops. Nothing outside tentacles is touched: branches the agent pushed stay on GitHub, and work it never pushed is gone with the workspace.

   440	tentacles does not tell the parent. The parent's plugin removes the session from its local list the first time it learns of the deletion (see [plugin](plugin.md)).
   441	
   442	The session's wake-up timer belongs to pi-durable, which uses it only to resume a run after an eviction. Nothing else schedules on it.
   443	
   444	> [!TIP] Rejected: scheduling each session's deletion on its own wake-up timer
   445	> A session has one wake-up timer, and pi-durable writes it and deletes it as runs start and end: after a run ends, the host clears it, and a new instance replaces it. A deletion written to the same alarm would be lost the first time a run stopped, and the alarm handler could not tell a due deletion from a resume. A daily job over the registry keeps the two apart.
