  persist: '\n' +
    '## Persist and Resume\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Use SQLite or JSONL storage to keep conversations across restarts:\n' +
    '\n' +
    '```typescript\n' +
    'import { openNodeSqliteStorage } from "@earendil-works/pi-durable/storage/sqlite/node";\n' +
    '\n' +
    'const harness = await Harness.open(await openNodeSqliteStorage("./session.sqlite"), { models, registry }, context);\n' +
    'const root = await harness.root(context); // the same root as last time\n' +
    'harness.resume(); // continue any run the last process left unfinished\n' +
    '```\n' +
    '\n' +
    "Work interrupted by a crash or close stays pending. `resume()` starts the task scheduler; submitting or waiting starts it too. A process that only shows a session another one drives opens it with `readOnly: true`: open recovers nothing, and every write, `resume()`, and every call that would run tasks rejects with `ReadOnlySession`. That option covers the Harness, not the storage open before it: open JSONL storage with `openNodeJsonlStorage(directory, context, { readOnly: true })` too, since a writable JSONL open repairs files the writer may be appending to (see [Storage](#storage)). SQLite storage opens as usual: SQLite's file locks keep it safe beside the writer. Each conversation has its own persisted UUIDv7 in `pi.provider`, forwarded to pi-ai as `sessionId` for provider prompt-cache and session affinity. It survives reopen, retries, reset, compaction, and model changes; a child or fork receives a fresh identity. A legacy conversation receives and persists one before its first generation or compaction request.\n" +
    '\n' +
    'A retried submission with the same `requestId` returns the existing submission instead of submitting twice:\n' +
    '\n' +
    '```typescript\n' +
    'const submission = await root.submit({ type: "input", content: "Hello", requestId: "greeting-1" }, context);\n' +
    '// After a restart: the same request ID finds the same submission.\n' +
    'const again = await root.submit({ type: "input", content: "Hello", requestId: "greeting-1" }, context);\n' +
    '// again.id === submission.id\n' +
    '```\n' +
    '\n' +
    '`harness.submission(id)` reacquires a submission by ID, for example to wait for it after a restart.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### Sleeping and Waking Up\n' +
    '\n' +
    'A task waits for time by ending its phase asleep. The sleep is stored, so the task holds no invocation meanwhile, survives restarts, and resumes at the checkpoint once the Harness clock reaches `until`:\n' +
    '\n' +
    '```typescript\n' +
    'const Reminder = defineTask<{ text: string; at: number }, { phase: "wait" } | { phase: "deliver" }, null>({\n' +
    '\tname: "app.reminder",\n' +
    '\tversion: 1,\n' +
    '\tinitial: () => ({ phase: "wait" }),\n' +
    '\tphases: {\n' +
    '\t\t// Resolves once the sleep is stored; the phase ends there.\n' +
    '\t\twait: (task, runtime, context) => runtime.sleepUntil(task.input.at, { phase: "deliver" }, context),\n' +
    '\t\tdeliver: async (task, runtime, context) => {\n' +
    '\t\t\tawait notify(task.input.text);\n' +
    '\t\t\tawait runtime.commit(() => ({ status: "terminal", outcome: { status: "completed", result: null } }), context);\n' +
    '\t\t},\n' +
    '\t},\n' +
    '\tabort: (_task, runtime, context) =>\n' +
    '\t\truntime.commit(() => ({ status: "terminal", outcome: { status: "aborted" } }), context),\n' +
    '});\n' +
    '```\n' +
    '\n' +
    'There is no sleep in the middle of a phase: a phase reruns from its top after a restart, so work after the wait goes in the next phase, and what it needs goes in the checkpoint. `{ status: "sleeping", until, checkpoint }` returned from `runtime.commit()` is the same sleep, committed together with other writes; with `signals` it also wakes on a signal (see [Signals](#signals)), and `until` becomes optional. Retry backoffs and deferred-response polls of the built-in tasks sleep the same way.\n' +
    '\n' +
    'The timers of the Session, the sc',
  env: '\n' +
    '## Environment\n' +
    '\n' +
    "`env` builds the execution environment for each tool call, section rendering, and `runtime.env()`. It receives the conversation's ID, its agent `cwd`, and committed reads, so one function serves a directory per conversation or a container per conversation:\n" +
    '\n' +
    '```typescript\n' +
    'import { NodeExecutionEnv } from "@earendil-works/pi-durable/env/node";\n' +
    '\n' +
    'const harness = await Harness.open(storage, {\n' +
    '\tmodels,\n' +
    '\tregistry,\n' +
    '\tenv: ({ cwd }) => new NodeExecutionEnv({ cwd: cwd ?? process.cwd() }),\n' +
    '}, context);\n' +
    '```\n' +
    '\n' +
    "A throw from `env` becomes the call's error result. Without an environment, the built-in tools fail with an error result. A fresh environment object per call is fine: `edit` and `write` serialize changes to one file by the environment's `id` and path. A custom `ExecutionEnv` sets `id` so that equal ids see the same files at the same paths, for example one id per container.\n" +
    '\n' +
    "Hosts can use the environment directly too, for example to show a project's files. `openBinaryReader()` reads byte ranges of one opened file, `openDirReader()` pages a directory, and `exec()` with an argv array runs a program without a shell, reporting which stream each output chunk came from:\n" +
    '\n' +
    '```typescript\n' +
    'const status = { stdout: "", stderr: "" };\n' +
    'await env.exec(["git", "status", "--porcelain=v2", "-z"], {\n' +
    '\tonOutput: (text, _context, { stream }) => {\n' +
    '\t\tstatus[stream] += text;\n' +
    '\t},\n' +
    '}, context);\n' +
    '```\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Abort the context to stop one call; `cleanup()` is for shutting the environment down. A custom environment can check itself with `registerEnvConformance()` from `@earendil-works/pi-durable/testing`, like storage below.\n' +
    '\n' +
    "Some environments also implement the optional `listFiles()`: the files and directories below a directory at any depth, as `fd` lists them, skipping what git ignores and stopping at bounds with `truncated`. `NodeExecutionEnv` does not; pi-env's `RemoteExecutionEnv` and `LocalExecutionEnv` do. Callers fall back to their own walk when the method is missing or fails with `not_supported`:\n" +
    '\n' +
    '```typescript\n' +
    'const listing = await env.listFiles?.(".", { exclude: ["node_modules"], maxEntries: 50_000 }, context);\n' +
    '```\n' +
    '\n' +
    '## Reload\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Installing an extension with an installed name replaces i',
  storage: '\n' +
    '## Storage\n' +
    '\n' +
    '| Backend | Import | Notes |\n' +
    '|---|---|---|\n' +
    '| Memory | `MemoryStorage` from the package root | Nothing is persisted. |\n' +
    '| IndexedDB | `IndexedDbStorage.open(name)` from `@earendil-works/pi-durable/storage/indexeddb` | Browser-only storage in one IndexedDB database. |\n' +
    '| SQLite | `openNodeSqliteStorage(file)` from `@earendil-works/pi-durable/storage/sqlite/node` | One database file. WAL mode with `synchronous = NORMAL`: commits survive process crashes; the newest may be lost on power or host failure. |\n' +
    '| JSONL | `openNodeJsonlStorage(directory, context)` from `@earendil-works/pi-durable/storage/jsonl/node` | Append-only files in one directory. Pass `{ fsync: true }` to flush before each commit marker, `{ readOnly: true }` to view a directory another process writes. Keeps the whole history in memory too, so memory grows with it; use SQLite for long-running agents. |\n' +
    '| Cloudflare Durable Object | `openDurableObjectSqliteStorage(ctx.storage)` from `@earendil-works/pi-durable/storage/sqlite/cloudflare` | The SQLite storage of one SQLite-backed Durable Object; commits are its storage transactions. |\n' +
    '\n' +
    'In a browser, open IndexedDB storage with `await IndexedDbStorage.open(name)`. One owner must hold the database at a\n' +
    'time; use a [Web Lock](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Web_Locks_API) around its lifetime rather than opening\n' +
    'it in competing tabs or workers. Call `await navigator.storage.persist()` when durable retention matters.\n' +
    '\n' +
    'SQLite storage can namespace its tables and indexes when sharing a database: pass `{ prefix: "pi_" }` to\n' +
    '`SqliteStorage.open(database, options)`, `openNodeSqliteStorage(path, options)`, or\n' +
    '`openDurableObjectSqliteStorage(ctx.storage, options)`. Storage renders the prefixed names into its SQL, so adapters\n' +
    'need no support. A prefix must be a SQLite identifier and cannot begin with `sqlite_`; a host may reserve more, such\n' +
    'as `_cf_` in Durable Objects. Changing the prefix does not migrate existing data.\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Multiple Pi storages opened through the Cloudflare adapter with the same storage object automatically share an\n' +
    'operation queue. To share the database with host tables, create an adapter and use it for both Pi and all host queries;\n' +
    'direct storage calls bypass the queue and may be rolled back with a Pi transaction:\n' +
    '\n' +
    '```typescript\n' +
    'const database = new DurableObjectSqliteDatabase(ctx.storage);\n' +
    'const piStorage = await SqliteStorage.open(database, { prefix: "pi_" });\n' +
    'await database.exec("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS host_notes (text TEXT)");\n' +
    'await database.run("INSERT INTO host_notes (text) VALUES (?)", text);\n' +
    '```\n' +
    '\n' +
    'One process writes a storage at a time; there is no cross-process locking. Opening JSONL storage writes too: it truncates torn lines and unconfirmed sidecar records, and removes sidecar records later commits made unnecessary. A viewer of a directory another process writes therefore opens it with `{ readOnly: true }`: that open writes nothing, skips the same records in memory, holds the state committed at open',
  code: '\n' +
    '## Code Mode\n' +
    '\n' +
    "`@earendil-works/pi-durable/codemode` adds a `codemode` tool: the model writes JavaScript that calls the conversation's tools as `await tools.<name>(args)`, in a QuickJS sandbox (`@earendil-works/pi-codemode`). Each call is a nested tool call, and only the script's output reaches the model. The script survives a restart: it resumes where it was, without running its finished calls again.\n" +
    '\n' +
    '```typescript\n' +
    'import { CodemodeSandbox } from "@earendil-works/pi-codemode";\n' +
    'import { createCodemodeExtension } from "@earendil-works/pi-durable/codemode";\n' +
    '\n' +

    '```\n' +
    '\n' +
    "The extension also adds a `codemode` prompt section listing the tools scripts can call, as TypeScript declarations within a token budget; scripts find the others with `searchTools()`, `describeTool()`, and `describeNamespace()`. Group tools into namespaces by declaring one on the extension that brings them, `namespace: { name, description, instructions? }`, for example one extension per MCP server: the section lists every selected extension's namespace with its one-line description (also before it has tools), and `describeNamespace()` returns its instructions. The result reads like the coding agent's: a header, the script's output, and on failure the calls already made; text past `max_output_tokens` is cut, with the full text in a temp file. Scripts also get `models.*`: the model catalog, `models.classify()`, and `models.generateImages()`, which run as nested calls of internal tools (`models: false` turns them off). On Cloudflare, pass a `RemoteCodemodeSandbox` instead. Closing the sandbox while a script runs (for example when shutting down) is not an outcome: the script resumes with the next proc",
  watch: '\n' +
    '## Watching a Conversation\n' +
    '\n' +
    "Everything a UI needs is committed state. `watch()` returns a watch of the conversation's structural view: its value at attachment, then each commit that touches it, with the Chord operations of that commit, one callback at a time:\n" +
    '\n' +
    '```typescript\n' +
    'const watch = await root.watch(context);\n' +
    'render(watch.value); // the state at attachment\n' +
    'watch.start(async (call) => {\n' +
    `\tif (call.kind !== "value") return; // Durable's watches end on a failure; they never send a failed call\n` +
    '\tconst { value, ops } = call;\n' +
    '\t// value.entries: a window over the transcript, newest last; value.before: the entry just before it\n' +
    '\t// value.docs["pi.live"]: the run, the running generation (streamed partial, retry, deferred), tool calls (output,\n' +
    '\t//   details), compactions, and why the last run ended without an answer (runFailure)\n' +
    '\t// value.docs["pi.inbox"], value.docs["pi.usage"], value.docs["pi.agent"], value.docs["pi.provider"]\n' +
    '\trender(value);\n' +
    '\tawait send(ops); // for example to a remote client that applies them\n' +
    '});\n' +
    '// later: await watch.stop();\n' +
    '```\n' +
    '\n' +
    "The view's `entries` are a window, so neither the first value nor a reconnect costs the whole transcript. A watch starts with the newest 50 entries; new entries are appended, and once the window would hold more than 100, its oldest leave in one splice, leaving the newest 50. `watch(context, { min, max })` changes the bounds. `from` picks where the first value starts (as `transcript.resume` does after a drop); every entry committed after the watch attached is appended, so a `from` past the newest entry starts empty and receives what comes next. Compaction summaries and resets are entries like any other, in place; a summary's `head` says where the entries it summarizes end. `conversation.context()` gives the active transcript the model sees.\n" +
    '\n' +
    '`ConversationTranscript` keeps what a client has seen beyond the window: call `merge()` with every value of the view, and render the `items` it returns, the client\'s whole transcript with a "load earlier" marker at the top and a "load more" gap wherever the client missed entries, after a stall or a reconnect:\n' +
    '\n' +
    '```typescript\n' +
    'import { ConversationTranscript } from "@earendil-works/pi-durable";\n' +
    '\n' +
    'const transcript = new ConversationTranscript((query, limit, ctx) => root.entries(query, limit, undefined, ctx));\n' +
    'const watch = await root.watch(context);\n' +
    'render(transcript.merge(watch.value));\n' +
    'watch.start(async (call) => {\n' +
    '\tif (call.kind === "value") render(transcript.merge(call.value));\n' +
    '})',
  design: '\n' +
    '## Design Documents\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- [`docs/spec.md`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/durable/docs/spec.md): the normative specification\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Benchmarks: `npm run bench:storage`, `npm run bench:storage:memory`, `npm run bench:tool-output`, and `npm run bench:nested-tools`.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '## License\n' +
    '\n' +
    'MIT\n',
  busy: '\n' +
    '## Busy Conversations\n' +
    '\n' +
    'A conversation is busy while a run is working on an input. Submitting to a busy conversation queues the submission in the conversation\'s inbox, `docs["pi.inbox"]` in the view:\n' +
    '\n' +
    '```typescript\n' +
    'await root.submit({ type: "input", content: "Also run the tests" }, context); // follow-up (default)\n' +
    'await root.submit({ type: "input", content: "Use pnpm, not npm", whenBusy: "steer" }, context);\n' +

    'await root.submit({ type: "write", entry: { kind: "app.note", data: "user opened a file" } }, context);\n' +

    '- **Steers** are placed after the current tool round and join the running work.\n' +
    '- **Follow-ups** are placed when the run answers, and start the next run.\n' +
    '- **`whenIdle: "reject"`** refuses an input when no run is working, so it never starts a run of its own. With `whenBusy: "steer"`, it steers the current run or throws `ConversationIdle`. A run that answered and waits for its [after-run tasks](#work-at-the-en',

While scheduling runs, a timer resumes sleeping tasks when they are due and keeps a Node.js process alive meanwhile.

A host whose process can be evicted, such as a Cloudflare Durable Object, wakes it itself. With `onWake`, the Harness arms no timer for sleeps; it tells the host what `harness.wake()` says whenever that changes: `active` while some task can run now or is running, and `at`, the earliest sleep. # Pi

Pi is a minimal, extensible agent harness that you can make your own.

Adapt Pi to your workflows, not the other way around. Customize Pi with [extensions](docs/extensions.md), [skills](docs/skills.md), [prompt templates](docs/prompt-templates.md), and [themes](docs/themes.md). Bundle them as [Pi packages](docs/packages.md) and share via npm or git.

Pi ships with powerful defaults but skips features like sub-agents and plan mode. Ask Pi to build what you want, or install a package that does it your way.

Use Pi [interactively](docs/usage.md), automate it in [print or JSON mode](docs/cli.md), control it over [RPC](docs/rpc.md), or build apps with the [Pi TypeScript SDK](docs/sdk.md). See [OpenClaw](https://github.com/OpenClaw/OpenClaw) for a real-world integration.

<result>tentacles runs the pi-durable `Harness` inside one Cloudflare Durable Object per session. A local pi or Claude Code plugin reaches it through an HTTP API and a WebSocket, using tools that call a helper CLI. The agent loop, its state and its tools all run remotely; nothing of a remote agent runs on the developer's machine.

Docs paths are under `/home/agus/workspace/asermax/tentacles/docs/`. Code paths are under `/home/agus/workspace/asermax/tentacles/`.

**1. Parts and connections**
- **Plugin** (`apps/plugin`, one source built into the pi package `@asermax/pi-tentacles` and a Claude plugin; `technical-design/plugin.md:11,56-60`).
  - Harness glue is a pi extension (`src/pi/extension.ts`) or a Claude mod (`src/claude/engine.ts`). It registers one tool per action: spawn, prompt, messages, list, close, answer, plus wait on pi only.
  - The helper CLI (`src/helper/*`) runs one process per command. A `watch` process holds one WebSocket per open session.
- **Worker** (`packages/provider-cloudflare/src/worker.ts`).
  - The only entry point. It serves the `/api` HTTP API (`packages/worker-api/src/api.ts:5`) behind a `TENTACLES_API_KEY` check (`worker.ts:72-86`), and also the preview route and a cron trigger.
  - The plugin-facing calls are create, prompt, answer, close, messages, status and list, plus a per-session socket (`technical-design/worker-api.md:11-24`). Payloads are JSON, and create carries base64 gzip-tar archives for skills, agents and context, up to 5 MB each (`worker-api.md:40-44`).
  - The socket sends one construct, the session state (status, settings, skill and agent names, question, failure, last entry), on connect and on every change (`worker-api.md:56`).
- **Registry Durable Object** (`registry-object.ts`, `packages/sql-registry`). It holds one entry per session (id, name, parent harness and id, status, `last_stopped`, settings, preview token). It serves list and preview lookups and feeds the daily cleanup (`sessions.md:136-140`).
- **Session Durable Object** (`session-object.ts:51`). It is keyed by session id and fills five contracts: SessionHost, SessionStorage, WakeTimer, ParentChannel and Workspace (`providers/cloudflare/deploy.md:73`). It reports each status change to the registry.
- **Workspace container**: a Cloudflare Computer container running computerd, started on the first command sent to it.
- **Shared Claude container** (`claude-object.ts`, `apps/claude-relay`): one container for all sessions, running pi-claude-code's relay and the claude CLI. It stops 15 minutes after the last call (`claude-object.ts:16`).
- **Other parts**: Codemode Worker (QuickJS sandbox Durable Object), Browser Run for previews, AI Gateway for non-Claude models, and a cron trigger (`deploy.md:75-107`).
- **Contracts**: the provider-neutral roles live in `packages/contracts/src/*`. A provider fills each one (`technical-design/runtime-components.md:64-83`).

**2. Agent loop, state, persistence, resume**
- The loop runs in the session Durable Object. `packages/core/src/session/session.ts:117` calls `Harness.open(storage, { models, registry, settings, onWake, env })`.
- State lives in pi-durable's SQLite tables inside that Durable Object (`session-object.ts:106`, `openDurableObjectSqliteStorage`). Conversations are pi-durable's own. tentacles adds a SESSION record, a questions document, and skills, agents and context documents (`sessions.md:62-134`). The workspace files live in the same SQLite (`providers/cloudflare/computer-workspace.md:35`).
- Status is derived from pi-durable state and is not a stored field (`sessions.md:131`, `core/src/session/state.ts`). The registry entry is a projection of it.
- Resume after an eviction goes through pi-durable's `onWake` and the Durable Object alarm (`session.ts:133`, `session-object.ts:216` `alarm: () => handle.wake()`). The alarm is reserved for pi-durable (`invariants.md:24`).
- Tools with `replay: "safe"` are rerun after an eviction. The workspace sets reads to safe and `write`, `edit`, `delete` and `exec` to unsafe (`workspace.md:98`, `computer-workspace.md:24`).
- A waiting question keeps its id across replays. `restartLimit` is `Infinity` while the question's call is live (`session.ts:127-131`), so it survives any number of evictions (`question-round-trip.md:50`).
- A daily cron deletes sessions whose last run stopped over a month ago, clearing the Durable Object storage and then the registry entry (`sessions.md:411-445`).

**3. Tools, dispatch, steer, question, collect**
- **Tool installation**: `packages/core/src/tools/extension.ts:55` installs pi-durable's `CodingTools`, codemode, the commit check, the preview tool, skills, context, agents and the root-only `ask_parent`. The `Workspace` contract's `create` returns pi-durable ToolRegistrations, each with its own `execute` (`workspace.md:98`).
- **Where the shell and filesystem are** (`computer-workspace.md:17-35`):
  - File tools work directly on the Durable Object's SQLite.
  - `exec` runs either on an isolate shell (just-bash in a Dynamic Worker, text tools and `git` only) or in the container. The container mounts `/workspace` through FUSE.
  - Only `/workspace` persists across a container stop.
  - Git clones and pushes from the Durable Object, and GitHub tokens are added outside the container, by the git client or the egress gateway.
- **Dispatch**: spawn packs the archives, calls create, and returns the session id once the first run has started (`worker-api.md:17`). A failed workspace setup leaves the session failed and returns the error.
- **Steer**: a prompt maps to a follow-up or a steer (`session.ts:264-282`). While a question waits, any prompt becomes a steer and is queued until the answer.
- **Question**: `ask_parent` stores the question and moves the session to waiting. The state goes over the socket to the helper `watch`, which wakes the parent with the session, question id and text. The parent calls the answer tool (`question-round-trip.md:38-48`).
- **Collect**: finish and failure wakes carry the last message or the failure (`plugin.md:83-89`). The messages tool returns the last N root-conversation entries. On pi, `tentacles_wait` blocks. Claude Code has no wait tool, because helper processes are capped at ten minutes (`plugin.md:78-79`).
- **Local list**: the plugin keeps a local session list, a pi session entry or a `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` file, and syncs it from the Worker at harness start (`plugin.md:101-136`).

**4. Trade-offs the docs name**
- There is no explicit comparison with pi-coding-agent, and the repo has no mention of it. The docs name these differences from a local agent:
  - Nothing runs locally. Parent-side state and output are reachable only through the tools (`plugin.md:62`).
  - Skills, agents and context are fixed at spawn. Context edits stay remote and never come back (`product-design/remote-agents.md:21-23`).
  - The isolate shell has no node or npm and returns output only when the command ends. The container has a cold start of about 1 to 3 seconds (`computer-workspace.md:21,30,92`).
  - A container stop loses running processes and anything outside `/workspace`, including mise runtimes (`computer-workspace.md:35`).
  - `npm install` was slower in the synced workspace: 11.4 s against 4.8 s on the container's disk (`computer-workspace.md:40`).
  - A headless `claude -p` parent never gets wakes (`plugin.md:98-99`).
  - Deleted sessions linger in the local list until the plugin learns of them (`plugin.md:141`).
  - Unpushed work is lost with the session a month after its last run (`remote-agents.md:66`).
  - Containers can be placed outside North America, and nothing enforces the region (`deploy.md:90-91`).
  - Cloudflare hosts every role in a single deploy. Mixing providers was considered and not taken (`runtime-components.md:112-113`).

I did not read `core/src/session/state.ts` or the plugin helper client in depth. The wire format of each call is in `packages/worker-api/src/sessions.ts`, which I did not open. The version of pi-durable is pinned at 1.5.1 (`pnpm-workspace.yaml:31`).</result>

<result>tentacles runs the pi-durable `Harness` inside one Cloudflare Durable Object per session. A local pi or Claude Code plugin reaches it through an HTTP API and a WebSocket, using tools that call a helper CLI. The agent loop, its state and its tools all run remotely; nothing of a remote agent runs on the developer's machine.

Docs paths are under `/home/agus/workspace/asermax/tentacles/docs/`. Code paths are under `/home/agus/workspace/asermax/tentacles/`.

**1. Parts and connections**
- **Plugin** (`apps/plugin`, one source built into the pi package `@asermax/pi-tentacles` and a Claude plugin; `technical-design/plugin.md:11,56-60`).
  - Harness glue is a pi extension (`src/pi/extension.ts`) or a Claude mod (`src/claude/engine.ts`). It registers one tool per action: spawn, prompt, messages, list, close, answer, plus wait on pi only.
  - The helper CLI (`src/helper/*`) runs one process per command. A `watch` process holds one WebSocket per open session.
- **Worker** (`packages/provider-cloudflare/src/worker.ts`).
  - The only entry point. It serves the `/api` HTTP API (`packages/worker-api/src/api.ts:5`) behind a `TENTACLES_API_KEY` check (`worker.ts:72-86`), and also the preview route and a cron trigger.
  - The plugin-facing calls are create, prompt, answer, close, messages, status and list, plus a per-session socket (`technical-design/worker-api.md:11-24`). Payloads are JSON, and create carries base64 gzip-tar archives for skills, agents and context, up to 5 MB each (`worker-api.md:40-44`).
  - The socket sends one construct, the session state (status, settings, skill and agent names, question, failure, last entry), on connect and on every change (`worker-api.md:56`).
- **Registry Durable Object** (`registry-object.ts`, `packages/sql-registry`). It holds one entry per session (id, name, parent harness and id, status, `last_stopped`, settings, preview token). It serves list and preview lookups and feeds the daily cleanup (`sessions.md:136-140`).
- **Session Durable Object** (`session-object.ts:51`). It is keyed by session id and fills five contracts: SessionHost, SessionStorage, WakeTimer, ParentChannel and Workspace (`providers/cloudflare/deploy.md:73`). It reports each status change to the registry.
- **Workspace container**: a Cloudflare Computer container running computerd, started on the first command sent to it.
- **Shared Claude container** (`claude-object.ts`, `apps/claude-relay`): one container for all sessions, running pi-claude-code's relay and the claude CLI. It stops 15 minutes after the last call (`claude-object.ts:16`).
- **Other parts**: Codemode Worker (QuickJS sandbox Durable Object), Browser Run for previews, AI Gateway for non-Claude models, and a cron trigger (`deploy.md:75-107`).
- **Contracts**: the provider-neutral roles live in `packages/contracts/src/*`. A provider fills each one (`technical-design/runtime-components.md:64-83`).

**2. Agent loop, state, persistence, resume**
- The loop runs in the session Durable Object. `packages/core/src/session/session.ts:117` calls `Harness.open(storage, { models, registry, settings, onWake, env })`.
- State lives in pi-durable's SQLite tables inside that Durable Object (`session-object.ts:106`, `openDurableObjectSqliteStorage`). Conversations are pi-durable's own. tentacles adds a SESSION record, a questions document, and skills, agents and context documents (`sessions.md:62-134`). The workspace files live in the same SQLite (`providers/cloudflare/computer-workspace.md:35`).
- Status is derived from pi-durable state and is not a stored field (`sessions.md:131`, `core/src/session/state.ts`). The registry entry is a projection of it.
- Resume after an eviction goes through pi-durable's `onWake` and the Durable Object alarm (`session.ts:133`, `session-object.ts:216` `alarm: () => handle.wake()`). The alarm is reserved for pi-durable (`invariants.md:24`).
- Tools with `replay: "safe"` are rerun after an eviction. The workspace sets reads to safe and `write`, `edit`, `delete` and `exec` to unsafe (`workspace.md:98`, `computer-workspace.md:24`).
- A waiting question keeps its id across replays. `restartLimit` is `Infinity` while the question's call is live (`session.ts:127-131`), so it survives any number of evictions (`question-round-trip.md:50`).
- A daily cron deletes sessions whose last run stopped over a month ago, clearing the Durable Object storage and then the registry entry (`sessions.md:411-445`).

**3. Tools, dispatch, steer, question, collect**
- **Tool installation**: `packages/core/src/tools/extension.ts:55` installs pi-durable's `CodingTools`, codemode, the commit check, the preview tool, skills, context, agents and the root-only `ask_parent`. The `Workspace` contract's `create` returns pi-durable ToolRegistrations, each with its own `execute` (`workspace.md:98`).
- **Where the shell and filesystem are** (`computer-workspace.md:17-35`):
  - File tools work directly on the Durable Object's SQLite.
  - `exec` runs either on an isolate shell (just-bash in a Dynamic Worker, text tools and `git` only) or in the container. The container mounts `/workspace` through FUSE.
  - Only `/workspace` persists across a container stop.
  - Git clones and pushes from the Durable Object, and GitHub tokens are added outside the container, by the git client or the egress gateway.
- **Dispatch**: spawn packs the archives, calls create, and returns the session id once the first run has started (`worker-api.md:17`). A failed workspace setup leaves the session failed and returns the error.
- **Steer**: a prompt maps to a follow-up or a steer (`session.ts:264-282`). While a question waits, any prompt becomes a steer and is queued until the answer.
- **Question**: `ask_parent` stores the question and moves the session to waiting. The state goes over the socket to the helper `watch`, which wakes the parent with the session, question id and text. The parent calls the answer tool (`question-round-trip.md:38-48`).
- **Collect**: finish and failure wakes carry the last message or the failure (`plugin.md:83-89`). The messages tool returns the last N root-conversation entries. On pi, `tentacles_wait` blocks. Claude Code has no wait tool, because helper processes are capped at ten minutes (`plugin.md:78-79`).
- **Local list**: the plugin keeps a local session list, a pi session entry or a `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` file, and syncs it from the Worker at harness start (`plugin.md:101-136`).

**4. Trade-offs the docs name**
- There is no explicit comparison with pi-coding-agent, and the repo has no mention of it. The docs name these differences from a local agent:
  - Nothing runs locally. Parent-side state and output are reachable only through the tools (`plugin.md:62`).
  - Skills, agents and context are fixed at spawn. Context edits stay remote and never come back (`product-design/remote-agents.md:21-23`).
  - The isolate shell has no node or npm and returns output only when the command ends. The container has a cold start of about 1 to 3 seconds (`computer-workspace.md:21,30,92`).
  - A container stop loses running processes and anything outside `/workspace`, including mise runtimes (`computer-workspace.md:35`).
  - `npm install` was slower in the synced workspace: 11.4 s against 4.8 s on the container's disk (`computer-workspace.md:40`).
  - A headless `claude -p` parent never gets wakes (`plugin.md:98-99`).
  - Deleted sessions linger in the local list until the plugin learns of them (`plugin.md:141`).
  - Unpushed work is lost with the session a month after its last run (`remote-agents.md:66`).
  - Containers can be placed outside North America, and nothing enforces the region (`deploy.md:90-91`).
  - Cloudflare hosts every role in a single deploy. Mixing providers was considered and not taken (`runtime-components.md:112-113`).

I did not read `core/src/session/state.ts` or the plugin helper client in depth. The wire format of each call is in `packages/worker-api/src/sessions.ts`, which I did not open. The version of pi-durable is pinned at 1.5.1 (`pnpm-workspace.yaml:31`).</result>

<result># Pi Durable (`@earendil-works/pi-durable`): report

Today is 2026-11-23. All facts below come from primary sources unless marked otherwise. I ran no trial; everything is read from source and documentation.

Two corrections to the premise:
- The announcement is dated 2026-10-01 and was published together with Pi 1.0.
- I found no Cloudflare-authored post. "pi-durable on Cloudflare" is the Earendil repo `earendil-works/pi-durable-cloudflare`.

## 1. What it is

- Pi Durable is an experimental harness framework for long-running, durable agents that run anywhere there is a JavaScript runtime. The announcement says it "does not replace the Pi coding agent". It is a framework for building any agentic application, coding agents included. (docs: https://earendil.com/posts/pi-durable/ and https://earendil.com/posts/pi-1-0/)
- Version: 1.6.0, released 2026-11-20 (npm registry, https://registry.npmjs.org/@earendil-works/pi-durable). It is MIT licensed and the repo was pushed on 2026-11-23. The README says "Experimental. The API changes without notice between releases." (source: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/tree/main/packages/durable)
- Pi packages it reuses:
  - It depends on `@earendil-works/pi-ai` for model access, which is the same package the coding agent uses.
  - It depends on `@earendil-works/chord` (document state and operations), `pi-schema`, `pi-codemode` and `pi-telemetry`.
  - The announcement says it shares the coding agent's TUI components in the demos.
- What it replaces or bypasses: the package list has no `pi-agent-core`. Durable has its own `Harness`, task scheduler and storage layer. It ships its own read, write, edit and bash tools (`CodingTools`). The announcement shows no use of `pi-coding-agent`; its demos live inside that package under `experimental/`, borrowing its TUI.

## 2. Architecture

- **Terms** (announcement):
  - Harness: storage plus the machinery to run conversations in parallel.
  - Conversation: a transcript of immutable entries.
  - Agent: a model plus its settings and tools.
  - Task: everything the harness runs, from model calls to tool calls.
  - Execution environment: where tools do their work.
- **Where the loop runs.** In the process that owns the storage. "One process owns a storage at a time, and other clients attach to that process." There is no cross-process locking (README, Storage). Read-only viewers can open the same storage with `readOnly: true`.
- **State and persistence.**
  - Every change goes through atomic commits. Nothing is shown before its commit is stored. A commit can write entries, documents and tasks together.
  - Documents are typed JSON next to the transcript. Built-in documents are `pi.agent`, `pi.live`, `pi.inbox`, `pi.usage` and `pi.provider`.
  - Storage backends are memory, IndexedDB, SQLite, JSONL and a Cloudflare Durable Object SQLite backend.
  - SQLite uses WAL with `synchronous = NORMAL`. Commits survive process crashes, but the newest may be lost on power or host failure.
  - JSONL keeps the whole history in memory, so the README says to use SQLite for long-running agents.
  - Older messages always stay in storage, even after compaction.
- **Crash recovery.**
  - Each task is a durable state machine that saves a checkpoint at every step. A new process opens the storage, finds unfinished tasks and calls `harness.resume()`.
  - A cut-off model request is re-sent, and the partial answer stays in the transcript marked aborted. A request that keeps killing the process eventually ends.
  - A cut-off tool call reruns only if the tool declares `replay: "safe"`. Otherwise the model is told the call was interrupted, along with the output stored so far.
  - A `requestId` on a submission makes it exactly-once.
  - Hooks that make decisions store them in a `memo`, where the first write wins.
- **Tool execution.**
  - Each tool call is its own task, and its intent is stored before it runs.
  - Tools reach files and shell through an `ExecutionEnv`. The `env` function runs per tool call, so each conversation can use a different directory, container, remote VM or in-memory sandbox.
  - Shipped: `NodeExecutionEnv` for local files. The README mentions pi-env's `RemoteExecutionEnv` and `LocalExecutionEnv`.
  - Codemode runs model-written JavaScript in a QuickJS sandbox (`pi-codemode`) that can also resume after a restart. On Cloudflare you pass a `RemoteCodemodeSandbox`.
  - The README does not document a built-in permission or approval system. The announcement shows an approval hook written as an extension (blocks `deploy`, asks in Slack).
- **Client connection.**
  - `conversation.watch()` returns the current view first, then each commit as Chord operations. These are "small enough to send over a socket", and you wire the transport yourself.
  - `watchEvents()` converts commits into the coding agent's event shapes, at the cost of more bytes on the wire.
  - The view holds a window of the newest 50 entries. `ConversationTranscript` handles reconnects and "load earlier".
  - A late-joining or reconnecting client starts from the current view.
  - I found no standard wire protocol. The Cloudflare example defines its own in `src/protocol.ts`.
- **Background and long-running work.**
  - Tasks are foreground by default, so Esc or an abort stops them and everything they own.
  - A background task (`ownership: { kind: "conversation" }, background: true`) lets the conversation go idle while it runs, and an ordinary abort leaves it alone. The announcement gives a subagent and a reminder that fires tomorrow as examples.
  - Tasks and conversations form one ownership tree, and aborts run bottom-up.
  - Sleeps are stored (`runtime.sleepUntil`) and hold no invocation while waiting.
  - Compaction is a task that runs in the background while the conversation continues. `reset()` and handoff start a new context.
  - Subagents are not built in. A tool creates a child conversation it owns.
- **Multiple clients and conversations.**
  - Any number of clients can attach to any conversation, and any client can steer.
  - Submitting to a busy conversation queues it in `pi.inbox`. `whenBusy: "steer"` joins the running work after the current tool round. A follow-up starts the next run.
  - One harness runs many conversations concurrently. A conversation can fork at any entry and sees the parent's history without copying it.

## 3. Differences from pi-coding-agent

The coding-agent side comes from https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/tree/main/packages/coding-agent and the Pi 1.0 post. I did not re-verify the JSONL session tree or the four-tool default in the coding-agent docs, so those items are your premise, not confirmed here.

| Aspect | Pi coding agent | Pi Durable (source) |
|---|---|---|
| Process model | "Runs on your (remote) machine, inside a terminal, driven by one person. If the process dies, you look at what happened and tell it to continue." | Process death is resumed automatically from checkpoints. Multiple humans can steer the same agents. |
| Session state | Your premise: JSONL tree | Entries, documents and tasks in pluggable storage (SQLite, Durable Object, etc.) with atomic commits. JSONL is one optional backend. Forks share parent history. |
| Core package | `pi-agent-core` loop | A separate `Harness` and task scheduler. |
| Tools | Your premise: four tools | Built-ins are `CodingTools` (read, write, edit, bash), plus codemode and tool search. Each conversation selects its own tool set. Each call is a durable task with a `replay` declaration. |
| Extensions | Your premise: in-process, full permissions | An extension is a named bundle of prompt sections, tools, hooks, tasks and documents. Conversations store extension names, never code. Extensions can be hot-replaced without stopping the agent. Hooks participate in durability. |
| UI | TUI (`pi-tui`) | No UI is built in. UIs attach through `watch()`. Demos reuse the coding agent's TUI components. |
| Subagents | The coding-agent README says it skips them | Not built in. A few lines of tool code build one. |
| Where tools run | Local machine | The execution-environment interface allows the harness on one machine and tools on another. |

## 4. Stated trade-offs

- **Gains** (announcement): runs anywhere, long conversations through compaction, crash survival, multi-client steering, and malleability. The source is about 15,000 lines without tests, which Earendil gives as about 150k to 250k tokens, so an agent can read it.
- **Costs and limits** (stated):
  - It is experimental and the API may change.
  - One process owns a storage, with no cross-process locking.
  - Recovery re-sends cut-off model requests, which costs tokens.
  - Non-idempotent tools must be written with replay semantics in mind. A tool without `replay: "safe"` is never rerun after a crash.
  - A phase reruns from its top after a restart, so work after a wait must go in the next phase.
  - SQLite can lose the newest commits on power or host failure.
  - The `watchEvents()` compatibility layer costs more bytes than operations.
  - Storage conformance suites and benchmarks ship in the package, but I found no published latency numbers.
- **Not documented:** latency overhead, a security or permission model, and infrastructure cost comparisons. The announcement does not name them as trade-offs. The Cloudflare sample says it has "no authentication or rate limiting" and warns to add both before exposing a deployment.

## 5. Cloudflare deployment

Source: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-durable-cloudflare, repo pushed 2026-11-10, depends on pi-durable 1.5.2.
- One SQLite-backed Durable Object class, `Session`, holds the harness. Commits are DO storage transactions (`openDurableObjectSqliteStorage(ctx.storage)`). The README states that "multiple Pi storages opened through the Cloudflare adapter with the same storage object automatically share an operation queue."
- Wake-up after eviction uses the `onWake` option. The harness arms no timers, and the host keeps a DO alarm armed from `harness.wake()` and calls `resume()` when it fires. The sample keeps a 60-second heartbeat alarm while work can run.
- Clients connect over Cloudflare hibernating WebSockets. Each socket watches one conversation, receiving a first value and then Chord operations. A React client applies them. Each connection is tagged with a username for multiplayer.
- The sample has features for forks, scheduled and recurring follow-ups, a search subagent, and an Activity view of live task ownership.
- There is no Cloudflare Sandbox or container in the sample. I found no `env` or Sandbox usage in `src/chat.ts`, and `wrangler.jsonc` binds only the Durable Object. The pi-durable README mentions only `RemoteCodemodeSandbox` for Cloudflare. Remote tool execution is possible through the `ExecutionEnv` interface but is not demonstrated.
- `wrangler.jsonc` enables observability and traces. The package emits telemetry spans (`pi.durable.phase`, etc.) through `pi-telemetry`.

## 6. Terminology and diagrams worth reusing

- The announcement has the harness definition quoted in section 2 and the "durable harness" framing. The Pi 1.0 post says "Pi must become more durable."
- Terms: conversation, entry, commit, document, task, submission, steer vs follow-up, ownership tree, background task, `replay: "safe"`, memo, checkpoint, extension, execution environment.
- Slack channel and thread analogy for forks: a channel is one conversation, and a thread is a fork at the message it replies to.
- Checkout example: split payments with fail-fast abort and refund.
- The announcement has a vacation-planner demo recording (restart mid-run, where only the unfinished search reruns). I found no architecture diagram.
- The normative spec is at https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/durable/docs/spec.md. I did not read it.

## Related repos by Earendil, not confirmed as part of pi-durable's design

- `earendil-works/dquickts`: QuickJS with durable execution that snapshots the whole heap and resumes it in another process.
- `earendil-works/gondolin`: a Linux microvm sandbox with a TypeScript control plane.
- `earendil-works/absurd`: "An experiment in durability".
- Third-party projects built on Pi Durable exist, such as `disler/durable-pi` and `HazAT/ultimate` (secondary, from GitHub search).

## Not verified

- The "Mario writes in more detail" post. Its link is on the Pi 1.0 page, but I did not locate or read it. The searches of mariozechner.at and lucumr.pocoo.org found no pi-durable article. Armin's "What is Codemode" post exists, but I did not read it.
- The spec at `docs/spec.md`, the 30-plus examples, and the actual protocol file `src/protocol.ts` in the Cloudflare repo.

content.text:
I added decisions 7 and 8 to the log, and drew the talk storyboard and the pi-durable research on the canvas.

- **Storyboard** (under the talk column): one frame for each of the talk's 15 slides, plus one for each of its 3 demos. Each frame has a sketch of the slide and a caption with the idea it carries, what's on screen, and its planned time. Frames reused in the Session 5 INSTRUCTOR, or out of date (the comparison table says Pi has no MCP), are marked. You can move them around freely.
- **Length**: `pi-talk.md` planned the talk at about 31 minutes: 28 of content plus 3 of questions. You remembered 45 to 60. How long it ran on the day isn't recorded anywhere.
- **Pi-durable research** (under the Session 6 column):
  - **Framing**: Earendil's announcement says pi-durable "does not replace the Pi coding agent". It's a framework for building agent applications, and coding agents are one kind. That conflicts with decision 8 calling it an alternative, so the first new card asks how to frame it.
  - **Comparison diagram**: it shows the two side by side, drawn from the sources. Pi-coding-agent is one process on your machine with a local JSONL session file. Pi-durable shares the same `pi-ai` but has its own Harness instead of `pi-agent-core`. Its storage is pluggable, its tasks save checkpoints and resume after a crash, any number of clients can watch and steer a conversation, and tools run in an execution environment that can be a different machine.
  - **Facts**: everything else comes from Earendil's announcement, README and Cloudflare sample, as read by a research subagent; nobody ran pi-durable. Facts from your vault notes are added.
  - **Tentacles**: a grey card shows how tentacles uses pi-durable, marked as reference only and not for the slides. Each session is one Durable Object running the harness, resumed by its wake alarm, with tools in a workspace container. The plugin talks to it over HTTP plus one WebSocket per session.
  - **New ❓ cards**: how to frame pi-durable, where it goes in the storyboard, and which differences become slides.

The canvas is still at http://localhost:5191, and I'm watching it for your sticky notes and voice messages.

Read the primary sources and report facts with URLs, no recommendations:
1. In Earendil's pi-durable (github.com/earendil-works/pi, packages/durable: README.md and docs/spec.md), what are the lifecycle phases or states of a model request task and of a tool call task? What gets committed to storage at each step (intent before running, partial output, result), and what happens on resume at each step (re-send, replay: "safe", interrupted notice)? Quote the state names the spec uses.
2. What a "commit" contains and how entries, tasks and documents relate in storage (one paragraph).
3. How defineTask phases, runtime.sleepUntil and signals work, in one short paragraph each.
4. In the Pi coding agent (packages/coding-agent docs: session-format.md / sessions.md), how a session is stored: the JSONL entry types, id/parentId tree, when entries are appended, and what happens to an in-flight turn if the process dies.
5. pi-durable's ExecutionEnv interface: its methods, NodeExecutionEnv, and pi-env's RemoteExecutionEnv / LocalExecutionEnv, and whether the env can change between tool calls of one conversation.
6. The watch()/watchEvents() and submit() API surface for multiple clients: method names, whenBusy values, what a late client receives.
Mark anything you couldn't find in a primary source.

# Durable specification

`@earendil-works/pi-durable` is a durable, extensible agent harness. This document is normative.
It uses existing package types as follows:

```ts
import type { Context } from "@earendil-works/chord/context";
import type { Draft, Op } from "@earendil-works/chord/delta";
import type { JsonRepresentation, JsonValue } from "@earendil-works/chord/json";
import type { WatchCall, WatchEnd, WatchHandle } from "@earendil-works/chord/watch";
import type {
  AssistantMessage,
  CacheRetention,
  DeferredHandle,
  Message,
  Models,
  ModelThinkingLevel,
  TextContent,
  Tool,
  ToolCall,
  ToolReference,
  ToolResultMessage,
  Transport,
  UserMessage,
} from "@earendil-works/pi-ai";
import type { ExecutionEnv } from "@earendil-works/pi-durable/env";

type JsonObject = { [key: string]: JsonValue };
type TaskOutcomeError = { message: string; detail?: JsonValue };
```

Durable targets the transcript `SystemMessage` contract from pi-ai PR
[#9548](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9548). `Message` includes that
type once the PR lands.

The core rule is:

> A Session atomically commits immutable entries, full task records, and
> Chord-tracked documents. Only committed state is observable. A commit marked
> deferred may be observed before it is stored (section 4.1).

## 1. Terms and invariants

- A **Session** owns one mutation line, conversations, entries, tasks,
  submissions, and documents.
- A **conversation** is a transcript scope. It may fork another conversation.
- An **entry** is an immutable transcript record.
- A **task** is a durable state machine attached to one conversation.
- A **document** is mutable JSON state represented by Chord operations and
  occasional complete bases.
- A **definition** is a typed token describing one document or document family.
- A **source** exposes committed document changes to Chord without exposing a
  mutable object.
- A **turn** is one assistant response and the tool calls it makes. A **run**
  is the sequence of turns from an admitted input to the final answer; turn
  boundaries (section 6) sit between its turns. A conversation is busy while a
  run is active.

Required invariants:

1. One Session commit is atomic across all record and document writes.
2. A stored commit is published once Storage made it durable, after the
   storage call that stored it settled, in line order (section 4), also when
   that call then rejects; a commit that fails before it is durable publishes
   nothing. Once the Session has failed, nothing more is published: a commit
   whose call settles after another error failed the Session, or whose turn to
   be published comes after that, is durable but unpublished, and reopening
   recovers it (section 10.1). A deferred commit (section 4.1) is published to watches and the
   conversation view when memory adopts it, once the commits before it are
   published, and to `observeCommits()` once it is stored.
3. All visible progress is durable, except what a deferred commit holds: what
   watches see can be ahead of Storage by up to that commit's window
   (`withinMs`), and a crash loses it. A commit is deferred only when its caller
   marks it so, and only when it changes nothing but existing latest,
   initial-fork conversation documents (section 4.1). Every stored document is
   a state memory had.
4. External effects do not run inside the Session mutation transaction.
5. Entries and IDs are immutable and never reused after a committed write.
6. Document drafts are fully revoked when their transaction callback settles:
   the Session synchronously prepares or aborts every open change at that point.
   Values assigned into a draft are copied by value and must be strict JSON.
7. The mutation line runs one commit callback at a time; their storage
   overlaps (group commit, section 4). A callback never observes what an
   unpublished commit wrote: at its first read or write of such a key it waits
   until that commit is stored and published. Commits are published in line
   order, and every outcome is delivered in line order. Commit/close observers
   run synchronously only to capture immutable state; document-state and watch
   user callbacks run later, as microtasks the line never waits for.
8. A storage error is fatal to the open Session (section 10.1), which must be
   reopened. A commit it fails publishes nothing, unless Storage had already
   made it durable (a durability receipt). Preparation and checkpoint failures occur before
   storage admission and roll back normally.

## 2. Core records

The concrete JSON representations may add bookkeeping fields, but must preserve
these contracts.

```ts
declare const idBrand: unique symbol;

b:
## 8. Built-in tasks

The initial implementation provides:

| kind | responsibility |
|---|---|
| `pi.generation` | prepare system prompt and tools, request or poll model, retry, classify response |
| `pi.tool` | validate, hook, execute, persist output and details, append result |
| `pi.compaction` | select a transcript range, summarize, place a headed summary |

Generation uses `HarnessOptions.models` without a Durable-specific model adapter. It
resolves `models.getModel(ref.provider, ref.modelId)`, builds a pi-ai `Context`
from the prepared prompt/messages/tools, and calls `models.streamSimple()` with
the task invocation's abort signal, the agent's thinking level, and the
settings' stream options. Deferred
continuation calls `models.fetchDeferred()` and `models.cancelDeferred()` with
that same model and signal. Missing models and synchronous/streamed pi-ai errors
are classified into the durable generation outcomes below.

Generation and tool progress are throttled document commits, deferred
(section 4.1): watches see each at once, and Storage gets them with the next
commit that reads `pi.live` or within `settings.progress.persistWithinMs`
(default 1,000 ms). A crash may lose the throttle window plus what was not
stored yet: a stream that crashes before its first store leaves no aborted entry,
and that attempt's usage is not recorded. Recovery converts stored partials
to normal interrupted/aborted transcript entries, clears presentation state,
and then retries or terminates according to the task phase. Retry deadlines,
attempts, compaction, and tool progress are current document state for late
joiners; completed-attempt usage/accounting is an entry or terminal detail.
Truncation and spill paths are tool diagnostics (section 7.3).

Compaction changes model context by appending a summary entry with a head. It
does not delete transcript history.

### 8.1 Built-in entries

Built-in entry kinds carry no `data`, except `pi.tool-result`, whose token is
`Entry<{ diagnostics: ToolDiagnostic[] }>`; every tool result carries `data`,
with an empty list when it has no diagnostics (section 7.3), and
`pi.compaction`, whose token is `Entry<{ reason: CompactionReason }>`. Each kind
is exported as an `Entry` token.

| kind | `model` | written by |
|---|---|---|
| `pi.user` | `[UserMessage]`, timestamp from the Harness clock at admission or placement | submissions, `onYield` continuations |
| `pi.assistant` | `[AssistantMessage]` with any stop reason | generation |
| `pi.system` | `[SystemMessage]` with `content: ""` (section 7.4) | generation preparation |
| `pi.tool-result` | `[ToolResultMessage]` | tool tasks; generation for calls an aborted round never started |
| `pi.reset` | absent, or `[UserMessage]` with the handoff text; always `head: "self"` | `reset()`, generation `tools` phase for `handoff` |
| `pi.compaction` | `[UserMessage]` with the wrapped summary; `head` is the first kept entry | compaction tasks (section 8.7) |

Every generation response becomes a `pi.assistant` entry: answers, failed attempts
with their error text and usage, and converted partials with stop reason
`aborted`. Context derivation (section 2.1, rule 9) keeps failed and aborted
messages out of later requests, so no separate usage or notice kind exists.

### 8.2 Live document</result>

### 8.2 Live document

```ts
type LiveState = {
  /**
   * Run control (section 6); present exactly while the conversation is busy. `turns` counts the run's tool rounds,
   * which `AgentState.maxTurns` bounds (section 8.5); an `onYield` continuation starts it over (section 8.3).
   */
  run?: {
    taskId: TaskId;
    /** Placed inputs, settled when the run ends; `[]` once it answered and waits for its after-run tasks. */
    inputs: SubmissionId[];
    turns: number;
    /**
     * The run's first entry, where `afterRun` hooks start reading (section 8.3): the first one the boundary that
     * started it placed, a write's or an input's; a continue's `runFailure.first`; otherwise the run's first
     * tool-calling answer. A run started before it was recorded may lack it and gets its answer instead.
     */
    first?: EntryId;
    /** The run answered and waits for the tasks its `afterRun` hooks asked for, listed once created (section 8.3). */
    afterRun?: { tasks?: TaskId[] };
    /**
     * The answer's entry and the tasks an `onYield` hook asked for, while they decide whether it stands (section
     * 8.3); the inputs stay open meanwhile.
     */
    yield?: { answer: EntryId; tasks: TaskId[] };
  };
  /** Presentation of the current generation attempt. */
  generation?: {
    attempt: number;
    /** Committed throttled partial of the in-flight response. */
    message?: JsonRepresentation<AssistantMessage>;
    /** Durable backoff before the next attempt. */
    retry?: { at: number; error: string };
    /** Provider-side deferred response being polled. */
    deferred?: { pollAt: number };
  };
  /**
   * Nested calls of running tool calls (section 7.3), in creation order, so a parent precedes its children and task
   * IDs ascend.
   */
  nestedTools?: {
    /** `<parentCallId>/<key>`: the call's ID, unique because keys contain no `/`. */
    callId: string;
    parentCallId: string;
    /** The calling tool task, model-issued or nested; the Harness relates slots by task ID. */
    parentTaskId: TaskId;
    taskId: TaskId;
    name: string;
    /** The call's arguments, unbounded; once it executes, those it runs with, after repair, hooks, and coercion. */
    arguments: JsonObject;
    /** `sleeping` or `waiting` while the call is parked (section 8.4). */
    status: "pending" | "running" | "sleeping" | "waiting" | "done";
    output?: string;
    droppedBytes?: number;
    droppedLines?: number;
    details?: JsonValue;
    diagnostics?: ToolDiagnostic[];
    /** Once done: how the call ended, with up to 500 characters of error text; the result is not here (section 7.3). */
    summary?: { isError: boolean; durationMs?: number; usage?: Usage; error?: string };
  }[];
  /** The current tool round in call order, from the tool-calling answer until the generation's `tools` phase ends it. */
  tools?: {
    callId: string;
    name: string;
    /** Absent for a call not started yet (sequential round, `pending`). */
    taskId?: TaskId;

### 8.4 Tool

```ts
type ToolTaskInput =
  | { kind: "model"; assistant: EntryId; callId: string }
  | { kind: "nested"; parent: TaskId; parentCallId: string; key: string; call: ToolCall; progress?: false };
type ToolTaskCheckpoint =
  | { phase: "call" }
  /** Intent: `execute()` runs in the phase that commits it; reached as a phase only by recovery. */
  | { phase: "execute"; arguments: JsonObject; replay: "safe" | "unsafe"; wake?: WakeReason; checkpoint?: JsonValue }
  /** The call is parked; its `sleeping` or `waiting` state holds this checkpoint. */
  | { phase: "parked"; arguments: JsonObject; replay: "safe" | "unsafe"; checkpoint?: JsonValue };
type ToolTaskResult = { kind: "model"; entryId: EntryId; control?: ToolControl } | { kind: "nested" };
```

`pi.tool` is version 4 and starts at `{ phase: "call" }`; `migrate` gives a
version 1 input `kind: "model"` and keeps a version 2 input (version 3 added
`unoffered`) and older checkpoints (version 4 added `parked` and the optional
fields of `execute`), and readers treat a terminal result without `kind` as a
model-issued call's. A call flagged `unoffered` resolves no tool: `call` settles
it `tool_unavailable` and the abort handler does too. A model-issued call's input stays small
because the terminal record keeps it; the call is read from the assistant
entry. A nested call (section 7.3) carries its call, since no entry holds it,
and settles differently: its result commit records the result's `usage`
(section 8.6), writes its result for programs to the caller's
`NestedCallDoc` (section 7.3), marks its nested slot `done` with its
summary, appends no entry, and ends with `{ kind: "nested" }`; `control` does
not apply.
Below, `{ entryId }` is a model-issued call's result.

- `call` reads the call with `runtime.entry()`, resolves the tool among the
  phase's agent `tools` (section 7.3), validates
  the arguments with pi-ai
  `validateToolArguments()`, runs the `beforeTool` chain, and validates again
  (section 7.3). A `sleep` from the chain parks the call at its gates: one
  commit sets the slot `sleeping` and commits `sleeping` at `{ phase: "call" }`,
  and every wake runs `call` again from the top (section 7.2); a sleep the
  commit refuses ends the call `invalid_park` like a block. Otherwise a deferred
  commit sets the slot `running`; one commit then
  records intent: it moves to `execute` with the final arguments and the tool's
  replay policy. After a crash the slot may still show `pending` while the task's
  checkpoint is `execute`; a safe rerun sets it `running` again. The
  same handler executes the tool, runs the `afterTool` chain, and commits the
  result; it builds `api.env` with `HarnessOptions.env` right before executing
  (section 2.2). A tool that does not resolve, invalid arguments, or a block
  runs the `afterTool` chain on the corresponding error result and commits it
  instead, without intent.
- When `execute()` returns a `ToolPark` (section 7.3), the handler closes the
  call's nested-call admission and lets admitted commits land, stops the
  progress throttle, and awaits the commit in flight. One commit then stores
  the latest buffered details and diagnostics (settling pending `details()`
  promises), sets the slot `sleeping` or `waiting` and clears its output,
  writes the checkpoint `parked`, and commits the park's `sleeping` or
  `waiting` state. A park that breaks a rule settles an `invalid_park` result
  instead and ends `failed`. When the park's commit is refused because the call
  was abort-marked meanwhile, the invocation runs `cancel` with `api.checkpoint`
  set to the park's checkpoint, in a context only the Harness's close cancels,
  before it ends. The park is not stored, so a crash before that `cancel`
  finishes leaves the call in `execute`: for a first run (no `wake`) the abort
  handler runs no `cancel`, and the tool's own idempotency key is the only way
  to its work (section 12); for a woken run it runs `cancel` with the checkpoint
  of the previous stored park.
- `parked` runs when the reservation wakes the call, with its `wake`. It
  resolves the tool as `call` does; a tool that no longer resolves settles a
  `tool_unavailable` result without `cancel` and ends `failed`, so work the
  call owns, which nothing supervises any more, is aborted, and the failure is
  reported. Otherwise it commits intent, `execute` with the arguments, the
  current replay policy, the wake, and the checkpoint, with the slot `running`
  by a deferred commit, and runs `execute()` with `api.wake` and
  `api.checkpoint` set in the same handler: a result settles the call, a park
  parks it again.
- `execute` is reached only by recovery. When both the stored and the current
  policy, resolved as in `call`, are `safe`, it executes again with the stored
  arguments, wake, and checkpoint, without `beforeTool`, and settles like
  `call`; the rerun clears the slot's running output, and also its details and
  diagnostics unless the run was woken. Otherwise it runs `cancel` first when
  the run was woken (the stored `wake` is set), then commits an
  `interrupted` error result from the slot's durable partial output, details, and
  diagnostics, after the `afterTool` chain, and ends `failed` with `{ entryId }`.
  A close and a crash both leave `execute`, so a replay-unsafe run is never
  repeated. Either way, a task cut off `settings.restartLimit` times ends with a
  `restart_limit` result instead (section 5.4), also after the chain.
- The result commit bounds the content, appends the diagnostics block (section
  7.3), appends one `pi.tool-result` entry with `model: [{ role: "toolResult",
  toolCallId, toolName, content, details, isError, durationMs, timestamp }]` and
  `data: { diagnostics }`, marks the slot `done`, and
  completes with `{ entryId, control }`. An `isError` result still completes.
  `durationMs` of every result the task writes, and of its nested result and
  slot summary, is the span from the task's `startedAt` to the result commit on
  the Harness clock: gate waits, parks, crash downtime, and reruns included. A
  record without `startedAt`, written by an earlier version, gets how long
  `execute()` took in its last attempt, and none when it did not execute.
- A throw from `execute()`, or from `HarnessOptions.env` building its
  environment, becomes a `tool_error` result and the task ends
  `failed` with `{ entryId }`; once the invocation is signalled it propagates
  instead. Ending `failed`, like `aborted`, records cancellation intent (section
  5.4), so conversations the call owns, which nothing supervises any more, are
  aborted. A returned `isError` result still completes, and its call's owned work
  survives. Either way the run continues with the result entry. A tool task whose
  owned conversations still have ordinary work when it commits its result holds
  `completing` with the result entry already written (section 5.5); the
  generation resumes only when the tool task is terminal.
- The abort handler first runs `cancel` when the checkpoint is `parked`, or
  `execute` with `wake` (a woken run that was cut off, aborted before
  `execute()` was entered, or abort-marked after a restart), on every attempt;
  for a tool that no longer resolves it reports that the call was not
  cancelled. It then commits an `aborted` error result from the slot's durable
  partial output, details, and diagnostics, after the `afterTool` chain, and ends
  `aborted` with `{ entryId }`. A restart mark's message names the phase the
  call was in: interrupted in `execute`, parked in `parked`, not started in
  `call`. A `cancel` that hangs holds Stop, as a slow `afterTool` does. The scheduler faults a task whose abort handler
  was cut off `restartLimit` times, without a result (section 5.4), so the last
  attempt it runs, at `restartLimit - 1` restarts, skips the chain.
- Each run of `execute()` starts with empty output; details and diagnostics
  stay in the slot across a park and its next run, which adds to them, so a
  result that omits `details` gets the newest value and the result's
  diagnostics are the slot's. A nested call with `progress: false` writes none
  to its slot, so none carry over. `beforeTool` runs before intent and never
  again once intent is committed; `afterTool` runs on the final result; neither
  sees a park.
- Every result the task writes passes the `afterTool` chain: the slot is read
  before the result commit, since hooks run outside commits, and does not change
  while the tool does not run. A result the Harness wrote itself is then bounded
  with the tool's output limits (the defaults when it did not resolve), gets a
  truncation diagnostic when that dropped content (a slot's truncation
  diagnostic stays only while the hooks keep its output), and loses any
  `structuredOutput`, except that a nested call the chain turns into a success
  gets its bounded output as value, as a schema-less tool's success does
  (unless the tool declares a schema, section 7.3); `control` applies only when
  the task completes. Once the
  task's restarts exceed `settings.restartLimit`, the chain no longer runs,
  since it may be what keeps cutting the task off. Results that no tool task
  writes never pass it: the generation's `aborted` results for calls a
  sequential round never started (section 8.5), a nested call's fallback result
  (section 7.3), and a missing result synthesized in context (section 2.1).

### 8.5 Tool rounds

### 8.4 Tool

```ts
type ToolTaskInput =
  | { kind: "model"; assistant: EntryId; callId: string }
  | { kind: "nested"; parent: TaskId; parentCallId: string; key: string; call: ToolCall; progress?: false };
type ToolTaskCheckpoint =
  | { phase: "call" }
  /** Intent: `execute()` runs in the phase that commits it; reached as a phase only by recovery. */
  | { phase: "execute"; arguments: JsonObject; replay: "safe" | "unsafe"; wake?: WakeReason; checkpoint?: JsonValue }
  /** The call is parked; its `sleeping` or `waiting` state holds this checkpoint. */
  | { phase: "parked"; arguments: JsonObject; replay: "safe" | "unsafe"; checkpoint?: JsonValue };
type ToolTaskResult = { kind: "model"; entryId: EntryId; control?: ToolControl } | { kind: "nested" };
```

`pi.tool` is version 4 and starts at `{ phase: "call" }`; `migrate` gives a
version 1 input `kind: "model"` and keeps a version 2 input (version 3 added
`unoffered`) and older checkpoints (version 4 added `parked` and the optional
fields of `execute`), and readers treat a terminal result without `kind` as a
model-issued call's. A call flagged `unoffered` resolves no tool: `call` settles
it `tool_unavailable` and the abort handler does too. A model-issued call's input stays small
because the terminal record keeps it; the call is read from the assistant
entry. A nested call (section 7.3) carries its call, since no entry holds it,
and settles differently: its result commit records the result's `usage`
(section 8.6), writes its result for programs to the caller's
`NestedCallDoc` (section 7.3), marks its nested slot `done` with its
summary, appends no entry, and ends with `{ kind: "nested" }`; `control` does
not apply.
Below, `{ entryId }` is a model-issued call's result.

- `call` reads the call with `runtime.entry()`, resolves the tool among the
  phase's agent `tools` (section 7.3), validates
  the arguments with pi-ai
  `validateToolArguments()`, runs the `beforeTool` chain, and validates again
  (section 7.3). A `sleep` from the chain parks the call at its gates: one
  commit sets the slot `sleeping` and commits `sleeping` at `{ phase: "call" }`,
  and every wake runs `call` again from the top (section 7.2); a sleep the
  commit refuses ends the call `invalid_park` like a block. Otherwise a deferred
  commit sets the slot `running`; one commit then
  records intent: it moves to `execute` with the final arguments and the tool's
  replay policy. After a crash the slot may still show `pending` while the task's
  checkpoint is `execute`; a safe rerun sets it `running` again. The
  same handler executes the tool, runs the `afterTool` chain, and commits the
  result; it builds `api.env` with `HarnessOptions.env` right before executing
  (section 2.2). A tool that does not resolve, invalid arguments, or a block
  runs the `afterTool` chain on the corresponding error result and commits it
  instead, without intent.
- When `execute()` returns a `ToolPark` (section 7.3), the handler closes the
  call's nested-call admission and lets admitted commits land, stops the
  progress throttle, and awaits the commit in flight. One commit then stores
  the latest buffered details and diagnostics (settling pending `details()`
  promises), sets the slot `sleeping` or `waiting` and clears its output,
  writes the checkpoint `parked`, and commits the park's `sleeping` or
  `waiting` state. A park that breaks a rule settles an `invalid_park` result
  instead and ends `failed`. When the park's commit is refused because the call
  was abort-marked meanwhile, the invocation runs `cancel` with `api.checkpoint`
  set to the park's checkpoint, in a context only the Harness's close cancels,
  before it ends. The park is not stored, so a crash before that `cancel`
  finishes leaves the call in `execute`: for a first run (no `wake`) the abort
  handler runs no `cancel`, and the tool's own idempotency key is the only way
  to its work (section 12); for a woken run it runs `cancel` with the checkpoint
  of the previous stored park.
- `parked` runs when the reservation wakes the call, with its `wake`. It
  resolves the tool as `call` does; a tool that no longer resolves settles a
  `tool_unavailable` result without `cancel` and ends `failed`, so work the
  call owns, which nothing supervises any more, is aborted, and the failure is
  reported. Otherwise it commits intent, `execute` with the arguments, the
  current replay policy, the wake, and the checkpoint, with the slot `running`
  by a deferred commit, and runs `execute()` with `api.wake` and
  `api.checkpoint` set in the same handler: a result settles the call, a park
  parks it again.
- `execute` is reached only by recovery. When both the stored and the current
  policy, resolved as in `call`, are `safe`, it executes again with the stored

  completes with `{ entryId, control }`. An `isError` result still completes.

  slot summary, is the span from the task's `startedAt` to the result commit on

  environment, becomes a `tool_error` result and the task ends
  `failed` with `{ entryId }`; once the invocation is signalled it propagates

  aborted. A returned `isError` result still completes, and its call's owned work

  before the result commit, since hooks run outside commits, and does not change

ID brands are compile-time only. IDs and sequences remain ordinary numbers in
memory, JSON, JSONL, and SQLite. Code applies a brand only at a trusted creation
or decoding boundary. The distinct sequence brand prevents an entity ID from
being used as a document commit point.

Conversation history parenting and task ownership are separate:

- `parent` controls inherited entries and historical documents.
- `owner` records task attribution and connects scopes for subtree abort and idle traversal. It is not an access-control capability.
- Creation always supplies `ConversationOwnership` explicitly. The Session
  derives the persisted owner's conversation from the named task; callers never
  construct the persisted owner pair.

A conversation's owner remains recorded after the owning task becomes terminal.

### 2.1 Entries and context

Entry IDs are Session-global and ordered. `parent.at` is an entry in the parent
history visible to the child.

The active transcript is the raw entry range from the newest applicable `head`
through the tail. A head on an entry changes subsequent context; it does not
remove older entries from storage. Fork traversal is child entries followed by
parent entries through each `parent.at` cap.

Context derivation:

1. Find the newest visible entry `H` at or before the cutoff that has `head`.
2. Let `from = H.head`, or transcript start when `H` is absent.
3. Scan visible entries from `from` through the cutoff.
4. For each target, the newest edit in that range wins. `omit` contributes no
   model messages; `replace` contributes its `messages` instead of the target's.
5. If `H` exists, context entries are `H` followed by non-head entries in the
   range. Otherwise they are the range.
6. Keep every positional system message and its tool/section changes.
7. Move each assistant's tool results, found before the next assistant message,
   directly after it in tool-call order, ahead of any intervening user or system
   message. The provider protocol requires results to follow their call.
8. Synthesize an error result for every call without one, for example after a
   fork cut or at an interrupted tail. Drop tool results with no preceding call.
9. Exclude model-less entries and assistant messages with `aborted`, `error`, or
   `deferred` stop reasons from future provider requests.
10. Move the first system message to the front when only user messages
    precede it, or when it is the baseline's: the first `pi.system` entry after
    `H`, unless an edit targets it. Generation writes it with every section and
    tool in effect before the first request after a compaction or reset, and
    omits the retained `pi.system` entries. Without `H`, the first `pi.system`
    entry is the baseline unless an earlier entry carries a system message, in
    its messages or an edit's replacement, even one an edit omits later: only
    then did generation write it with every section and tool in effect, before
    the first request or once an agent without any gets one. A run's input
    is committed before generation renders the system prompt, so the context
    otherwise starts with the input, or with the kept history, assistant
    messages included. Providers treat only a leading system message as the
    initial prompt and tool set; without one, a later tool change rewrites the
    request's tool list and invalidates the whole prompt cache. Only the first
    system message moves, so replay gives the same sections and tools. Any other
    system message with an assistant message before it stays in place, since
    moving it would change what it means; a retained system message of another
    kind ahead of the baseline therefore keeps the baseline from leading.
    Stored entries and `contributions` keep the committed order.

The conversation view (section 9.3) carries a window over the visible
entries in ID order, head markers in place; `Conversation.context()` derives
the active transcript. UI reduction and model-context reduction are separate
consumers. Entries outside the window are available through the owning
`Conversation` object's cursor-based `entries()` scan.

The Session keeps the documents it loads or creates in memory, as Chord
trackers, so reads and changes need no Storage access. The cache is bounded by
use, not by history: a document no watch observes leaves it
