---
date: 2026-08-07
updated: 2026-11-23
tags: [teaching, course, session]
status: shaping
---

# Session 5: Coding Harness (internals)

Open the box. What is the machinery the intern works inside actually made of?

**Schedule change**: Session 6 ran before Session 5, because of date conflicts with the guest. One class is left, and it combines Session 5 (harness internals) with Session 6's open-weight models block (Diego's deck).

Owner: Agus. Duration: 2 h. The delivered materials (instructor notes, deck, exercise) go in Spanish, like sessions 2, 3, 4 and 6. These vault notes stay in English.

Drafted 2026-08-30 from the [[04_Archive/pi-talk/pi-talk|BeerJS Pi talk]] (2026-06-25) plus Pi's own docs and its example extensions.

## The frame

Teach the concept, use Pi as the specimen. Every block is a design decision that any harness has to make, and Pi is the one we can open. Session 6 closes the course on the idea that what you build survives the change of tool, so this session rehearses it a week early.

## Draft skeleton (~2 h)

| Block | ~min | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Recap | 8 | Show-and-tell on Session 4's homework. Where did the docs help, where did they go stale against the code? Open questions from Session 4. |
| What we're covering today | 3 | Four sessions spent driving the thing. Today we open it. Name the shift: this is the first of two sessions that take the machine apart. |
| What a harness is, and the others | 10 | The layered diagram (Interface → Agent Loop → Tools/Memory/Context → LLM). An LLM on its own predicts tokens and can't do anything; the harness connects it to the world. Then the others: Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek's, opencode. Not a ranking. What's worth naming is open against closed source, what ships built in against what you add, whether you can extend it at all and how deep that reaches, and who controls the system prompt. Somebody decided each of those. |
| The loop, and Pi's parts | 14 | How a turn actually runs, step by step, with the extension points marked on the arrows. Then Pi's four packages, base to surface, and the line that you use only the layers you need. The densest block of the day. |
| The session tree, and steering vs follow-up | 7 | Two behaviours of the loop, quickly. The tree: entries carry `id` and `parentId`, the current position is the active leaf, the whole thing sits in one JSONL file. That's why `/tree` is cheap. You move a pointer, you don't delete anything. Steering: when does new information reach an agent that is already running? Mid-stream, after it settles, or queued for the next turn. Every harness answers this. Pi is a good specimen because it names all three out loud. |
| Break | 5 | |
| Three ways to give a model a tool, and subagents | 13 | The general design decision. An extension reaches harness internals and goes deep, but only works in that harness. A CLI is the simplest thing that works and runs anywhere there's a shell, with no auth story. MCP is for tools other people use, for auth, for remote services. What decides it is who the consumer is. Then subagents as mechanism: a separate context with its own transcript, whose entire result comes back to the parent as one message. |
| Compaction | 7 | The trigger is one line (`contextTokens > contextWindow - reserveTokens`). Then the four-step algorithm and the before/after diagram of the entry array. `session_before_compact` can cancel it or hand back a summary you wrote. |
| **Hands-on** | **35** | Read your own session file, then have the agent extend the agent. Detail below. |
| Run modes | 4 | Interactive, headless one-shot, embedded as a library, served over a protocol. The point underneath is that the agent loop is a library and the terminal is one frontend. That's why CI agents, bots and browser agents exist at all. |
| Security | 9 | Threat models, permission models, the sandbox ladder. The honest close. |
| Closing | 5 | What surprised you? Homework. Name the transition to Session 6. |

If the hands-on has to be 45 instead of 35, two content blocks pay for it. Not five minutes off each. Decide that before the class, not during it.

## Hands-on: have the agent extend the agent (~35 min)

**Step 0 (~5 min): open your own session file.** Sessions live in `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`, one JSONL file each, organised by working directory. Find your own entries, look at the `id` and `parentId` pairs, find a branch point. If anyone in the room has a compaction entry, project it. The summary they have been carrying around is a line in a file.

Everything from the theory blocks stops being a diagram here. Five minutes, no more.

**Steps 1-3 (~30 min): pick a target and direct the agent.** A menu, so a room this heterogeneous can self-select:

- a `/command` that does something small and yours
- a tool that wraps a CLI you already use
- a hook that warns or blocks on something (writing to `.env`, a `git push`)
- a widget or a status line

**You don't need to know TypeScript.** That is the exercise. They have spent four weeks learning to direct an agent, and today the target is the tool itself. Install into `.pi/extensions/` or `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`, then iterate with `/reload`. No restart, the loop stays warm.

Everything the course has taught gets pointed at the harness for the first time. Plan first, from Session 2. The `AGENTS.md` and skills they built in Session 3. And Session 4's research move, which here means pointing the agent at Pi's docs and its examples directory before it writes a line.

### What to watch for while walking the room

- **The agent will hallucinate Pi's API, and that's the best thing that can happen.** Pi is small and recent. It isn't in the model's training the way React is. This will happen on its own, to most of the room, and it makes the case about grounding better than any slide can. Don't prevent it. Let it happen, then fix it the Session 4 way, with the docs in context.
- **Watch the size of what they ask for.** The failure mode is asking for a big extension. Push for something that fits on one screen. The exercise is the loop between direction and result, not the artefact.
- **Whoever finishes doesn't start a second one.** Send them to read Pi's own `subagent/` example and compare it with the 200-line version from the talk.
- **A callback to throw while walking**: did you give it the docs before or after it invented that function?

## Security: the honest close (~9 min)

General first, Pi as the example.

- **Threat models.** What are you actually defending against? Prompt injection from repo content, a malicious extension or skill or MCP server, the agent's own destructive mistakes, credentials walking out the door. Different problems, different answers.
- **Permission models** as a design space: allowlist and denylist, ask every time, fully autonomous, read-only modes.
- **The sandbox ladder**: none → in-process → container → micro-VM → remote machine. The argument worth stating plainly is that a partial sandbox is worse than none, because it reads as a boundary while still sitting on your shell, your filesystem, your package managers and your credentials. Real isolation comes from the operating system.
- **Pi as the example.** No sandbox, on purpose. Project trust guards what gets loaded; it is not a safety boundary.

This block goes after the hands-on because that is what earns it. They just wrote an extension and installed it. Pi's own docs say it in one line: extensions run with your full system permissions and can execute arbitrary code. They have been installing them since Session 2.

## Key decisions

- **Concepts general, Pi as the specimen.** Every block is a decision any harness makes. Session 6 closes the course on the same idea, so this rehearses it a week early.
- **No harness comparison table.** The survey block names the axes, not a winner.
- **TypeScript is not assumed.** Session 3 says outright that we can't. Having the agent write the extension removes the problem, and I think it makes a better exercise than writing TypeScript would have been.
- **Security closes the session, after the hands-on.**
- **The session tree stays short.** Pi-specific, a quick look, not a block of its own.
- **Dropped from the design**: provider-level hooks (`before_provider_request` and friends) and the example catalogue as an argument — both only pay off if you already care about Pi. Two former drops need revisiting after PR #16: plan-mode internals (the `{ block: true }` hook is Session 2's unpaid debt, now this session's) and "MCP as just another extension", stale since Pi 1 ships MCP built in with `exposure`.

## Cross-session wiring

- **From [[sessions/session-1/session-1|Session 1]]**: the debt this session was created to pay. Context hygiene was taught there as four commands to use, explicitly "operations, not mechanism". Here `/compact` and `/tree` get their mechanism.
- **From [[sessions/session-3/session-3|Session 3]]**: the boundary moved again (PR #16). The anatomy block — tool, harness, extension points, plan mode as `tool_call` → `{ block: true }`, permissions and security — left Session 3's deck and is now this session's territory, unclaimed by its current INSTRUCTOR. Diego's notes ask for exactly that coordination: confirm this session covers the plan-mode hook, because nobody else pays that debt now. Session 3 also parks "writing a TypeScript extension" here, unchanged, and proposes `propuesta-mcp/` (MCP transports, code mode from the inside, FastMCP) — a deck waiting on a decision, not in this session's plan or timing.
- **From [[sessions/session-4/session-4|Session 4]]**: Session 3 now introduces subagents (PR #16); whether Session 4 still opens them through the documentation use case is unsettled — PR #6's move was reversed. Here they get their mechanism either way. Name the operation early, open the machinery in Session 5. Session 4's closing already announces this session by name.
- **To [[sessions/session-6/session-6|Session 6]]**: the handoff changed, and it got better. Nobody leaves here with a hand-written client, so Session 6's optional "point your own loop at the gateway" extension has no audience from this session. What replaces it is stronger. Session 6's opening recap asks what extension they wrote and whether it survived the week, and Session 6's whole thesis is that everything they built survives the model swap. The extension included. Diego can't write that block until this one exists.

## Homework for Session 6

Keep the extension alive during the week. Note what you had to fix and whether you reached for it again. Bring it. Next week the model underneath changes and we find out what survives.

## What's left before this is done

### To write

- The three repo files, in Spanish: `INSTRUCTOR.md`, `slides.md`, `exercise/README.md`. The deck is the biggest single lift
- Tier 5 in `COURSE_PROGRAM.md`, still one line reading "TBD, topics to be defined by the owner", and the Session 5 section under Proposed Sessions with it
- **Audience and assumptions**, the section every other session's notes open with. What they arrive with (per the merged `INSTRUCTOR.md`, touched by PR #16): Pi 1 with Plannotator and `pi-subagents`, an MCP server in `.pi/mcp.json`, their repo, their `AGENTS.md` and skills, their docs from Session 4. Nothing new gets installed, which makes this the only session in the course with no setup risk. Worth saying out loud in the notes
- The reading list. Two references are seeded in the program (Zechner on the Pi coding agent, Pi's example extensions); the rest is the owner's
- The Security and Trust cross-cutting entry, still `TBD` for this session in the program. This design answers it

### To decide

- **The fallback if the hands-on collapses.** Every other session has one and this doesn't. If the agent can't produce a working extension in 30 minutes, or the API rate-limits 30 people at once, or the room's network folds, they need a pre-written extension to read and modify instead. **The biggest unmitigated risk in the design**
- **What's on screen during the theory.** Session 3 decided its demo project is the course repo; this needs the same call. Probably Pi's own source and docs, plus a live session for the tree and compaction blocks
- **Which blocks run live rather than as diagrams.** The loop, the tree and compaction all want to be shown. Decide which, and record a backup clip for each
- How much threat-model material fits in 9 minutes. Left alone it is easily 20
- Whether the hands-on should be 45, and which two blocks pay for it
- The expected result, in the exercise's own terms: a working extension in `.pi/extensions/` that they got there by directing the agent

### To test

- **The hands-on on a clean machine, timed.** How long does the agent take to produce a *working* extension with Pi's docs in context? If it runs past about 15 minutes, the menu gets smaller, not the block longer
- One reference extension per menu item, pre-built, so nobody is stuck at minute 30 with nothing
- Slides 3, 9, 10 and 11 from the BeerJS talk carry most of the opening. Check what needs redrawing now that the frame is specimen and not pitch

### To coordinate with Diego

- The Session 3 boundary — now concrete: the anatomy block and the plan-mode hook debt landed here (PR #16), and `propuesta-mcp/` waits on a decision
- The changed Session 6 handoff. No client comes out of this session, so his opening recap and his closing extension both change

## Related

- [[04_Archive/pi-talk/pi-talk|BeerJS: Pi, the self-building agent]], the source material. Slide specs in `04_Archive/pi-talk/slides/`, and a working subagents extension in `demos/demo-2-subagents/`
- [[sessions/session-3/session-3|Session 3]], where tool, harness and extension-point vocabulary gets introduced from the outside
- Pi's docs ship with the install: `extensions.md`, `compaction.md`, `sessions.md`, `session-format.md`, `security.md`, `containerization.md`, `sdk.md`, plus around 80 example extensions

---
date: 2026-03-28
updated: 2026-11-23
tags: [teaching, course, agentic-coding, university]

---

# From Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering

6-week course for university CS students on the full spectrum of AI-assisted development — from pure vibe coding to structured agentic engineering. FaMAF extension course.

> **Source of truth**: the repo `filadd/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course`. Session artifacts here (`INSTRUCTOR.md`, `slides.md`, `exercise/README.md`) are mirrors — edit them in the repo, not here. The `session-N.md` notes are vault-native.
>
> **Mirror state, 2026-11-23.** Every session artifact and [[topic-inventory]] mirror `main` at `f4eb3fe`. Session 4 has no `exercise/` any more. Session 3's `INSTRUCTOR.md` and `slides.md` picked up Diego's Oct 25–26 commits pushed straight to `main` after PR #16 merged. Session 2 also carries `prompts.md`. The Session 1 PDF export, the HTML decks (`sessions/session-{1,2,3,4,6}/deck/index.html`), Session 5's `propuesta-mcp/` deck, Session 2's vibe-coded demo app and its replay (`sessions/session-2/{app,replay}/`) and the `session-replay` skill (`.claude/skills/`) stay in the repo only.
>
> The repo folded the standalone tier notes into `COURSE_PROGRAM.md` and dropped `resources/`, so [[topic-inventory]] now mirrors that file directly.
>
> **Session materials are in Spanish, instructor notes included**, for every session except Session 5's `INSTRUCTOR.md`. Session 1 switched to Spanish in PR #10. These vault `session-N.md` notes stay in English.

## Format

- 6 sessions, 1 per week, in two arcs — **base (1-4)**: *how do I work well with this thing?*, closed by Session 4; **advanced (5-6)**: *what is this made of, and what if I swap its parts?*, closed by Session 6. Same cohort throughout; the split is announced to students in Session 1. **In practice the run had five classes**: Session 6's guest block ran before Session 5, and the last class combines Session 5 with Session 6's open-weight models block
- **Session 1 is 3 hours; the rest are 2** — the extra hour buys introductions, the fundamentals block, and the Pi install
- Theory → hands-on → show-and-tell discussion
- Same project across all sessions; must run in the browser. Students bring their own idea — Session 1 now ships `proyecto-de-respaldo` for those who don't
- Tool: **Pi** (`pi.dev`) — decided. Students install it in Session 1
- Class size: ~30 students, quota of 35. Audience widened in PR #10 to advanced CS students *and* junior programmers

## People

- **Agustin Carrasco** — instructor. Owns sessions 2, 4, 5; the Pi intro and demo in Session 1
- **Diego Piloni** — instructor. Owns sessions 1, 3, 6
- **Ale Silva** (CCAD) — guest, Session 6
- Filadd TAs — floor support during hands-on blocks

## Key Thesis

Vibe coding is a great on-ramp, but professional software development demands accountability. The course shows *why* each level of structure matters by letting students experience the failures firsthand before introducing the solutions.

**Core mental model: "Managing a smart intern."**

**Companion idea: responsibility stays with the person.** If it breaks, if a key leaks, if the code is unmaintainable — you are accountable, not the AI. "The agent wrote it" is not an excuse that exists.

## The Spectrum

1. Vibe Coding — prompt-and-accept, no code review
2. AI-Assisted Coding — copilot completions, developer maintains control
3. Directed AI Assistance — experienced use with constraints, specs, review
4. Agentic Coding — orchestrating AI agents on tasks with oversight
5. Agentic Engineering — full discipline: specs, quality gates, multi-agent coordination

## Repo state (synced 2026-11-23)

Repo: `~/workspace/filadd/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course`; `origin/main` is at `f4eb3fe`, and the local checkout is on `main`. **Sessions 1–4 have run, and so has Session 6 with Ale**, moved earlier because of date conflicts. One class is left: Session 5 combined with Session 6's open-weight models block.

**Every PR is merged.** `feat/session-4-deck` was merged into `main` on 2026-11-02 without a PR (`f57d9e3`), together with three kurasu web commits. The other session-material changes since PR #16 are Diego's Session 3 deck commits on `main` (Oct 25–26) and the Session 6 deck (#20, #21):

| PR | Session | Merged |
|---|---|---|
| #3 | Skeleton and Session 1 | 2026-07-28 |
| #4 | Session 2, rebuilt on Pi | 2026-08-07 |
| #6 | Session 3, repetition as the spine | 2026-08-20 |
| #7 | Session 6, CCAD through a gateway | 2026-08-22 |
| #8 | Session 4, documentation as the spine | 2026-08-23 |
| #9 | Session 5, harness internals with Pi as the specimen | 2026-08-31 |
| #10 | Session 1 reworked in Spanish, final deck in Claude Design, METR dropped | 2026-09-27 |
| #11 | Session 2 reworked around design first, animated HTML deck | 2026-09-28 |
| #12 | Session 1 deck rebuilt as an animated HTML deck at `sessions/session-1/deck/index.html` | 2026-10-04 |
| #14 | Session 2: verification added, second half reworked, 25 slides with one per planning step; also the vibe-coded demo app, its replay video, the `session-replay` skill and Git LFS for images | 2026-10-20 |
| #15 | Session news by mail and a shared D1 repository — kurasu app work, no session-material changes | 2026-10-23 |
| #16 | Session 3: animated deck with the notes aligned to it — Pi 1 native MCP (`exposure`), subagents back in, anatomy to Session 5, code mode/FastMCP proposed for Session 5 | 2026-10-24 |
| #17 | Email validation end to end — kurasu | 2026-10-26 |
| #18 | Session feedback poll — kurasu | 2026-11-02 |
| #19 | Questions on the featured session's card, featured session as an explicit mark — kurasu | 2026-11-02 |
| — | Session 4 reworked as a live run with a concept-only animated deck, homework dropped, program aligned (`feat/session-4-deck`, merged without a PR) | 2026-11-02 |
| #20 | Session 6: open-weight models deck at `sessions/session-6/deck/index.html`, built from Copes's post | 2026-11-11 |
| #21 | Session 6 deck: Ollama, Pi and Hugging Face demo slides, the kurasu slides API, and the *Qwen adaptado a Pi* slide | 2026-11-23 |

Every session has `INSTRUCTOR.md`, `slides.md` and an `exercise/` in the repo, Session 5 included (written 2026-08-30, program Tier 5 filled in the same day). `COURSE_PROGRAM.md` carries the six tiers, and `resources/` is gone again. `PROGRAMA.md` is the two-page Spanish program for the FaMAF extension submission, which lists Marcos Gómez as docente responsable.

## Session Status

|---|---|---|

## Blockers

- **Concurrency on the gateway**: 25-30 students hitting one LiteLLM endpoint for an hour. Rate limits and key handout were settled in #7's follow-ups; confirm under load before the session.
- **Subagents are split**: Session 3 teaches the primitive and installs `pi-subagents`; Session 4 shows them in use during the live run. `COURSE_PROGRAM.md` and the repo `README.md` say so on `main`; confirm the split with Diego.
- **Session 3's exercise README lags its INSTRUCTOR** (four steps, planning skill, no subagent step) and the room's Pi version needs confirming (`pi-subagents` asks for 1.2.0+, the material says Pi 1.0) — both on Session 3's INSTRUCTOR pendientes.
- **Session 6's opening recap** should reflect that Session 5 produces an extension, not a hand-written client. Check the merged notes say so.

## Known inconsistencies on the repo

Checked against `main` (`1de8330`) on 2026-11-02; none of the mirrored files changed up to `f4eb3fe` (2026-11-23):

- **When is `pi-subagents` installed?** Three answers coexist: the repo `README.md` says Session 2, `COURSE_PROGRAM.md` says Session 4, and Session 3's práctica (PR #16) installs it. Diego's notes flag this himself.
- ~~Where are subagents taught?~~ → Session 3 the primitive, Session 4 the use, Session 5 the mechanism; the program says so on `main`.
- ~~Cost/tokens has no home~~ → Session 4's reworked deck closes with *Todo tiene un costo* (money, context, attention).
- Session 3's `exercise/README.md` still shows four steps with the planning skill; its INSTRUCTOR and deck say five steps with a verification skill.
- **Session 5 still runs Session 4's recap** inside its demo block, with the homework (keep docs alive, note when they went stale) that Session 4 no longer gives. Its `INSTRUCTOR.md` and `slides.md` need aligning; `COURSE_PROGRAM.md` already dropped that line.

- ~~Claude Code vs alternatives~~ → **decided: Pi**, for all six sessions
- ~~Which `pi-subagents` package?~~ → **decided: the unscoped `pi-subagents`** — since PR #16 it's installed in Session 3's práctica (moved back from Session 4); confirm the package against the npm forks, per Diego's notes
- ~~Which session owns the full-course retrospective now that there are six?~~ → **resolved**: sessions 1-4 are the base arc, 5-6 the advanced arc. Session 4 closes the base arc with the judgment material (cost/tokens, when NOT to use AI, skill atrophy, career); Session 6 closes the course with the artifact material (repo retrospective, spectrum, transfer thesis)
- Does the extension-course format allow 6 weeks at all? Confirm before announcing
- Confirm the 3-hour room slot for Session 1
- API keys: course-wide, a proxy, or students' own? Session 5 may need raw API access, which is a different requirement from "the agent works"

3:A 6-session extension course at FaMAF (Universidad Nacional de Cordoba) that walks CS students and Junior programmers through the full spectrum of AI-assisted development — from pure "vibe coding" to structured agentic engineering, and then into the internals: how a coding harness works, and running open-weights models on UNC's supercomputing center.
11:1. **The Vibe Coding Experience** — prompt-and-accept workflow, anatomy of a coding agent (tool + harness + LLM), analyze what the AI actually produced
13:3. **Tooling & Skills** — tools and harness deep dive, AGENTS.md in depth, custom skills, MCP, documentation tools
18:5. **Coding Harness (internals)** — the agent loop and its extension points, the session tree, compaction, three ways to give a model a tool, subagents as mechanism, run modes, and agent security
30:The course runs on [Pi](https://pi.dev) for all six sessions — terminal-based, minimal, standard `AGENTS.md`. Students install it in session 1, and later sessions add extensions on top of it rather than switching harness: `@plannotator/pi-extension` (file-based plan mode and review) in session 2, and `pi-subagents` in session 3. The course uses Pi 1, which ships MCP built in, so MCP needs no extension. In session 6 the same tool is pointed at an open-weights model served by UNC's HPC center — which is the point of teaching structure instead of a product.

# Demo 1 prompt

Build a small Pi extension that adds a playful mascot to the TUI.

The mascot should appear under the input bar and move on its own:
- use a widget below the editor, not an overlay or command output
- render a compact ASCII mascot on one or two lines
- move it horizontally across the available terminal width
- on each animation tick, give it a 10% chance to change direction
- always reverse direction when it reaches either terminal border
- make it visibly jump while it moves

When I run a user shell command with `!`, the mascot should celebrate:
- listen for user bash commands, not slash commands
- do not block or replace the command execution
- trigger a short celebration animation with bigger jumps and fireworks around the mascot
- return to the normal wandering animation after the celebration finishes

Keep this stage-friendly:
- implement it as a single TypeScript extension file
- avoid dependencies
- keep the code readable enough to explain live
- guard TUI-only behavior so non-interactive modes do not break
- start any timers on session start and clean them up on session shutdown
- include the command I should run to test it locally with Pi
</result>
</event>

# Demo 3 — Pi in the browser

## Context

This is the closer for the "Pi, the self-building agent" talk (~5 min). The entire Pi agent loop runs **client-side in the browser** — no backend, no server. The audience sees a chat panel where they talk to the agent, and a live preview panel where the single HTML page the agent writes renders in real time.

**The wow moment**: Ask "build me a landing page for a coffee shop" and watch the agent write HTML on the left while the page assembles itself on the right.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
│ Chat  [⚙ settings]  │   Live preview           │
│─────────────────────│   (right)                │
│   (left)            │                          │
│                     │   <iframe srcdoc="...">  │
│   Message history   │   (re-renders when       │
│   (scrollable)      │    the file changes)     │
│                     │                          │
│   Streaming text    │                          │
│   Tool call feed    │                          │
│   ("write…")       │                          │
│─────────────────────│                          │
│   [ input box...  ] │                          │
└─────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┘
```

**Tech stack**: Vite + TypeScript, vanilla DOM (no framework), `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core/base` + `@earendil-works/pi-ai/base`.

**LLM**: Configurable at runtime via a settings screen. User enters a `provider/model` string (e.g. `zai/glm-5.2`) and an API key. Common provider APIs (openai-completions, anthropic-messages, etc.) are registered at startup so any model works. Settings persist in `localStorage`.

/* ───────────── Stage ───────────── */

* { box-sizing: border-box; }

html, body {
  margin: 0;
  height: 100%;
  background: var(--bg);
  color: var(--ink);
  overflow: hidden;
  font-family: var(--font-body);
  transition: background .4s, color .4s;
}

body {
  background-image: var(--bg-pattern);
  background-size: var(--bg-size);
}

#deck {
  position: absolute;
  left: 50%;
  top: 50%;
  width: 1280px;
  height: 720px;
  transform-origin: center;
}

.slide {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  padding: 50px 72px;
  opacity: 0;
  pointer-events: none;
  transform: translateX(60px) scale(.98);
  transition: opacity .45s, transform .55s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.2);
}

.slide.active {
  opacity: 1;
  pointer-events: auto;
  transform: none;
}

.slide.past { transform: translateX(-60px) scale(.98); }

h1, h2, h3 {
  font-family: var(--font-display);
  font-weight: 700;
  margin: 0 0 22px;
  line-height: 1.1;
  letter-spacing: -.02em;
}

h1 { font-size: 104px; }
h2 { font-size: var(--title-size); white-space: nowrap; }
h3 { font-size: 30px; }

p { margin: 0; }

.big { font-size: 40px; line-height: 1.25; }
.mid { font-size: 30px; }
.small { font-size: 22px; color: var(--muted); }
.mono { font-family: var(--font-mono); }
.center { text-align: center; }
.hl { color: var(--a1); }

.card {
  background: var(--card);
  border: var(--border);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  box-shadow: var(--shadow);
  padding: 22px 26px;
}

.slide > .mascot { position: absolute; right: 80px; bottom: 50px; --size: 130px; }

/* ───────────── Fragments ───────────── */

[data-step] {
  opacity: 0;
  transform: translateY(18px);
  transition: opacity .45s, transform .6s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.4);
}

[data-step].on { opacity: 1; transform: none; }

.f-drop { transform: translateY(-120px) rotate(-8deg); }
.f-drop.on { transform: rotate(var(--r, 0deg)); }
.f-flip { transform: perspective(900px) rotateY(-95deg); transform-origin: left center; }
.f-flip.on { transform: perspective(900px) rotateY(0); }
.f-pop { transform: scale(.3); }
.f-pop.on { transform: scale(1); }

/* ───────────── Mascot ───────────── */

.mascot {
  width: var(--size, 120px);
  height: var(--size, 120px);
  display: inline-block;
}

.mascot svg { width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: visible; animation: bob 2.4s ease-in-out infinite; }
.mascot.jump svg { animation: jump .6s cubic-bezier(.3, 1.5, .5, 1) 1, bob 2.4s ease-in-out .6s infinite; }
.mascot.bigjump svg { animation: bigjump .9s cubic-bezier(.3, 1.5, .5, 1) 1, bob 2.4s ease-in-out .9s infinite; }
.mascot.shake svg { animation: shake .12s linear infinite; }

@keyframes bob { 50% { transform: translateY(-5px) scaleY(1.02); } }
@keyframes jump { 0% { transform: none; } 15% { transform: scale(1.15, .85); } 50% { transform: translateY(-90px) scale(.92, 1.1) rotate(-6deg); } 85% { transform: scale(1.12, .88); } 100% { transform: none; } }
@keyframes bigjump { 0% { transform: none; } 15% { transform: scale(1.2, .8); } 45% { transform: translateY(-150px) rotate(-200deg); } 70% { transform: translateY(-40px) rotate(-360deg); } 85% { transform: scale(1.15, .85) rotate(-360deg); } 100% { transform: rotate(-360deg); } }
@keyframes shake { 25% { transform: translateX(-3px) rotate(-2deg); } 75% { transform: translateX(3px) rotate(2deg); } }
@keyframes wave { 50% { transform: rotate(-22deg); } }

.mascot .arm { transform-origin: 84px 60px; animation: wave .5s ease-in-out infinite; }
.mascot .drop { animation: drip 1.1s ease-in infinite; }
.mascot .qmark { animation: qbob 1s ease-in-out infinite alternate; transform-origin: 80px 4px; }
.mascot .steam { animation: steam .35s ease-in-out infinite alternate; }
@keyframes qbob { to { transform: translateY(-4px) rotate(12deg); } }
@keyframes steam { to { opacity: .4; transform: translate(2px, -2px); } }
@keyframes drip { 0% { transform: translateY(-4px); opacity: 0; } 30% { opacity: 1; } 100% { transform: translateY(14px); opacity: 0; } }

.confetti { position: absolute; width: 12px; height: 18px; border-radius: 3px; pointer-events: none; animation: confetti 1.4s cubic-bezier(.2, .6, .4, 1) forwards; }
@keyframes confetti { 0% { transform: translate(0, 0) rotate(0); opacity: 1; } 100% { transform: translate(var(--dx), var(--dy)) rotate(var(--rot)); opacity: 0; } }

/* bloques en fila */
.blk { padding: 14px 18px; border: var(--border); border-radius: 14px; background: var(--card); box-shadow: 5px 5px 0 #05051a; white-space: nowrap; font-size: 24px; font-weight: 700; }
.blk small { display: block; margin-top: 4px; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 400; color: var(--muted); white-space: normal; max-width: 240px; }
.blk.rev { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 40%, var(--card)); }
.blk.calm { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 35%, var(--card)); }
.blk.des { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 35%, var(--card)); }
.arrow { padding-top: 14px; font-size: 30px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--muted); }
.row { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 12px; }
.stg { opacity: 0; transform: scale(.6); transition: opacity .35s, transform .45s cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.6); transition-delay: calc(var(--i) * .16s); }
.on .stg { opacity: 1; transform: none; }


/* portada */
.cover { display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center; height: 100%; }
.cover .kicker { font-size: 30px; color: var(--muted); }
.cover h1 { font-size: 170px; margin: 0; line-height: 1; white-space: nowrap; }
.cover .subt { margin: 6px 0 26px; font-family: var(--font-display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 58px; letter-spacing: -.02em; white-space: nowrap; min-height: 66px; }
.cover .cursor { display: inline-block; width: .45em; height: .85em; background: var(--a1); vertical-align: -.06em; animation: blink 1s steps(1) infinite; }
@keyframes blink { 50% { opacity: 0; } }
.cover .mascot { position: absolute; right: 110px; top: 90px; --size: 200px; }
.cover .mascot.enter { animation: dropIn .9s cubic-bezier(.3, 1.5, .5, 1) both; }
@keyframes dropIn { from { transform: translateY(-600px) rotate(-20deg); } to { transform: none; } }

.lead { margin: -8px 0 20px; font-size: 25px; color: var(--muted); }
.lead b { color: var(--ink); }
.punch-step { margin-top: 22px; }
@keyframes loopflow { to { stroke-dashoffset: -19; } }

/* ventanas */
.win { display: flex; flex-direction: column; overflow: hidden; background: var(--card); border: var(--border); border-radius: 16px; box-shadow: var(--shadow); }
.win .bar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; padding: 10px 16px; background: #ffffff14; border-bottom: 2px solid #fdf6e322; }
.win .bar i { width: 14px; height: 14px; border-radius: 50%; background: #ff5f57; }
.win .bar i:nth-child(2) { background: #febc2e; }
.win .bar i:nth-child(3) { background: #28c840; }
.win .bar .title { margin-left: 10px; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 16px; color: var(--muted); }
.win .body { flex: 1; padding: 16px 20px; }
.win.dark .body { background: var(--term-bg); font-family: var(--font-mono); font-variant-ligatures: none; }
.shot { position: absolute; right: 10px; bottom: 8px; padding: 2px 8px; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted); border: 1px dashed var(--muted); border-radius: 6px; }

/* harness: capas */
.stack { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 820px 240px; gap: 12px 26px; margin-top: 8px; }
.layer { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 20px; padding: 16px 24px; font-size: 28px; font-weight: 700; border: var(--border); border-radius: 14px; box-shadow: 5px 5px 0 #05051a; }
.layer small { font-size: 20px; font-weight: 400; color: var(--muted); }
.layer.ui { grid-row: 1; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 34%, var(--card)); }
.layer.loop { grid-row: 2; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 30%, var(--card)); }
.trio { grid-row: 3; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 12px; }
.trio .layer { flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 26%, var(--card)); }
.layer.llm { grid-row: 4; color: #15153a; background: var(--a3); }
.layer.llm small { color: #15153a; opacity: .7; }
.brace { grid-column: 2; grid-row: 1 / 4; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; }
.brace .bar { align-self: stretch; width: 26px; border: 5px solid var(--a3); border-left: none; border-radius: 0 18px 18px 0; }
.brace b { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 40px; color: var(--a3); }
.side-llm { grid-column: 2; grid-row: 4; align-self: center; font-size: 20px; color: var(--muted); }

/* ejemplos */
.cascade { position: relative; height: 530px; }
.cascade .win { position: absolute; width: 470px; }
.cascade .win img { display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; }
.win .bar .kind { margin-left: auto; padding: 2px 10px; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; color: #15153a; background: var(--a3); border-radius: 8px; }
.wins3 { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 30px; margin-top: 18px; }
.wins3 .win { height: 400px; }

/* agentes de código */
.dirs { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1.15fr; gap: 30px; margin-top: 30px; align-items: start; }
.dirs .body { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; font-size: 22px; }

/* qué es pi */
.author { display: inline-flex; gap: 12px; align-items: center; margin: -10px 0 20px; padding: 6px 16px; font-size: 20px; border: 2px solid var(--muted); border-radius: 999px; color: var(--muted); }

.pi-cards .card:nth-child(1) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 26%, var(--card)); }

.provs { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 6px; width: 190px; justify-content: flex-end; }

/* planilla */

/* arquitectura de pi */

/* ciclo de vida: agent loop */

.elabel { position: absolute; font-size: 14px; color: var(--muted); }
.onapi { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 48px; margin-top: 6px; padding: 14px 20px; font-size: 19px; white-space: nowrap; border: var(--border); border-radius: 14px; background: var(--card); }

/* api programática */

/* PD1: ¿y si...? */
.whatif { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 380px 1fr; gap: 30px; height: 480px; margin-top: 10px; }
.whatif .center { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 14px; padding: 24px; text-align: center; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 22%, var(--card)); }

.whatif .q:nth-child(4) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 18%, var(--card)); }

/* PD2: arquitectura de pi-durable */
.dur { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 860px 1fr; gap: 0 26px; align-items: start; }
.dur .col { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 14px; }
.clients { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 34px; }
.clients .noclient { flex: 1; padding: 6px 14px; font-size: 17px; line-height: 1.3; color: var(--muted); border: 2px dashed var(--muted); border-radius: 10px; }
.clients .noclient b { color: var(--a3); }
.clients .cl { padding: 10px 18px; font-size: 20px; font-weight: 700; border: var(--border); border-radius: 12px; background: var(--card); }
.frame { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; padding: 34px 20px 20px; border: 4px solid var(--ink); border-radius: 20px; background: #ffffff08; }
.frame .lbl { position: absolute; top: -20px; left: 22px; padding: 2px 14px; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 24px; font-weight: 700; color: #15153a; background: var(--ink); border-radius: 8px; }
.frame .r { display: grid; gap: 12px; }
.frame .r3 { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); }
.frame .r2 { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); }
.part { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; padding: 12px 18px; font-size: 23px; font-weight: 700; border: 3px solid; border-radius: 12px; }
.part small { font-size: 17px; font-weight: 400; color: var(--muted); }
.part.same { border-color: var(--a4); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 20%, var(--card)); }
.part.new { border-color: var(--a1); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 22%, var(--card)); }
.base { padding: 16px 22px; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 26px; font-weight: 700; color: #15153a; background: var(--a3); border: var(--border); border-radius: 14px; box-shadow: 5px 5px 0 #05051a; }
.base small { margin-left: 16px; font-family: var(--font-body); font-size: 19px; font-weight: 400; }
.legend { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 14px; margin-top: 70px; font-size: 20px; }
.legend span { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; }
.legend i { width: 26px; height: 26px; border: 3px solid; border-radius: 6px; }
.legend .same i { border-color: var(--a4); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 20%, var(--card)); }
.legend .new i { border-color: var(--a1); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 22%, var(--card)); }

/* PD3: storage */
.store { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 290px 150px 1fr; align-items: center; gap: 10px; margin-top: 4px; }
.hbox { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; padding: 22px; font-size: 20px; border: 4px solid var(--ink); border-radius: 18px; background: #ffffff08; }
.hbox b { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 30px; }
.hbox code { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 16px; color: var(--a3); }
.flow { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 4px; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 15px; color: var(--muted); text-align: center; }
.flow .ar { font-size: 44px; line-height: 1; color: var(--ink); }
.backends { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; }
.be { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 50px 1fr; align-items: center; gap: 2px 14px; padding: 9px 18px; border: var(--border); border-radius: 14px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 18%, var(--card)); }
.be .ico { grid-row: span 2; font-size: 30px; }
.be b { font-size: 22px; }
.be span { font-size: 16px; color: var(--muted); }
.contrast { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 18px; margin-top: 22px; padding: 14px 22px; font-size: 22px; border: 3px dashed var(--a4); border-radius: 14px; }
.contrast code { font-family: var(--font-mono); color: var(--a3); }

/* PD4: entornos */
.envs { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 330px 260px 1fr; align-items: center; gap: 22px; margin-top: 16px; }
.machine { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; padding: 30px 20px 20px; border: 3px solid transparent; border-radius: 20px; transition: border-color .5s; }
.machine .lbl { position: absolute; top: -16px; left: 18px; padding: 2px 10px; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 700; color: #15153a; background: var(--a3); border-radius: 8px; opacity: 0; transition: opacity .5s; }
.machine.away { border-color: var(--a3); border-style: dashed; }
.machine.away .lbl { opacity: 1; }
.machine .call { padding: 10px 14px; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 17px; border: 2px solid #fdf6e366; border-radius: 10px; }
.envfn { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; padding: 18px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 26%, var(--card)); }
.envfn code { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 19px; color: var(--a3); }
.envfn span { font-size: 18px; line-height: 1.3; color: var(--muted); }
.targets { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 16px; }
.tg { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; padding: 14px 20px; font-size: 23px; font-weight: 700; border: var(--border); border-radius: 14px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 20%, var(--card)); }
.tg .ico { font-size: 34px; }
.tg small { display: block; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 400; color: var(--muted); }
.uses { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 24px; margin-top: 26px; }
.uses .card { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; padding: 16px 20px; font-size: 21px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.3; }
.uses .card .ico { font-size: 36px; }
.uses .card:nth-child(1) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 22%, var(--card)); }
.uses .card:nth-child(2) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 26%, var(--card)); }
.uses .card:nth-child(3) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 22%, var(--card)); }
.arrowcol { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; font-size: 40px; color: var(--muted); }

/* PD5: durabilidad */
.dur2 { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 430px 1fr; gap: 30px; margin-top: 4px; }
.jsonl .body { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; font-size: 14px; }
.jsonl .ln2 { padding: 4px 8px; border-radius: 6px; background: #ffffff0d; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; }
.jsonl .ln2.cut { color: var(--bad); background: #ff5c5c22; }
.jsonl .txt { margin-top: 10px; font-family: var(--font-body); font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.35; color: var(--ink); }
.jsonl .txt span { color: var(--muted); }
.sandwich { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; }
.sandwich h3 { margin: 0 0 4px; }
.sw { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; padding: 14px 22px; font-size: 23px; font-weight: 700; border: var(--border); }
.sw .n { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 30px; color: var(--a3); }
.sw small { margin-left: auto; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 15px; font-weight: 400; color: var(--muted); }
.sw.bread { border-radius: 30px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a3) 30%, var(--card)); }
.sw.fill { border-radius: 10px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 30%, var(--card)); }
.crash { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; margin-top: 8px; padding: 14px 20px; font-size: 20px; line-height: 1.3; border: 3px dashed var(--bad); border-radius: 14px; }
.crash b { color: var(--bad); }
.crash code { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 17px; color: var(--a3); }

.nest { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; margin-top: 14px; padding: 10px 20px; font-size: 18px; line-height: 1.35; border: 3px solid var(--a2); border-radius: 14px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 14%, var(--card)); }
.nest .ico { font-size: 34px; }
.nest b { color: var(--a3); }
.nest code { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 16px; color: var(--a3); }

/* comparación final */
.vs-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 170px repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr)); grid-template-rows: auto 1fr 1fr; gap: 16px 18px; height: 500px; margin-top: 6px; }
.vs-grid .vh { grid-row: 1; padding: 0 4px 4px; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 24px; font-weight: 700; }
.vs-grid .vl { grid-column: 1; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 24px; font-weight: 700; }
.vs-grid .vl .dot { flex: none; width: 22px; height: 22px; border: 3px solid; border-radius: 6px; }
.vs-grid .dot.ca { border-color: var(--a4); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 20%, var(--card)); }
.vs-grid .dot.pd { border-color: var(--a1); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 22%, var(--card)); }
.vs-grid .vc { display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 16px 18px; font-size: 21px; line-height: 1.35; border: 3px solid; border-radius: 14px; box-shadow: 5px 5px 0 #05051a; }
.vs-grid .vc.ca { border-color: var(--a4); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 20%, var(--card)); }
.vs-grid .vc.pd { border-color: var(--a1); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 22%, var(--card)); }
.vs-grid code { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 17px; color: var(--a3); white-space: nowrap; }
.vs-grid .vc.pd[data-step] { transition-delay: .15s; }

/* PD6: multiplayer */
.multi { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 340px 1fr 300px; gap: 24px; align-items: center; margin-top: 10px; }
.multi .side { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 22px; }
.cli { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; padding: 16px 18px; font-size: 19px; }
.cli h3 { margin: 0; font-size: 24px; }
.cli code { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 14px; white-space: nowrap; color: var(--a3); }
.cli:nth-child(1) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a1) 22%, var(--card)); }
.cli:nth-child(2) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a2) 26%, var(--card)); }
.cli.late { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--a4) 22%, var(--card)); }
.convo .body { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; min-height: 330px; }
.msg { padding: 10px 14px; font-size: 18px; border-radius: 12px; background: #ffffff10; }
.msg b { display: block; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: .06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); }
.msg.steer { border: 2px solid var(--a1); }
.msg.steer b { color: var(--a1); }
.msg.fu { border: 2px dashed var(--a2); }
.msg.fu b { color: var(--a2); }
.msg.busy::after { content: " ▍"; animation: blink 1s steps(1) infinite; }
.tie { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 14px; margin-top: 20px; font-size: 22px; }
.tie code { padding: 3px 10px; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 19px; color: #15153a; background: var(--a3); border-radius: 8px; }

/* ───────────── HUD ───────────── */

#hud {
  position: fixed;
  left: 0;
  right: 0;
  bottom: 0;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  padding: 10px 18px;
  font: 14px/1 system-ui, sans-serif;
  color: var(--muted);
  opacity: .25;
  transition: opacity .3s;
  z-index: 60;
}

#hud:hover { opacity: 1; }
#hud.hidden { display: none; }
#hud .stepdots i { display: inline-block; width: 7px; height: 7px; margin: 0 2px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; opacity: .3; }
#hud .stepdots i.on { opacity: 1; }
</style>

<body>

<div id="deck">

  <!-- 1 · Portada -->
  <section class="slide" data-id="portada">
    <div class="cover">
      <div class="kicker">Última clase · el harness</div>
      <h1><span class="typed"></span></h1>
      <div class="subt"><span class="typed2"></span><span class="cursor"></span></div>

    </div>
  </section>
  <!-- Notas: arrancamos con el nombre: Pi es un coding agent open source con un núcleo mínimo. "Se construye solo" porque le pedís una capacidad nueva y lee su propio código para escribirse la extensión. La hora no es para vender Pi: es para entender qué es un harness, y Pi nos sirve de espécimen porque es chico y se puede abrir entero. -->

  <!-- 2 · Harnesses -->
  <section class="slide" data-id="harness">
    <h2>Harnesses</h2>
    <div class="stack">
      <div class="layer ui" data-step="3">Interfaz <small>chat · terminal · web</small></div>

El harness (arnés) es lo que lo conecta al mundo: le da tools, memoria, contexto, un loop que repite pensar, actuar y observar, y una interfaz. Construir de abajo hacia arriba. Todos los productos de IA son un modelo más un harness, y la diferencia entre productos está en el harness, no en el modelo. -->

Un coding agent en terminal: lee y edita tus archivos y corre comandos en tu máquina. El harness que elegís define qué podés hacer. -->

  <!-- Notas: preguntar quiénes usaron alguno. Los dos grandes primero, después la carpeta de otros. No profundizar: es solo el mapa para ubicar a Pi en la próxima slide. -->

No profundizar en cada punto: solo plantarlos. -->

  <!-- Notas: el coding agent agrega una línea al JSONL por entrada; si el proceso muere a mitad de un turno, no hay nada que lo retome: abrís la sesión, mirás y le decís que siga. pi-durable envuelve cada efecto entre dos commits: la intención y el resultado. Al reabrir, sabe qué quedó a medias. Las fases reales: pi.tool pasa por call, execute y resultado, y queda "parked" mientras espera; pi.generation pasa por prepare, request y tools o finish, más retry y poll. Si se cae a mitad de una respuesta del modelo, el parcial queda como entrada abortada y se reintenta según la política. Las tareas se anidan: una tarea puede ser dueña de tareas hijas con política failFast (falla una, se cancelan las demás), allSettled (espera a todas) o any (alcanza con una); tareas y conversaciones forman un solo árbol de pertenencia, y un abort corre de abajo hacia arriba, de las hojas a la raíz. Ejemplo: la llamada al modelo espera las tareas de tools de su ronda con allSettled. Fuente: spec de pi-durable §5 y README. -->

        <div class="body">
          <div class="msg"><b>usuario</b>migrá los tests a Vitest</div>
          <div class="msg busy"><b>agente</b>leyendo la configuración…</div>
          <div class="msg steer" data-step="1"><b>steer · A</b>ojo, no toques los e2e</div>
          <div class="msg fu" data-step="2"><b>followUp · B</b>después actualizá el README</div>
        </div>
      </div>

    </div>
    <div class="tie" data-step="4">Los mismos modos que vimos en la API de Pi: <code>steer</code><code>followUp</code><code>nextTurn</code></div>

  <!-- Notas: una sola conversación y varios clientes. A manda un steer: entra mientras el agente está trabajando. B manda un follow-up: queda para cuando termine. Alguien que se engancha tarde llama a watch(): recibe la vista actual y después cada commit; no se le re-reproduce la historia. Son los mismos modos de entrega que vimos en la API programática del coding agent (steer, followUp, nextTurn), ahora entre personas distintas. -->

  <!-- 18 · Coding agent vs pi-durable -->
  <section class="slide" data-id="versus">
    <h2>Coding agent vs pi-durable</h2>
    <div class="vs-grid">
      <div class="vl" style="grid-row: 2"><i class="dot ca"></i>coding agent</div>

      <div class="vh" data-step="2" style="grid-column: 3">🛰️ Entorno de ejecución</div>
      <div class="vc ca" data-step="2" style="grid-column: 3; grid-row: 2"><span>la máquina donde corre el proceso</span></div>
      <div class="vc pd" data-step="2" style="grid-column: 3; grid-row: 3"><span><code>env()</code> en cada llamada: directorio local, contenedor, VM remota</span></div>
      <div class="vh" data-step="3" style="grid-column: 4">⏳ Durabilidad</div>
      <div class="vc ca" data-step="3" style="grid-column: 4; grid-row: 2"><span>si el proceso muere, mirás y le decís que siga</span></div>

      <div class="vc pd" data-step="4" style="grid-column: 5; grid-row: 3"><span>varios clientes: watch, steer, follow-up</span></div>
    </div>
  </section>
  <!-- Notas: el cierre del bloque, aspecto por aspecto en el mismo orden de las slides: storage, entorno de ejecución, durabilidad, multiplayer. No es que uno sea mejor que el otro: pi-durable no reemplaza al coding agent. Son respuestas distintas a las mismas decisiones de diseño: dónde se guarda la sesión, dónde actúan las tools, qué pasa si el proceso se cae y quién puede seguir y dirigir la conversación. El coding agent elige lo simple para una persona en una terminal; pi-durable paga más complejidad para sostener lo demás. -->

</div>

<div id="hud">
  <div><span class="count"></span>   <span class="stepdots"></span></div>
  <div>← → navegar · F pantalla completa · H ocultar</div>
</div>

<script>
const $ = (sel, root = document) => root.querySelector(sel);
const $$ = (sel, root = document) => [...root.querySelectorAll(sel)];
const rand = (a, b) => a + Math.random() * (b - a);
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

/* ───────────── Mascot ───────────── */

const EYES = {
  open: '<ellipse cx="38" cy="52" rx="5" ry="6.5" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/><ellipse cx="62" cy="52" rx="5" ry="6.5" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/><circle cx="40" cy="50" r="1.8" fill="#fff"/><circle cx="64" cy="50" r="1.8" fill="#fff"/>',
  wide: '<circle cx="38" cy="51" r="8" fill="#fff" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="62" cy="51" r="8" fill="#fff" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="39" cy="52" r="3.5" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/><circle cx="61" cy="52" r="3.5" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/>',
  half: '<path d="M32 51 h12 M56 51 h12" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M33 52 q5 6 10 0 M57 52 q5 6 10 0" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/><path d="M31 42 l12 3 M69 42 l-12 3" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
  x: '<path d="M33 47 l10 10 M43 47 l-10 10 M57 47 l10 10 M67 47 l-10 10" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3.5" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
  happy: '<path d="M32 54 q6 -9 12 0 M56 54 q6 -9 12 0" fill="none" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3.5" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
  odd: '<circle cx="38" cy="53" r="4" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/><circle cx="62" cy="50" r="8" fill="#fff" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="61" cy="51" r="3.5" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/><path d="M30 44 l14 -3 M55 36 l14 4" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
};

const MOUTH = {
  smile: '<path d="M42 64 Q50 73 58 64" fill="none" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3.5" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
  grin: '<path d="M40 63 Q50 78 60 63 Z" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/><path d="M45 69 Q50 73 55 69" fill="#ff7a93"/>',
  worried: '<path d="M43 69 Q50 63 57 69" fill="none" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3.5" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
  flat: '<path d="M44 67 h12" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3.5" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
  wow: '<ellipse cx="50" cy="68" rx="4.5" ry="5.5" fill="var(--mascot-ink)"/>',
  squiggle: '<path d="M40 68 q3 -4 6 0 t6 0 t6 0" fill="none" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/>',
};

const MOODS = {
  happy: { eyes: "open", mouth: "smile" },
  wave: { eyes: "happy", mouth: "grin", arm: true },
  joy: { eyes: "happy", mouth: "grin" },
  sweat: { eyes: "wide", mouth: "worried", drop: true },
  dizzy: { eyes: "x", mouth: "squiggle" },
  skeptic: { eyes: "half", mouth: "flat" },
  wow: { eyes: "wide", mouth: "wow" },
  confused: { eyes: "odd", mouth: "squiggle", q: true },
  frustrated: { eyes: "half", mouth: "worried", steam: true },
};

const mascotSVG = (mood) => {
  const m = MOODS[mood] || MOODS.happy;

  return `<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100">
    <ellipse cx="50" cy="94" rx="30" ry="4" fill="#000" opacity=".12"/>
    ${m.arm ? '<path class="arm" d="M84 60 q14 -8 10 -26" fill="none" stroke="var(--mascot)" stroke-width="9" stroke-linecap="round"/>' : ""}
    <path d="M50 12 C78 12 90 34 90 58 C90 80 74 90 50 90 C26 90 10 80 10 58 C10 34 22 12 50 12Z" fill="var(--mascot)" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="2.5"/>
    <ellipse cx="34" cy="28" rx="9" ry="5" fill="#fff" opacity=".45" transform="rotate(-25 34 28)"/>
    <circle cx="28" cy="63" r="5" fill="#ff7a93" opacity=".45"/><circle cx="72" cy="63" r="5" fill="#ff7a93" opacity=".45"/>
    ${EYES[m.eyes]}${MOUTH[m.mouth]}
    ${m.q ? '<text class="qmark" x="74" y="12" font-size="30" font-weight="700" fill="var(--a1)" font-family="var(--font-display)">?</text>' : ""}
    ${m.steam ? '<path class="steam" d="M84 22 l8 -8 M90 32 l11 -3 M76 16 l2 -11" stroke="var(--a1)" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"/>' : ""}
    ${m.drop ? '<path class="drop" d="M80 26 q-5 8 0 11 q5 -3 0 -11Z" fill="#6ec3ff" stroke="var(--mascot-ink)" stroke-width="1.5"/>' : ""}
  </svg>`;
};

const setMood = (el, mood) => {
  if (el == null || el.dataset.cur === mood) {
    return;
  }

  el.dataset.cur = mood;
  el.innerHTML = mascotSVG(mood);
};

const replay = (el, cls) => {
  el.classList.remove(cls);
  void el.offsetWidth;
  el.classList.add(cls);
};

const confetti = (container, x, y, count = 28) => {
  const colors = ["--a1", "--a2", "--a3", "--a4"];

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) {
    const c = document.createElement("div");
    c.className = "confetti";
    c.style.left = `${x}px`;
    c.style.top = `${y}px`;
    c.style.background = `var(${colors[i % colors.length]})`;
    c.style.setProperty("--dx", `${rand(-220, 220)}px`);
    c.style.setProperty("--dy", `${rand(-200, 160)}px`);
    c.style.setProperty("--rot", `${rand(-540, 540)}deg`);
    container.appendChild(c);
    setTimeout(() => c.remove(), 1500);
  }
};

/* ───────────── Slide hooks ───────────── */

let run = 0;
let visit = 0;

const typeInto = async (el, text, speed, token, clock = () => run) => {
  el.textContent = "";

  for (const ch of text) {
    if (token !== clock()) {
      return;
    }

    el.textContent += ch;
    await sleep(speed);
  }
};


const hooks = {
  portada: (step, el, { entered }) => {
    const m = $(".mascot", el);

    if (!entered) {
      return;
    }

    // Tied to the visit, not the render: the re-render after the web fonts load must not cut the typing
    const token = visit;
    m.classList.remove("enter");
    m.style.opacity = 0;
    $(".typed2", el).textContent = "";

    typeInto($(".typed", el), "Pi:", 110, token, () => visit)
      .then(() => typeInto($(".typed2", el), "el agente que se construye solo", 55, token, () => visit))
      .then(() => {
        if (token !== visit) {
          return;
        }

        m.style.opacity = 1;
        m.classList.add("enter");
      });
  },

  demo: (step, el, { entered }) => {
    if (entered) {
      replay($(".mascot", el), "bigjump");
    }
  },

  entornos: (step, el) => $(".machine", el).classList.toggle("away", step >= 3),
};

/* ───────────── Titles ───────────── */

// Titles stay on one line: shrink the ones that would overflow the slide width
const fitTitles = () => $$(".slide h2").forEach((h) => {
  h.style.fontSize = "";

  let size = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(h).fontSize);

  while (h.scrollWidth > h.clientWidth && size > 30) {
    size -= 2;
    h.style.fontSize = `${size}px`;
  }
});

/* ───────────── Navigation ───────────── */

const slides = $$(".slide");
let idx = 0;
let step = 0;

// Inside kurasu the deck runs in a sandboxed iframe: the web moves it with kurasu:go messages and owns the
// navigation, so the deck leaves the keys, the address bar and its own HUD alone. Other iframes (a review tool's
// preview, for instance) send no kurasu:go, so the deck keeps its own controls until the first one arrives.
const framed = window.parent !== window;
let embedded = false;

const stepsOf = (s) => Number(s.dataset.steps || Math.max(0, ...$$("[data-step]", s).map((e) => Number(e.dataset.step))));

const show = (entered, forward) => {
  run += 1;

  if (entered) {
    visit += 1;
  }

  slides.forEach((s, i) => {
    s.classList.toggle("active", i === idx);
    s.classList.toggle("past", i < idx);
  });

  const slide = slides[idx];
  slide.dataset.step = step;
  $$("[data-step]", slide).forEach((e) => e.classList.toggle("on", Number(e.dataset.step) <= step));
  $$("[data-step]", slide).forEach((e) => e.classList.toggle("cur", Number(e.dataset.step) === step));

  const hook = hooks[slide.dataset.id];

  if (hook != null) {
    hook(step, slide, { entered, forward });
  }

  $(".count").textContent = `${idx + 1} / ${slides.length}`;
  $(".stepdots").innerHTML = Array.from({ length: stepsOf(slide) }, (_, i) => `<i class="${i < step ? "on" : ""}"></i>`).join("");
  if (!embedded) {
    history.replaceState(null, "", `${location.search}#${idx + 1}${step > 0 ? `.${step}` : ""}`);
  }
};

const next = () => {
  if (step < stepsOf(slides[idx])) {
    step += 1;
    show(false, true);
  } else if (idx < slides.length - 1) {
    idx += 1;
    step = 0;
    show(true, true);
  }
};

const prev = () => {
  if (step > 0) {
    step -= 1;
    show(false, false);
  } else if (idx > 0) {
    idx -= 1;
    step = stepsOf(slides[idx]);
    show(true, false);
  }
};

document.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  if (embedded) {
    return;
  }

  if (["ArrowRight", " ", "PageDown", "Enter"].includes(e.key)) {
    e.preventDefault();
    next();
  } else if (["ArrowLeft", "PageUp", "Backspace"].includes(e.key)) {
    e.preventDefault();
    prev();
  } else if (e.key === "f" || e.key === "F") {
    document.fullscreenElement == null ? document.documentElement.requestFullscreen() : document.exitFullscreen();
  } else if (e.key === "h" || e.key === "H") {
    $("#hud").classList.toggle("hidden");
  }
});

const fit = () => {
  const k = Math.min(innerWidth / 1280, innerHeight / 720);
  $("#deck").style.transform = `translate(-50%, -50%) scale(${k})`;
};

addEventListener("resize", fit);

/* ───────────── Init ───────────── */

$$(".mascot").forEach((m) => setMood(m, m.dataset.mood));
fit();

fitTitles();

const [hashSlide, hashStep] = location.hash.slice(1).split(".").map(Number);
idx = Math.min(Math.max((hashSlide || 1) - 1, 0), slides.length - 1);
step = Math.min(hashStep || 0, stepsOf(slides[idx]));
show(true, step === 0);

document.fonts.ready.then(() => {
  fitTitles();
  show(false, false);
});

/* ───────────── kurasu ───────────── */

// kurasu counts slides and steps from 1 and gives a slide without inner steps one step, so the deck's
// step 0 is kurasu's step 1.
if (framed) {
  window.parent.postMessage({
    type: "kurasu:manifest",
    slides: slides.map((s) => ({ steps: stepsOf(s) + 1 })),
  }, "*");

  addEventListener("message", (e) => {
    const go = e.data;

    if (e.source !== window.parent || go?.type !== "kurasu:go" || !Number.isInteger(go.slide) || !Number.isInteger(go.step)) {
      return;
    }

    if (!embedded) {
      embedded = true;
      $("#hud").classList.add("hidden");
    }

    const nextIdx = Math.min(Math.max(go.slide - 1, 0), slides.length - 1);
    const nextStep = Math.min(Math.max(go.step - 1, 0), stepsOf(slides[nextIdx]));
    const forward = nextIdx > idx || (nextIdx === idx && nextStep >= step);
    const entered = nextIdx !== idx;

    if (!entered && nextStep === step) {
      return;
    }

    idx = nextIdx;
    step = nextStep;
    show(entered, forward);
  });
}
</script>
</body>
</html>

No hay código: la demo es pedirle a Pi, en vivo, que se escriba la extensión. \`PROMPT.md\` tiene el pedido: una mascota ASCII que camina debajo del input y festeja cuando corrés un comando con \`!\`, en un solo archivo TypeScript y sin dependencias.

- Correr Pi en un directorio vacío y pegarle el prompt.
- Probar con \`/reload\`, sin reiniciar.
- Lo que muestra: extender el harness es barato y el resultado se lee.

## 2 · Subagentes (\`demo-2-subagents/\`)

Una extensión de proyecto en \`.pi/extensions/subagents.ts\` con dos tools:

- **\`delegate\`** abre una sesión de Pi headless con su propio contexto, devuelve el control enseguida y, cuando termina, inyecta el resultado como \`followUp\`. Un widget muestra los subagentes activos.
- **\`pipeline\`** corre una lista de agentes en secuencia; cada uno recibe la salida del anterior (por ejemplo research → implement → review).

## 3 · Pi en el navegador (\`demo-3-browser-agent/\`)

await write(`${r}/sessions/session-5/INSTRUCTOR.md`, `# Sesión 5 — Coding Harness (internals) — Notas para el instructor

> A cargo: Agus. Estado: borrador. Todo el material de la sesión está en español.

## Dónde entra esta hora

La última clase del curso junta la Sesión 5 con el bloque de modelos open-weight de la Sesión 6, que lleva el deck de Diego (\`sessions/session-6/deck/index.html\`). La Sesión 6 con Ale ya se dio antes, por un conflicto de fechas.

Estas notas cubren solo **la hora del harness**: unos 60 minutos, con el deck \`deck/index.html\` y su esqueleto con notas de orador en \`slides.md\`. Las demos de proyectos, el bloque open-weight y el cierre del curso se resuelven aparte, en la misma clase. La versión anterior de esta sesión (2 h 30 con demos, bloques de teoría y una extensión de tarea) queda en el historial de git.

## Objetivo de la hora (en una frase)

Que salgan entendiendo **de qué está hecha la herramienta que usaron todo el curso**, y que las mismas piezas se pueden resolver de otra forma cuando el agente tiene que hacer más que un coding agent.

## El encuadre

**Enseñar el concepto, usar Pi como el espécimen.** Cada slide es una decisión de diseño que cualquier harness tiene que tomar; Pi es el que podemos abrir entero porque es chico.

La base del deck es la charla de BeerJS *Pi: el agente que se construye solo*, que estaba pensada para vender Pi. Dos slides vienen de ese tono: *La misma filosofía* (VS Code vs Vim) y *La diferencia en números*. Decirlas como decisiones distintas, no como un ranking: Claude Code trae todo de fábrica, Pi trae lo mínimo, y ninguno de los dos está mal.

La segunda mitad presenta **pi-durable** con el mismo movimiento: no como un reemplazo de Pi (Earendil dice explícitamente que no lo es), sino como otra respuesta a las mismas decisiones cuando querés guardar la sesión en cualquier lado, correr las tools en otra máquina, sobrevivir a un crash o tener varias personas en la misma sesión.

## Audiencia y supuestos

- Llegan con Pi 1, Plannotator, \`pi-subagents\`, un servidor MCP, su repo, su \`AGENTS.md\` y sus skills.
- **No se instala nada y no se escribe código.** Las demos las corre el instructor.
- **No se asume TypeScript.** El código aparece en pantalla para leerlo, no para escribirlo.
- Ya pasaron por la Sesión 6: vieron cambiar el modelo debajo del mismo harness. Esta hora abre lo que quedó arriba de ese modelo.

## Plan slide por slide

Los tiempos son una guía; el detalle de cada slide está en las notas de \`slides.md\` y en los comentarios del deck.

### Parte 1 — Pi como espécimen (~20 min)

| # | Slide | Tiempo | La idea que tiene que quedar |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Portada | 1 min | Pi "se construye solo": le pedís una capacidad y lee su propio código para escribirse la extensión |
| 2 | Harnesses | 2 min | Un LLM solo predice tokens; el harness (interfaz, loop, tools, memoria, contexto) lo conecta al mundo. La diferencia entre productos es el harness |
| 3 | Ejemplos de harnesses | 1 min | ChatGPT, Lovable y un coding agent: el mismo tipo de modelo con harnesses distintos |
| 4 | Agentes de código | 1 min | El mapa: Claude Code, Codex y los otros. Preguntar quién usó alguno |
| 5 | ¿Qué es Pi? | 2 min | Cuatro tools, prompt de menos de mil tokens, cualquier proveedor, sin permisos, sesiones en árbol |
| 6 | La misma filosofía | 1,5 min | VS Code ≈ Claude Code (todo de fábrica), Vim ≈ Pi (lo mínimo y armás lo tuyo) |
| 7 | La diferencia en números | 2 min | Skills, MCP y code mode en los dos; subagentes, plan mode y memoria en Pi no vienen de fábrica, se agregan |
| 8 | Arquitectura | 2 min | Los cuatro paquetes con la misma estructura de capas que el harness: pi-tui, pi-coding-agent, pi-agent-core, pi-ai. Usás solo las capas que necesitás |
| 9 | Extensiones: la vida de una sesión | 2 min | Una extensión es un archivo TypeScript que escucha eventos; la vista de lejos y los hooks de sesión (switch, fork, compact, tree) |
| 10 | Extensiones: el agent loop | 3 min | El loop como ciclo, un momento por paso. \`tool_call\` → \`{ block: true }\` es el plan mode de la Sesión 2, ahora en su lugar |
| 11 | API programática | 2,5 min | Las extensiones no solo miran: cambian modelo y tools, registran capacidades, inyectan mensajes (steer, followUp, nextTurn) y manejan sesiones |

### Demos (~14 min)

| Demo | Tiempo | Qué muestra |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · Una mascota | 3 min | Pi se escribe una extensión en vivo a partir de \`demos/demo-1-mascot/PROMPT.md\`. Extender es barato y se lee |
| 2 · Subagentes | 6 min | \`demos/demo-2-subagents\`: \`delegate\` abre una sesión headless en background y el resultado vuelve como \`followUp\`; \`pipeline\` encadena agentes. Doscientas líneas son el mecanismo; el resto es producto |
| 3 · Pi en el navegador | 5 min | \`demos/demo-3-browser-agent\`: el loop corriendo en el navegador sin backend. El loop es una librería y la terminal es una de sus interfaces |

Cómo correr cada una está en \`demos/README.md\`. **No tipear en vivo** salvo la demo 1, que es justamente eso.

### Parte 2 — pi-durable (~17 min)

| # | Slide | Tiempo | La idea que tiene que quedar |
|---|---|---|---|
| 13 | ¿Y si queremos más que un coding agent? | 2 min | Un agente pensado para una persona, una terminal y la vida del proceso. Cuatro "y si…" que se salen de eso |
| 14 | Arquitectura de pi-durable | 3 min | La misma estructura de capas. pi-ai abajo; el harness es el marco. Conversaciones, tools y extensiones son las mismas ideas; tareas, entorno de ejecución y storage son nuevos. No trae cliente: lo armás vos |
| 15 | La sesión se guarda donde quieras | 2 min | El harness commitea lo mismo en memoria, IndexedDB, SQLite, JSONL o un Durable Object. El coding agent siempre usa un JSONL |
| 16 | Entornos de ejecución | 2,5 min | El harness está separado de donde actúan las tools. Casos: sandbox, un agente remoto que toca varios sistemas, una sesión que se mueve entre entornos |
| 17 | Durabilidad | 3 min | El "sándwich" de cada efecto: commitear la intención, hacer el efecto, commitear el resultado. Si se cae en el medio, una tool se vuelve a correr solo si es \`replay: "safe"\`. Las tareas se anidan |
| 18 | Multiplayer | 2,5 min | Varios clientes en una conversación: steer, follow-up, y quien llega tarde arranca de la vista actual |
| 19 | Coding agent vs pi-durable | 2 min | Aspecto por aspecto. No es que uno sea mejor: son respuestas distintas a las mismas decisiones |

**Total: ~51 minutos**, con unos nueve de colchón para preguntas. Si el tiempo aprieta, lo primero que se achica son las demos (la 3 puede quedar en un clip) y después las slides 3 y 4.

## Qué vigilar

- **El tour de features.** La primera mitad viene de una charla que vendía Pi. Si la sala sale pensando "Pi es mejor que Claude Code", el encuadre falló.
- **pi-durable es experimental.** Su README dice que la API cambia sin aviso entre versiones. Presentarlo por las ideas, no como algo para adoptar mañana.
- **El ciclo del loop (slide 10)** es la slide más densa. Ensayarla con reloj.

## Puentes con el resto del curso

- **Sesión 1**: LLM + tool + harness. Hoy se abre el harness entero.
- **Sesión 2**: el plan mode que les restringía las tools aparece en el loop como \`tool_call\` → \`{ block: true }\`.
- **Sesión 3**: subagentes como primitiva y MCP de fábrica en Pi 1. Hoy se ve el mecanismo de un subagente en doscientas líneas.
- **Sesión 4**: los subagentes en uso durante la corrida en vivo; acá, cómo están hechos.
- **Sesión 6**: ya cambiaron el modelo debajo del harness. La slide del Qwen adaptado a Pi del deck de Diego muestra el otro sentido: un modelo entrenado para un harness.

## Lo que quedó afuera a propósito

- El árbol de sesión y la compactación en detalle, las tres formas de darle una tool a un modelo, los run modes y el bloque de seguridad del diseño anterior.
- Cómo implementa Pi 1 el MCP (\`exposure\`, code mode por dentro): solo aparece como una fila de la tabla.
- La propuesta de Diego \`propuesta-mcp/\` (transportes, code mode y FastMCP): queda en pausa.
- Los documentos de pi-durable: son interesantes pero confunden y no suman a la comparación.
- La extensión como tarea: no hay clase después de esta para revisarla.

## Pendientes

- **Ensayar las tres demos** en la máquina de la clase. La demo 3 usa paquetes de la época de la charla (0.79); probar si siguen andando o actualizarlos.
- **Logos de Amp, Droid, Aider, Cline y Goose** en la slide 4: hoy son texto.
- **Revisar contra las docs de Pi** el texto de la slide 9 (qué aporta \`resources_discover\` y "puede frenarlo o cambiar cómo se hace") y el parámetro de los modos de entrega de \`sendMessage\` en la slide 11.
- **Confirmar que Claude Code tiene code mode**, como dice la tabla de la slide 7.
- **\`exercise/README.md\`** sigue describiendo la extensión de tarea del diseño anterior.
`);

> A cargo: Agus. Estado: borrador. Todo el material de la sesión está en español.

### Parte 1 — Pi como espécimen (~20 min)

| # | Slide | Tiempo | La idea que tiene que quedar |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Portada | 1 min | Pi "se construye solo": le pedís una capacidad y lee su propio código para escribirse la extensión |
| 2 | Harnesses | 2 min | Un LLM solo predice tokens; el harness (interfaz, loop, tools, memoria, contexto) lo conecta al mundo. La diferencia entre productos es el harness |
| 3 | Ejemplos de harnesses | 1 min | ChatGPT, Lovable y un coding agent: el mismo tipo de modelo con harnesses distintos |
| 4 | Agentes de código | 1 min | El mapa: Claude Code, Codex y los otros. Preguntar quién usó alguno |
| 5 | ¿Qué es Pi? | 2 min | Cuatro tools, prompt de menos de mil tokens, cualquier proveedor, sin permisos, sesiones en árbol |
| 6 | La misma filosofía | 1,5 min | VS Code ≈ Claude Code (todo de fábrica), Vim ≈ Pi (lo mínimo y armás lo tuyo) |
| 7 | La diferencia en números | 2 min | Skills, MCP y code mode en los dos; subagentes, plan mode y memoria en Pi no vienen de fábrica, se agregan |
| 8 | Arquitectura | 2 min | Los cuatro paquetes con la misma estructura de capas que el harness: pi-tui, pi-coding-agent, pi-agent-core, pi-ai. Usás solo las capas que necesitás |
| 9 | Extensiones: la vida de una sesión | 2 min | Una extensión es un archivo TypeScript que escucha eventos; la vista de lejos y los hooks de sesión (switch, fork, compact, tree) |
| 10 | Extensiones: el agent loop | 3 min | El loop como ciclo, un momento por paso. \`tool_call\` → \`{ block: true }\` es el plan mode de la Sesión 2, ahora en su lugar |
| 11 | API programática | 2,5 min | Las extensiones no solo miran: cambian modelo y tools, registran capacidades, inyectan mensajes (steer, followUp, nextTurn) y manejan sesiones |

Cómo correr cada una está en \`demos/README.md\`. **No tipear en vivo** salvo la demo 1, que es justamente eso.

### Parte 2 — pi-durable (~17 min)

| # | Slide | Tiempo | La idea que tiene que quedar |
|---|---|---|---|
| 13 | ¿Y si queremos más que un coding agent? | 2 min | Un agente pensado para una persona, una terminal y la vida del proceso. Cuatro "y si…" que se salen de eso |
| 14 | Arquitectura de pi-durable | 3 min | La misma estructura de capas. pi-ai abajo; el harness es el marco. Conversaciones, tools y extensiones son las mismas ideas; tareas, entorno de ejecución y storage son nuevos. No trae cliente: lo armás vos |
| 15 | La sesión se guarda donde quieras | 2 min | El harness commitea lo mismo en memoria, IndexedDB, SQLite, JSONL o un Durable Object. El coding agent siempre usa un JSONL |
| 16 | Entornos de ejecución | 2,5 min | El harness está separado de donde actúan las tools. Casos: sandbox, un agente remoto que toca varios sistemas, una sesión que se mueve entre entornos |

| 18 | Multiplayer | 2,5 min | Varios clientes en una conversación: steer, follow-up, y quien llega tarde arranca de la vista actual |
| 19 | Coding agent vs pi-durable | 2 min | Aspecto por aspecto. No es que uno sea mejor: son respuestas distintas a las mismas decisiones |

- **Sesión 3**: subagentes como primitiva y MCP de fábrica en Pi 1. Hoy se ve el mecanismo de un subagente en doscientas líneas.
- **Sesión 4**: los subagentes en uso durante la corrida en vivo; acá, cómo están hechos.
- **Sesión 6**: ya cambiaron el modelo debajo del harness. La slide del Qwen adaptado a Pi del deck de Diego muestra el otro sentido: un modelo entrenado para un harness.

- **Confirmar que Claude Code tiene code mode**, como dice la tabla de la slide 7.
- **\`exercise/README.md\`** sigue describiendo la extensión de tarea del diseño anterior.
